# Vellum kernel specification

## Adopted v1 delivery clarifications

The user approved these four choices during delivery review. They supersede
conflicting earlier scope/lookup/completion language below, not unrelated safety
contracts. Selection does not establish implementation or proof qualification.

- **F05:** the host establishes logical-source correspondence; the engine issues
  bounded opaque bindings to native document owners. Naming/substrate resolution
  remains external. Binding possession grants no read authority. Preserve native
  incarnation/revision and applicable profile/generation checks, foreign/stale
  refusal and explicit ownership retirement; reopening cannot revive old bindings.
- **F16:** v1 uses immutable catalog correspondence binding only. Distinct atomic
  document/analysis-context activation is explicitly deferred, not implemented by
  relabeling binding. Binding cannot start provider work, change interpretation,
  activate analysis or expand authority; stale correspondence refuses. Startup/
  execution remains host/integration-owned; native validation/result acceptance
  remain engine-owned. Existing required settings/registry operations are retained.
- **C4/F19:** engine dispatch uses a closed sum of original typed native handles.
  Generic-ID lookup, if needed, belongs to bounded stale-safe integration mappings,
  not a new engine-global erased-context registry. Engine owners retain validation,
  authorization, command/result/event correlation, loss/resync/revocation and
  protected retirement. No trial calls across owners; no revival through ID reuse.
- **C5/F18:** a shutdown attempt may return an explicit unresolved report while
  retaining necessary owners/root and the admission fence. This is not complete
  discharge or permission for final release/process exit. Stop, quiescence,
  settlement and retirement remain distinct; reporting grants no discard/retry
  authority. Protected late evidence and cleanup remain available. Final release
  requires actual discharge. Host scheduling/waiting/process exit stays external;
  in-memory retained ownership does not establish crash persistence.

Selected F19 baseline (2026-11-06): source/named-facet/collection establishment and
resynchronization use owner-local bounded original-command records and retained
results, separate current receipt authority, and shared command lifecycle
conventions. One engine/common dispatcher does not imply one global authored-
invocation result owner. Reuse the registry's original intent/retry/busy/result/
retention laws; do not flatten observation establishment into authored publication
outcomes. Each owner must fund its actual command/result records and receipt holds.
Explicit v1 revocation targets one original observation context, independently
authorized and absorbing. It does not revoke sibling grants or prevent separately
authorized new admission. Existing stop-control validation remains independently
required; no permission is synthesized from target possession. This selection
resolves U06 scope and publication-command ownership, not their implementation or
formal-proof completion. The native revocation entry now has an installed
discovery route with separate current metadata-release and native-control checks.
Complete untyped attachment resolution remains open. No old exhaustive executable
profile is widened by this selection.

Native receipt-control completion: `ObservationStopPortV4` adds source,
named-facet and collection receipt targets as exact original command/context
pairs, delegating existing roles to V3. `TrustedObservationRevocationV2` binds
that same target to independently supplied revocation authority. Both direct and
sealed installed typed/dynamic routes retain the closed `read-context/1`
grammar and current native scope checks. Stop/revocation closes only the selected
context; it neither cancels producers nor retires commands, releases retention,
heals faults or closes siblings. Protected direct control does not depend on
ordinary discovery readiness. The earlier executable enums remain unchanged.

The named-facet publisher now owns bounded native establishment/resynchronization
commands using the shared finite lifecycle. An issued command binds its exact
scope, native root and (for resynchronization) stream generation. First execution
retains the actual baseline or native error; retries return only the original
command identity, without another attempt. Interrupted acknowledgment leaves an
unknown/faulted command and preserves actual native effects and retention. Command
records contribute to document pins and shutdown funding until protected cleanup;
retiring an empty command pool refunds its original reservation once. Privileged
host inspection is not F06 disclosure authority. Separately funded named-facet
receipts now retain the exact original baseline/error. Their privileged historical
authorization basis identifies the complete mixed projection, not merely a source
version; current receipt authority is independently required at admission/release.
Stale/foreign bases cannot apply permission loss; attributed current loss closes
that receipt absorbingly. Stopped receipts retain command claims until protected
retirement. Direct and installed typed/dynamic ingress use closed
`named-facet-publication-command/1` and `named-facet-publication-receipt/1` profiles,
with the `named-facet-baseline` retained-outcome facet. Metadata does not grant
execution or disclosure. Broader heterogeneous attachment/control composition
remains implementation work.

Collection establishment/resynchronization now uses the same native lifecycle,
additionally binding one exact original visibility-preparation identity. Admission
validates without consuming; first execution consumes through the actual native
kernel. A known refusal after consumption remains a retained result, not permission
to retry with another packet. Replay neither revalidates a spent packet nor runs
the producer again. Interrupted acknowledgment preserves unknown effects and spent
input. Separate receipts authorize the complete original collection projection,
including its observer-local references. Closed typed/dynamic and installed routes
use `collection-publication-command/1` (2/4/5 fields) and
`collection-publication-receipt/1` (`collection-baseline` facet). Native command and
receipt reservations contribute to shutdown inventory and document pins until
protected retirement. New collection owners/commands/receipts and unexecuted
establishment are fenced at shutdown; existing receipts and settled replay survive.
The same admission boundary now applies to source, named-facet and registry
publication owners, command issuance, new streams and new receipt contexts.
Fresh unbound collection-visibility capture is fenced before allocation/issuance;
original packets remain eligible for existing authorized technical service and
cleanup. Fencing neither refunds owners nor turns retained inventory into drain.

## 1 Exact edit scope and contract status

The operation family is `ApplyExactEdits`: submit explicit replacements against
identified source revisions, validate declared dependencies and current authority,
then publish all required local participants atomically or leave them unchanged.
The name is a specification label, not an assigned stable public command ID.

This slice defines the successful text-changing path, validated unchanged success
under adopted D01 (§6.4), and ordinary prepublication rejection/cancellation
guarantees. D03 replay/status-retention is adopted in §6.5, with concrete refinement open. Line,
anchor, syntax and UI targets must first resolve to the canonical byte contract;
their conversion/profile specifications follow separately; §29.2 selects the
reference logical-line profile.

It does not load documents, save files, rename resources, call providers, perform
semantic discovery or execute sagas. A plan requiring any such effect must use a
separate supported contract; it cannot silently weaken this one's local atomicity.

### 1.1 Engine, integration and frontend ownership

The engine behavior facade exposes semantic editing operations, not every action
an interactive editor can perform. It owns document/annotation state, explicit
logical selection ranges and mapping, history, semantic interpretation, dependency/
authority checks, atomic local publication and structured outcomes. Equivalent
normalized requests use these same contracts regardless of their invocation UI.

Keymaps, chords, interaction modes, focus, gestures, palettes, themes and native
preedit belong to frontends. Shared UI helpers may prevent adapter duplication;
they must depend on the engine facade, not make input policy an engine dependency.
The bounded keymap/chord reference is useful frontend work assigned to the
ratatui example integration, not a reason to add a native engine keymap job.
Both required frontend adapters and thin examples remain in v1 scope.

Only settings that affect an engine-owned interpretation participate in its
semantic configuration and generations. Frontend preference resolution may reuse
pure utilities, but pending chords and compiled bindings are not engine-root
components. No joint atomic engine/UI preference publication is promised. UI
activation may reject or cancel its own stale input; a subsequently dispatched
semantic command still faces current engine validation. A UI-only change must
not consume an engine invocation or advance engine semantic generations.

Logical selections remain validated semantic targets. Native focus and pointer
coordinates are not substitutes for those targets. Optional view/geometry services
may convert accepted layout evidence into source targets; layout, viewport and
rendering policy are not mandatory headless engine state. Source editing must not
wait for repaint or keymap activation. Host/provider ports execute actual OS I/O,
clipboard and native accessibility services; applicable engine effect/evidence
guards do not make the engine their platform implementation.

This ownership rule governs the older combined settings/keymap wording and the
editor-wide facade inventory. The combined fixture is relocated to frontend
reference modules. F16 now names `semantic-settings`, not `settings-keymap`;
§22.3.1.1 supplies the bounded engine-only settings argument product;
§§22.3.1.2–22.3.1.4 supply selected owned resolution, activation and layer lifecycle.
Complete consumers, public products and implementation refinement remain open.
formal/engine-facade.mjs separately projects 71 engine variants from the 87-label
editor inventory. Five clipboard workflow variants use the headless-capable
integration facade: F22 read, both F23 exports and F11 accepted-paste/validated-cut.
Eleven presentation variants remain separate. These three owner classes are
total and disjoint; original editor-wide family indices do not change. Native
gateway refinement remains separate from this reference facade. UI-only F09/
F15/F25 and purpose-specific F26/derived-geometry products need explicit optional
presentation ownership; do not remove logical editing, task cancellation or
host-effect safeguards merely because their callers can be UIs.

Boundary acceptance requires an engine import graph free of frontend keymap
dependencies, rejection of UI-only fields by engine request products, unchanged
engine state for UI-only transitions, and equivalent semantic dispatch through
typed/dynamic facade paths. Existing keymap trace and stale-cutoff evidence is
retained as frontend/reference evidence. formal/engine-ui-boundary.md records
44,544 routing cases per engine/integration projection, 121 UI/native-domain
frames, ten integration-routing frames, eighteen controls and ten
assertion-killed mutations after an unchanged graph baseline. This scoped
reference evidence does not establish all native gateways, registered settings
semantics, platform behavior or independent assurance. No new solver condition
or whole-engine categorical closure is claimed.

### 1.2 Engine and substrate ownership

Requirements §§3.1/3.3 and §5.9 separate observable editing/persistence contracts
from filesystem and provider mechanisms. A document may exist without a file,
directory, native handle or storage connection. An admitted local edit must not
perform hidden resource resolution or storage I/O during validation/publication.
Explicit load/save requests use staged effect paths; no separate editing mode or
network service is implied.

| Engine responsibility | Host or substrate responsibility |
|---|---|
| Own document incarnations, revisions, history and local atomic publication | Open handles and execute byte reads/writes and platform procedures |
| Validate bindings and ownership against accepted resource evidence | Resolve locators and report scoped identity/equivalence/continuity evidence |
| Require lossless fidelity, logical coordinates and explicit serialization profiles | Implement codecs and byte conversion without silently changing the promised fidelity |
| Capture immutable save intent, coordinate engine-mediated writers and adopt eligible baselines | Perform replacement/synchronization and preserve attributes/security under the advertised procedure |
| Validate attributed receipts and expose failure, conflict, unknown and achieved guarantees | Report actual execution, completion, quiescence and acknowledgment evidence |

Resource substrates are independently wired modules implementing engine-owned
resource/effect contracts. The first target is the local filesystem module.
The semantic engine depends on those contracts, not concrete filesystem calls,
native path/SDK/credential or provider connection types. Opaque engine-owned
resource references may retain declared locator evidence without importing a
provider's concrete locator representation. Additional modules,
such as a future S3 provider, need their own declared identity/capability/guarantee
profiles and conformance; no cloud module, filesystem emulation, runtime plugin
loader or arbitrary hot swapping is required in v1. A headless engine may have
no substrate module attached.

Each module declares actual identity/comparison/continuity, read coherence,
write/precondition, acknowledgment/synchronization, failure/unknown and cleanup
semantics. Module availability is not authority; the host explicitly wires and
authorizes access. Incomparable cross-module evidence is not known distinction
or an ordered revision. Replacing a module cannot erase admitted attempts,
retained assets, unknown effects or discharge obligations. Per-destination engine
coordination is not a universal external mutex or cross-module atomic write.
The existing ordinary local-filesystem best-effort baseline remains unchanged.

IF-04 carries typed effects and evidence; IF-10 carries resolver/binding evidence;
IF-13 carries serialization preparation and per-artifact persistence contracts.
Opaque host tokens do not become ordered revisions, paths do not become document
identity or authority, and a native handle grants no semantic mutation bypass.
Encoding failure before dispatch is distinct from an unknown external write.
Cancellation fences eligible future work but does not erase a possible write or
permit an automatic retry. Late evidence retains its original snapshot, binding,
attempt and procedure; only eligible evidence can update the current baseline.

Storage layout, temporary-file naming, sidecar location, platform replacement and
synchronization calls belong to the reference host/provider profile, not the
authoritative content model. Required reference integrations remain in scope.
Their concrete supported procedures and guarantees require conformance evidence;
an interface or mock cannot supply it. Local publication is not filesystem atomicity,
and replacement visibility is not crash durability or isolation from outside writers.

Boundary acceptance distinguishes static packaging from execution. Production
semantic packages must not depend on concrete filesystem/provider implementations;
edge implementations depend on the behavior/effect contracts. Reference catalog
loading, provider bridges and verification tools must be identified as such, not
used to claim that the executable design-reference import graph is host-free.
Selected post-import paths run with filesystem/process calls intercepted in an
isolated verification process; injected hidden I/O must be detected after a coherent
baseline. [Scoped evidence](formal/engine-substrate-boundary.md) covers 59 controls,
source-read activation and save-evidence handling, six interception controls and
three source-save dispatch mutants. Both metadata typed/dynamic routes also run
without intercepted I/O; three metadata hidden-I/O variants across both routes
must record the exact attempted call and produce common faulted/unknown outcomes,
admission fencing and protected retirement. Coherent baselines precede all variants.
This does not establish every path, arbitrary
code isolation, production package separation or actual host truth.

INS-08 observes resolution/binding; INS-07 observes decoding/encoding and artifact
preparation; INS-04 observes dispatch, provider procedure and receipt processing.
Separate engine queue/service time from provider-reported write/synchronization
time and observation delay. No successful local validation or diagnostic event
establishes an external effect. MELT/golden/RED/USE and STRIDE/LINDDUN retain safe,
bounded labels; paths, handles, content and opaque resource tokens are not ordinary
metric labels. Existing invariants and conditional storage/evidence laws retain
their scope; this boundary adds no whole-engine or host-conformance theorem.

## 2 Identity and state domains

| Domain | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| Authority identity | One live local mutation authority; workspace membership or file paths cannot substitute for it |
| Document reference | Authority identity plus document identity/incarnation; disposal and reopen cannot make an old reference valid for a new incarnation |
| Source revision | Non-confusable revision scoped to one document incarnation; comparable only within its declared domain. Equal bytes do not imply equal revisions |
| Publication generation | One fresh coordinator generation per applied local publication; distinct from document, annotation, selection, policy and binding versions |
| Operation identity | One logical invocation shared by its participants, publication and linked history; not a capability, revision, physical effect attempt or diagnostic trace ID |
| Context dependency | Typed domain, identity and expected generation/evidence; a source revision cannot stand in for selection, membership, policy, binding or provider context |

Let `S` denote the engine state. Let `P(S)` be its authoritative publication
projection: managed source roots/revisions, required selection/attachment/history
participants and publication generation. Operation-status records, admission
reservations and optional diagnostics are distinct from `P`.

`P` is a logical coherent state, not a selected storage structure. A read must
observe one supported coherent snapshot/projection; multiple independent reads
are not automatically one transaction or a globally current snapshot.

## 3 Logical request data

The following are required semantic fields, not frozen Rust or wire types.

| Field | Contract |
|---|---|
| Contract version and operation family | Identify the supported declared contract; unknown versions/verbs do not execute |
| Operation identity and authority | Identify this invocation and its one local coordinator; cross-authority plans cannot enter local publication |
| Write participants | Finite explicit document references, exact source revisions and replacement collections; no target may be inferred from current focus |
| Expected target content | Exact starting-snapshot bytes for each replaced range, including the empty string for insertion; no fuzzy match or spelling-based retargeting |
| Read dependencies | Explicit document incarnations/revisions and relevant non-text context used to derive or prepare the operation; may include documents not written |
| Write scope and required guarantees | Explicit bounded permitted footprint and required local atomicity; scope is not a grant and does not authorize annotation authoring or external effects |
| Authority context | Host-established principal/executor/capability context, independently validated against current policy; caller-supplied identity is not trusted by declaration |
| Resource and lifetime profile | Declared bounded input, staging/history/mapping and execution/retention profile; actual capacities and deadlines belong to a later concrete profile |

All write participants are also exact-revision dependencies. Repeated document
entries must resolve to one unambiguous per-document change set before publication;
they cannot create multiple owners or independently committed subtransactions.
Selection-derived requests capture the view/selection generation actually used.
Requests with explicit targets do not acquire accidental focus dependencies.

Supplied semantic/discovery evidence identifies its scope, coverage, provenance
and generations where the requested guarantee needs it. Freshness of returned
objects alone is insufficient to establish absence of newly matching objects.
An external dependency is usable only under a declared validation/isolation
contract sufficient for the requested guarantee. No final-validation callback
may block on uncoordinated external work or invent such a guarantee.

## 4 Canonical replacement semantics

### 4.1 Byte positions and ranges

For starting text `T`, a position is a UTF-8 document-byte boundary in
`0..byte_length(T)`, tied to its document incarnation and source revision. A range
`[lo, hi)` satisfies `0 <= lo <= hi <= byte_length(T)` and both endpoints are
valid UTF-8 boundaries. An insertion has `lo = hi`; the end of the document is a
valid position. Serialized file offsets, BOM bytes, UTF-16 indices, grapheme
indices, screen columns and tokenizer tokens are not these coordinates.

Replacement content must be valid UTF-8. Preserve its exact supplied content:
no normalization, newline rewriting, formatting or grapheme-boundary rounding.
Grapheme navigation is a separate contract. Splitting a UTF-8 scalar is invalid;
splitting a grapheme at a valid scalar boundary is not automatically invalid for
an explicit programmatic edit.

### 4.2 Simultaneous batch application

All ranges and expected bytes refer to the same starting revision, not to the
result of an earlier list entry. Sequential callers must compose their changes
into this representation before submitting them.

For a well-defined per-document collection, order by increasing starting byte
position. Replaced interiors cannot overlap. Adjacent nonempty replacements have
an unambiguous concatenation; coincident insertions or an insertion touching
another edit's endpoint need an explicitly resolved ordering/combined replacement
and are not silently ordered by container iteration. An insertion inside another
replacement conflicts. PA-02 accepts adjacent nonempty replacements; adopted
D02 normalization follows §4.2.1. The original strict-gap
batch model does not cover adjacency; the additional SMT condition does (§27).

For ordered edits `e1..en` with valid nonoverlapping ranges, the candidate text is:

```text
T[0:lo1] ++ insert1 ++ T[hi1:lo2] ++ insert2 ++ ... ++ insertN ++ T[hiN:end]
```

All slices above are from starting `T`; `++` is byte concatenation. The result
must satisfy:

```text
candidate_bytes = starting_bytes + sum(inserted_bytes - replaced_bytes)
```

Expected content must equal each corresponding starting slice. Equality of those
small slices does not waive the exact document revision or read dependencies.
Write-scope and read-only checks cover insertions as well as replaced ranges;
undefined boundary permissions cannot be inferred from successful rendering.

### 4.2.1 Shared ordering normalization

D02 is adopted: shared engine admission accepts an unambiguous unsorted collection
of original-snapshot edit records for one identified document context and
normalizes it once to increasing starting-byte order. All invocation surfaces
share this pipeline; adapters do not implement competing ordering semantics.
Sequential plans still require explicit composition into original-snapshot edits.

Normalization is a permutation of complete records, retaining their individual
boundaries, payloads, expected-content conditions, context/dependencies and
associated semantic metadata. It neither coalesces adjacent replacements nor
silently removes duplicates or identity-looking records. Required validation
must not disappear through normalization or early D01 elision. A compact internal
representation may refine the complete logical record/boundary semantics without
imposing a particular storage or allocation strategy.

Reject unresolved overlap, coincident insertion, insertion inside replacement or
insertion/replacement endpoint ambiguity. Do not use input enumeration, arrival,
priority or correlation labels as an implicit tie breaker. Caller-resolved intent
must lower to an explicitly unambiguous supported request, not an undocumented
ordering mode. This selects no public tie-encoding or correlation schema.

The normalized result is idempotent and independent of permutation of the same
complete unambiguous input records. Equal resulting bytes alone do not establish
semantic equivalence: merging adjacent edits can change whether a shared-boundary
attachment survives. Retain mapping, conditional inverse and metadata meaning.
Actual classifiers/profiles, owned metadata and implementation refinement remain
D04/D13/D19/D33/D45; formal/batch-normalization.md gives the exact argument,
finite reference checks, local SMT conditions and coalescing counterexample.

Bound input validation, copying/sorting, comparison and retained metadata under
§17; exhaustion follows declared refusal/bounded deferral before publication,
not partial application or a fabricated canonical result. Normalization is
private preparation, not authority or freshness evidence. The coordinator still
revalidates current dependencies/rights and all required participants at the
atomic boundary; one successful per-document normalization cannot publish while
another required participant fails. No numeric budget or sorting algorithm is
selected by this semantic contract.

### 4.2.2 Normalization and owned compound admission

Bind §4.2.1 normalization to owned invocation admission before immutable intent
comparison/capture and before source-dependent view preparation. Resolve repeated
source entries with the same exact document incarnation to one participant in
first-occurrence order. Their source and engine annotation-set expectations must
agree; conflicting headers refuse rather than choosing one. Concatenate complete
records without elision, then sort that participant's edit sequence under its
identified original-coordinate context. Duplicate records are not silently
deduplicated; overlapping replacements or unresolved insertion ties still refuse.
Do not reorder authored
annotation operations, merge adjacent edits, discard empty records or replace
per-document contexts with a global position ordering. Reject malformed ranges
and unresolved overlap/insertion ambiguity before accepting an executable intent.

Matching permutations of the same complete unambiguous source records normalize
to the same retained intent. This applies before service and to retries after
publication: normalization must not reacquire current source, refresh expected
revisions, update dependency expectations or reclassify the old result. Changed
payloads, expected bytes, contexts, participant intent or descriptor remain a
different request. Unknown contract versions do not inherit this vocabulary.
Current authority, source bytes/revisions, read dependencies, scopes, companions
and capacities remain native final-validation obligations, not consequences of
sorting. A malformed expected-byte condition on an empty edit cannot disappear
through elision or no-op classification.

F10 advice uses the same normalization before its pure candidate/view decision;
its observation basis still binds the original complete request, current root
and recipient context. Malformed/ambiguous normalization yields no verdict, not
a reusable prepared command. Structurally accepted proposals still return the
existing current-check advice, which reserves no future validity or execution.

The normalized compound evaluator remains an ordered-input private port. The
shared owner supplies that precondition rather than teaching each evaluator or
frontend a competing sorting rule. Existing invocation byte ceilings bound the
captured product; finite copy/sort/scan work has no extension callback or provider
I/O. Each grouped participant owns a separate edit array: appending repeated input
must not extend an array being traversed, even when normalized native inputs share
record or array references. The grouping traversal therefore consumes only the
finite original entries/records. Temporary physical allocation, actual synchronization and host service remain
implementation/refinement obligations. No additional persistent canonical buffer
or numerical production default is selected.

[Invocation composition evidence](formal/invocation-publication.md) now includes
60 permutation/profile/route cases and ten repeated-participant/profile/route
cases through the actual reference owner, including
F10 advice, multi-document source/annotation/current-view publication and linked
history. Controls check replay, ambiguity, complete record boundaries,
empty expected-content obligations, repeated-header conflict, shared native aliases
and later stale-source refusal. The current existing owner
check has 27 controls and 37 assertion-detected mutations; its original gate and
finite trace populations remain unchanged. This closes that reference admission
bridge, not complete public envelopes, every operation family, production
normalizer refinement, concurrency/crash safety or independent certification.
Frozen qualification and matching endpoint adoption remain required.

INS-01 distinguishes bounded normalization, refusal and immutable replay;
INS-02 records final validation and publication rather than candidate sorting;
INS-03 gates advice/outcome release; INS-06 retains actual linked history
participants. Existing MELT/golden/RED/USE populations and STRIDE/LINDDUN/hazard
cases cover ordering substitution, partial publication, erased conditions,
retargeted replay and resource exhaustion. Use bounded stage/disposition codes,
not source bytes, object identities, offsets or payload-derived metric labels.

### 4.3 Shared transformation meaning

For a supported unambiguous change set, resulting source is independent of
storage chunking and invocation surface. Publication, selection/attachment mapping,
conditional history inverses and derived invalidation refine the same source-change
meaning, rather than implementing incompatible edits at each adapter. Their typed
representations may differ. Mapping and inverse laws apply only over their declared
domains/affinities: deleted targets or lost context can require detachment or
unavailable evidence rather than a fabricated total inverse. Required authored
companions still stage and publish coherently under sections 5–6. This selects no
universal struct, storage backend or arbitrary callback extension mechanism.

### 4.3.1 Purpose-specific attachment mapping

D04 is adopted: use one source-change algebra with a small closed set of typed,
purpose-specific mapping profiles, not a universal survival rule or callbacks
inside publication. Positional profiles may collapse a deleted caret/navigation
position to a declared surviving boundary; valid geometry proves neither content
identity nor continuing applicability. Exact caret/selection interaction defaults
remain D45, and each supported replacement/deletion profile must declare its
boundary disposition rather than infer one from presentation.

Content-sensitive targets retain location separately from applicability evidence.
A partially edited nonempty target may remain mapped but is affected/stale, not
thereby semantically validated. Complete deletion or replacement of the original
target content, including coverage by several adjacent edits, detaches it without
deleting its authored annotation body/version. Equal inserted bytes do not alone
establish target identity. Genuine semantic identity still follows §6.4's complete
classification; an empty insertion alone cannot manufacture affected evidence.
No fuzzy quote match, restored bytes or source undo automatically reattaches a
detached target or overwrites a later explicit attachment choice.

The default nonempty content-range profile excludes pure insertions exactly at
its outer boundaries: the start follows insertion at the start, and the end stays
before insertion at the end. This does not exclude interior insertion from its
location span or certify unchanged applicability. A collapsed range is a point
with one explicit affinity, not two opposed endpoint affinities that may invert
or silently widen it. Shared nonempty-range policy does not impose a UI selection
model, primary-selection rule or implicit point-affinity default.

Exact-revision proposals remain bound to their captured revision, dependencies
and authority. A mapped location can support preview or creation of a new proposal;
it cannot refresh expected revisions or authorize executing stale work. Missing
mapping history/context produces explicit unavailable/detached evidence under the
declared profile, not guessed coordinates or permission. Document-wide targets
retain their document identity contract rather than invent a source-byte range.
Explicit reattachment uses current identity/version/source evidence and rights.

All required mappings/evidence stage and publish coherently with the source under
§§5–6, preserving separate authored body state and current release gates. Bound
mapping traversal, retained evidence and attachment fan-out under §17; unavailable
required mapping cannot be replaced by partial success or diagnostic output.
Observe mapped/affected/detached/unavailable dispositions and cost without body,
quote, private target or identity-valued metric labels. Exact point-context loss,
replacement-boundary maps, schemas, native geometry and actual retained-history/
coordinator refinements remain explicit work, not inferred from the reference.
See formal/mapping-profiles.md for conditional laws, finite checks and limits.

## 5 Preparation and final validation

Preparation may use immutable snapshots and stage work outside serialized
publication. It must acquire source/context under the applicable read authority,
validate supported request shape and bounds, construct exact candidates, and
stage every required selection/attachment/history participant. Authored annotation
bodies are preserved by a source edit; attachment mappings are separate derived
participants with explicit profile/deletion dispositions.

The final publication predicate requires all of the following in one serialized
validation/publication boundary:

1. The authority and all participant incarnations remain valid and local.
2. Every write/read revision exactly matches the request and every relevant
   context dependency satisfies its declared current-validation contract. A
   changed source revision rejects this invocation; the engine cannot refresh
   expected revisions internally and call it the same exact-revision request.
   This slice supplies no automatic rebase or fuzzy mapping.
3. Current authority, read-only rules and declared write scopes allow the entire
   proposed operation; advisory discovery/enablement is not permission.
4. Expected bytes, candidate source and required mappings/history correspond to
   the same validated starting state under their declared profiles.
5. Required capabilities, guarantees, bounds and staging/completion reservations
   are satisfied; no required participant is omitted or silently downgraded.
6. No accepted cancellation/deadline has stopped the execution before publication.

There is no intervening mutation between this predicate and publication. A
stale candidate is rejected or its private staging rebuilt and validated within
the unchanged request preconditions; changed expected source revisions require
a fresh proposal. A prior validation never authorizes a later publication.
Arbitrary provider, extension,
formatter, subscriber or exporter callbacks do not execute in this boundary.

An unrelated publication need not invalidate an otherwise current request merely
because the global generation changed. Its effects must nevertheless be carried
forward: do not publish a stale whole-coordinator copy that restores unrelated
documents, policies or views from the preparation snapshot.

### 5.1 Native compound advisory validation

F10's `advisory-validation` has the private `proposal-validation/1` request with
exact contract, operation and plan fields. The selected
`native-compound-current-checks/1` profile accepts the exact owned compound `/1`
or explicit-read `/2` product, plus §5.2's explicitly scoped `/3` product.
Other native job families, external effect plans and
semantic-provider assertions require their own supported validation profiles; an
unsupported product gives no verdict, not an invented generic validator.

Both native routes resolve through the existing F10 catalog entry to the query
facet of the actual local owner. Validate the actual domain/context and native
health, current read/scope/continuity, complete proposal readability and permission
to observe the whole predicate, including private capacity/companion influences.
All named query facts are strict true and bound to the exact request, actual
current root identity and complete caller context by the trusted host basis.
Different copies, stale roots, mismatched proposals or contexts do not satisfy
that basis. Host truth and complete visibility of every influencing predicate
remain supplier obligations, not facts inferred from possession of a proposal.

Evaluate the same source/annotation/read-dependency, mapping, history and attached
view candidate rules used by command publication, under existing finite input,
root, result and companion bounds. Separate pure candidate/view decisions from
source-journal preparation, commitment and carry. Candidate histories and versions
are private computed values: they do not enter the current root or allocate live
history/version identities. The query issues no invocation, starts no task,
reserves no command capacity, installs no root/result, mints no committed source
receipt and dispatches no provider I/O. Query temporary derived work remains
bounded; no physical-allocation or timing noninterference guarantee is inferred.

The copied reply is exactly status `advice`, this profile, and Boolean
`checksSatisfied`. True means only the selected current candidate checks passed;
false means they did not. It does not classify a future command's terminal outcome.
Both changed and unchanged candidates can satisfy the predicate. Unsupported,
unreadable, unobservable, malformed outer products, insufficient query capacity or
unexpected private evaluation failure return unavailable without a Boolean verdict.
An unexpected private evaluation failure fences the native owner under its existing
supervision contract without changing authored state or reclassifying admitted
tickets. It must not be laundered into a proven invalid proposal.
The scoped reply adds no raw cause, object identity, future version or grant token.

Advice is not retained execution status, a reservation, a reusable admission
certificate or permission. A plan's proposed invocation label is descriptive here;
actual command submission still binds an issued native invocation. Any later
command independently rechecks identity, current authority/dependencies,
companions, reservations, cancellation, final capacity and publication/outcome
installation. Equal or unchanged advice does not bypass these obligations.
Unrelated intervening publication alone need not invalidate a precise proposal.

[Scoped evidence](formal/proposal-validation.md) covers the actual query/router,
shared decisions, nonpublication frames and negative mutations. Public encoding,
all-family validation, rich private explanations, provider/schema truth, complete
allocation/accounting, production concurrency/crash and independent assurance
remain gates. No F10-wide or engine-wide categorical completeness is claimed.

### 5.2 Exact bounded source operation scopes

Requirements §5.1's operation scope is a caller restriction, not a grant, new
document, translated coordinate system or separate mutation owner. The private
`owned-annotation-plan/3` retains `/2`'s explicit read conjunction and adds mandatory
`scopes`; `/1` and `/2` keep their exact previous products. Both native command
routes and §5.1 advisory validation use the same scope predicate.

Each source participant has exactly one scope with the exact document identity/
incarnation, expected source revision, profile `bounded-source-scope/1`, and two
independent finite sets. `replacementRanges` contains nonempty half-open `[lo,hi)`
original-source byte intervals. `insertionSites` contains inclusive `[first,last]`
intervals of permitted pure-insertion positions. Scope endpoints must be valid
source scalar boundaries; actual edits still require all ordinary UTF-8 boundary,
expected-byte and batch rules. An insertion interval cannot license a byte-interior
edit. Its singleton form permits one site, including the gap in an empty source.
No endpoint permission is inferred from replacement containment or a default
affinity. This distinguishes write containment from attachment mapping affinity.

For a nonempty replacement/deletion, every removed original-source cell must be
covered by the replacement-range union. Touching ranges may jointly cover an edit;
separated ranges must not be replaced by their convex hull. Replacement text is
within that replacement operation; it does not additionally require a separate
pure-insertion-site permission. A zero-width edit, including an identity-looking
record, requires its explicit insertion-site permission. An empty edit list is
the empty conjunction, not an out-of-scope edit that may be silently discarded.

Admission checks closed finite products, rejects duplicate document scopes and
overlapping range/site records, and canonicalizes scope/set order only. Do not
merge records, rewrite authored edits, swap reversed endpoints, clamp extents or
invent a missing scope. Final validation requires exact current source identity/
revision and captured source-participant correspondence, complete scope coverage
and finite aggregate scope/range/site/identifier limits. Missing, unused, stale,
foreign, disposed, reincarnated, malformed or exceeded scopes refuse the entire
candidate before changes or no-op classification. A profile with no source
participants uses an explicit empty scope list without unused new scope facts.

Every edit remains in original document coordinates. An earlier edit must not
shift or widen permission for a later record. Validate all participants before
publishing one root; a violating record does not leave allowed peers published.
The constraint does not mutate read-only dependencies or add history participants.
Current read/write authority, read-only policy and required annotation/view/history
companions remain independently mandatory. Source containment grants no annotation
authoring, persistence/export or external resource authority, and does not change
the meaning of an ordinary whole-document save. Exact revision is this profile's
baseline; mapped scopes require another explicit supported contract.
The forward invocation's constraint is not standing document policy or a future
undo/redo grant. Other job families retain their own current scope/authority and
frontier contracts; this product does not silently add scoped reversal support.

For one exact snapshot, scalar cells and insertion gaps form a finite typed
permission universe. Its powerset has empty/full bounds and intersection/union;
caller constraints cannot amplify independent current policy. This is not a
single lattice across arbitrary document revisions/authorities or an engine-wide
categorical completeness claim. A representation/metadata cap can prevent a join
from fitting: refuse or obtain a new supported bounded profile, never widen.

[Scoped evidence](formal/source-scopes.md) combines actual native command/query
composition, independent cell/gap oracles, negative mutations and ten conditional
solver cases. Current baseline totals are 52 conditions in that manifest and
262 across fourteen manifests. Host policy truth, mapped profiles, public wire,
complete other dependency domains, physical/global/concurrent/crash refinement
and independent assurance remain gates; no whole operation family or D-row closes.

## 6 Atomic publication and outcomes

### 6.1 Applied publication

For a validated text-changing request, publication is one local state transition.
It installs the exact candidate sources and all required authoritative companion
participants, one shared operation identity and one fresh publication generation.
Each text-changing document receives one new monotonically advancing source
revision. Source revisions do not change for selection-only updates; equal content
reached later through undo does not restore an old revision identity.

Unlisted participants are unchanged relative to immediately before publication,
except explicitly required mappings/invalidation governed by their own contracts.
Those required changes cannot be hidden from participant validation or observation
policy. Publication stages linked history sufficient for the declared reversal
contract; this does not choose undo grouping or prove arbitrary inverse mappings.

Internal commit evidence identifies the operation, generation and affected
documents' before/after revisions. It is not persistence evidence. Recipient
release may project or withhold private participant details under current policy.
No visible observer or host effect receives a committed change before publication.

### 6.2 Unchanged rejection and stopping

Ordinary malformed/unsupported, stale/conflicting, denied or capacity rejection
before publication preserves `P(S_after) = P(S_before)` for that decision step.
The comparison is with immediately preceding state, not the old preparation
snapshot: rejecting one operation must not undo somebody else's publication.
Discarding private staging and releasing safe local reservations is permitted.

Accepted cancellation or deadline before publication similarly stops without
publication. If publication wins the race, a later cancellation cannot turn it
into an unchanged rejection or undo it. Cancelling caller observation is not
proof the operation was stopped; authoritative status remains the source of truth.

### 6.3 Outcome dimensions and fault containment

| Outcome category | Guaranteed meaning |
|---|---|
| Applied | Local publication happened; identify its internal evidence and release only the recipient-authorized projection. No claim of file persistence |
| Validated unchanged success | Required checks passed and the declared semantic effect is identity; no edit publication generation, source revision or undo entry. Bounded invocation status is separate |
| Rejected | No publication by this invocation; structured safe disposition, not raw protected content or host errors |
| Stopped before publication | Accepted cancellation/deadline prevented this invocation's publication; not a rollback or general effect-quiescence claim |
| Internal fault | Stop affected execution and isolate uncertain owner integrity. Do not label uncertain publication as a known unchanged rejection or blindly restart |

These are admissible semantic outcomes, not the final public result enum.
No-op semantics are adopted in §6.4 and bounded replay semantics in §6.5;
layered outcome/explanation policy is adopted in §23.1.1. Concrete result fields,
replay representation/retention, per-operation reason precedence and unavailable
shapes remain D03/D05/D09/D12/D33 refinements. Correctly rejecting
untrusted input is not an internal fault. Notification/telemetry failure after a
known publication cannot change Applied into Rejected. If process/owner failure
destroys trustworthy status, report the observation/integrity limit rather than
inventing either successful publication or rollback.

### 6.4 Validated unchanged success

D01 is adopted: after normal required identity/incarnation, exact revision,
dependency/context, current authority, scope/read-only, capability and bounds
validation, return unchanged success if the operation has no declared semantic
effect. Classify at the serialized final decision boundary against its current
state, not merely an old preparation snapshot. Accepted cancellation/deadline
before that decision still stops the operation; identity is not a bypass.

The comparison includes required source, selection, attachment, annotation and
explicit history-intent effects under their declared profiles. Equal source bytes
alone do not establish identity. Exclude automatic publication/revision/history
bookkeeping from deciding identity, otherwise generated bookkeeping makes the
definition circular. Explicit external-effect intent cannot be dropped through
text equality, and invocation observation is not an edit publication.

A genuine no-op preserves the current authored/publication projection, edit
generation, source revisions and undo entries, including unrelated intervening
commits. Bounded invocation-status records and optional authorized observations
may record the disposition separately under §6.5's adopted D03 contract;
this does not introduce durable receipts, exactly-once effects or indefinite
status availability. Later diagnostic/notification failure cannot relabel a known
unchanged success as validation rejection, just as it cannot undo Applied.

Each supported operation/profile needs a bounded, sound and complete identity
predicate and the required exact comparison or by-construction evidence. Do not compare whole
workspaces or solve arbitrary program equivalence. Exhausted comparison/staging
resources follow the declared refusal/bounded-deferral contract, not an assumed
identity or fabricated change. Validated identity cannot be relabeled Applied
merely to generate a commit. Actual fields, mappings, grouping and semantic
participant completeness remain D04/D13/D19/D33/D45 refinement work.

PS-NO imports finite splice/map operators for representative identity and
equal-text companion cases. Its 43 bounded configurations and eight local SMT
conditions are scoped evidence; see formal/noop-publication.md for the general
frame argument, mutation sensitivity and remaining implementation obligations.

### 6.4.1 Equal-byte annotation and selection companion classification

The normalized source/annotation publisher maps current placements through exact
original-snapshot edits even when emitted bytes equal the original. Equal inserted
values do not restore original-byte identity for content-sensitive targets; positional
points retain explicit affinity/collapse rules. Detached evidence stays detached
without justified reattachment. Validate private annotation-set and every required
current view dependency, current rights/stop/compatibility/resources before deciding.

If source bytes are equal, preserve source revision. If automatic placements change,
advance the changed annotation-set generation and one local publication, not authored
body/target versions or source/annotation undo entries. Automatic mapping alone leaves
existing authored undo/redo frontiers intact. Selection effects advance only changed
selection generations in that same publication. Authored body/target or real text
changes in other compound participants retain their actual history scopes; do not
invent a source participant for an equal-byte mapping-only document. Pure identity
preserves every semantic/edit generation/history field after normal validation.

The actual ordinary-selection and owned search publishers preserve an already-applied
mapping candidate rather than dropping it when source/view comparisons are equal.
Clipboard paste composes the same path. Exhausted required publication/annotation/
selection counters refuse without wrap; unchanged success needs no unused counter.
Native F14 reverses actual authored participants, preserving conservative current
placements rather than reattaching from equal text. No new parser source-transform
receipt follows from unchanged source bytes/revision; derived contexts retain their
own annotation/view dependencies. No new history policy or mutation path is added.

[Equal-byte companion evidence](formal/equal-byte-companions.md) includes 8,060
independent single/paired-edit oracle cases, 256 compound/selection gate decisions,
thirteen controls/eleven mutants and conditional arguments through actual compound,
selection/search/native F14/parser references. These close the earlier normalized
mapping-classification refusal, not all profiles or general target restoration.
Source/version/history/view equality in paired hidden worlds does not prove public
outcome/status/event/timing/cache noninterference: internal Applied/Unchanged and raw
publication/annotation counters can differ and require protected recipient projection.
Full replay/events, native/concurrent/physical/production refinement and independent
assurance remain gates. INS-01/02/06/03/05/10/13 retain admission/publication/history,
private dependencies, derived invalidation and bounded capacity observations.

### 6.5 Bounded invocation replay and retirement

D03 is adopted: one incarnation-scoped invocation identity denotes one immutable
semantic intent. Admit it for execution at most once under the declared bounded
admission lifetime. Matching retries through any invocation surface observe the
same pending execution or retained terminal facts; they do not prepare another
edit, reclassify an old no-op, republish, regroup history or restart stopped work.
Reuse with different semantic parameters rejects. Intent comparison includes
targets, exact preconditions, effects and semantic metadata under the supported
profile; matching source bytes or a diagnostic trace ID is insufficient.
Admission and consumption of first-execution eligibility must be serialized with
duplicate detection. A hash alone requires a justified equality/collision contract.

Keep execution eligibility, retained status and outstanding obligations distinct.
Status eviction or expiry never restores execution eligibility, implies known
nonapplication or releases an unresolved provider/worker/resource obligation.
Retirement invalidates an old identity without making it fresh after its detailed
result is forgotten. Late requests/completions cannot match a reused slot, new
incarnation or different invocation. No counter/generation wrap or namespace reuse
may silently alias obsolete work; exhaustion must refuse or establish a justified
new non-confusable admission domain. A cache miss alone cannot admit a request.

An actual bounded admission/fencing mechanism must distinguish a valid first
submission from retired or unissued identities without an unbounded tombstone
set. A bounded session/sequence/generation construction is possible precedent,
not a selected public representation, mandatory network service or additional
round trip. Concrete schemas, comparison/work/status budgets, supported retention
and clock/epoch profiles remain technical refinements. Reserve required bookkeeping
before accepting its obligation; pressure cannot silently weaken promised replay
protection. An active request needs its safety-critical execution/obligation state
even if caller observation ends. Retirement does not itself cancel running work.

Historical execution facts and current release authorization are separate. A
retained Applied result remains Applied after revision or rights change, but its
delivery is reauthorized and projected under current recipient policy. Denial or
unavailable status cannot fabricate rejection/nonapplication. D05/D09/D12 still
govern public reason/token/disclosure shapes; request identity is not a capability.
New intent uses a new invocation and ordinary current validation, not a retry that
silently refreshes preconditions. Unknown outcomes require reconciliation or an
independently demonstrated safe-retry basis before a new potentially duplicating
mutation. D01/D02 semantics remain unchanged for the one eligible execution.

The v1 baseline is not crash-durable deduplication or exactly-once external
effects. Losing the trusted owner/admission domain invalidates old eligibility;
it does not establish whether a prior effect occurred. Effect dispatch, safe
disposition and retry ownership retain §16–17's separate provider contracts.
Observe attempts, first admissions, duplicate observations, mismatch/retirement,
retained-status occupancy and unresolved obligations separately from commits.
Use INS-01/02 for authoritative decisions and INS-03 for current release; no raw
intent, invocation-valued metric labels or telemetry-based deduplication.

formal/replay-reference.md records the conditional induction, finite shared-state
reference and local SMT conditions. They do not prove an actual ticket encoding,
clock, intent validator, provider, multi-document coordinator or crash recovery.

### 6.5.1 Owned invocation and actual publication composition

The local normalized composition in formal/invocation-publication.md connects
§6.5 to actual owned source/body/target compounds, all current supported positional
source-view companions, prepared native F14 reversal and §23's outcome projector.
Its private ticket objects/reference spelling are reference machinery, not a new
public token format, mandatory network round trip or operation family. One trusted
engine/root domain spans its documents and recipients. Each invocation binds its
own recipient/purpose/destination/profile/continuity and rechecks that complete scope
at submit, execution and observation. Actual unique ownership and host policy/
reservation truth remain premises, not consequences of checking a supplied flag.

Bind one complete immutable normalized prepared intent to an issued owned identity.
Typed and dynamic routes share the same relation. Mismatched intent refuses; a
matching pending or terminal retry observes existing work and never prepares again.
Copy ordinary plans; retain actual immutable native reversal ownership and recheck
its original dependencies at execution. Do not refresh a stale plan behind a retry.
Complete upstream canonicalization and other families' extra semantics remain their
own contracts; equal output bytes are not complete intent equivalence.

Bound active slots, lifetime issuance, intent/root/result bytes and declared held
capacity. Before accepting the execution obligation, reserve supported terminal
fact shapes and all minimal-policy combinations, independent of the eventual result.
Owned tokens cannot be cloned into authority; retirement removes eligibility without
resetting issuance or making a cache miss fresh. Exhaustion refuses; automatic
admission-domain renewal, clock-based expiry and crash durability are not supplied.

Only pending→running starts a job. Stage actual source/annotation/history/current-view
candidates and aggregate view work before installing the complete root together with
terminal facts/done phase. Preserve committed parser-journal references when carrying
the root. Validated Unchanged records the spent invocation without an authored
publication; later source changes cannot reclassify it. Unexpected internal protocol
fault leaves the previous installed root, records conservative Unknown/faulted facts
and fences new mutation admission/execution rather than inventing confirmed rejection
or silently restarting. No arbitrary callback, telemetry or I/O is inside this decision.

Use current scoped release and the captured minimal outcome ceiling. Fact eviction
means unavailable, not NotApplied or new eligibility. Stop intent does not discharge
pending work; explicit drained retirement follows actual local terminal disposition.
Post-publication observer/transfer failure cannot erase the installed root/fact or
enable another execution. These closed synchronous local jobs do not establish
provider-effect retirement, exactly-once external effects or crash recovery.

256 publication/128 release/1,024 policy/64 paired cases, 720 action permutations/
4,320 edges, seventeen controls/25 mutants and conditional induction/composition
arguments. Other operation/gateway/wait/event products, actual host uniqueness/
policy/retention, hostile decoding/canonicalization, concurrent/physical/timing/
resource/production and independent refinement remain. Existing INS-01/02/03/06/13
separate first admission/retry, actual local disposition, current release, history

Extend §6.5.1's normalized shared-root reference with four closed private producer

remain open. A retry must resolve its existing invocation, not
silently prepare again from newer carets, query matches or settings.

Producer handles can have equal visible fields but different private meaning.
For these jobs bind the original producer-owned candidate identity together with
its bounded complete semantic descriptor. Unknown, copied or foreign-kind handles
refuse; rebuilding a new equal-looking preparation is not the same retained candidate.
Capture request, actual dependencies, settings/query/profile context, derived work
and post-selection meaning, including unused literal replacement on zero matches.
Keep opaque occurrence/boundary bindings attached to their actual producer rather
than serializing lookalikes. The descriptor is private engine data, not a read grant.

Bound producer data and the full normalized descriptor envelope before first
execution eligibility is consumed. Recheck the retained semantic snapshot at the
one eligible run. Unexpected disappearance/drift is a fenced Unknown/faulted
integrity failure, not replacement intent or fabricated confirmed rejection.
Normal current permission, selection, settings, query/evidence/profile validation
uses the actual producer and may refuse known nonpublication. Preserve ordinary
caret-after/mapped meaning, all supported current companions, view-only permission/
history frames, original query generation and already-acquired Unicode evidence.
Do not run a search or native boundary tool inside publication to repair old context.

Install the actual producer candidate and reserved terminal facts through the
existing root decision. No-op eligibility stays spent after later source/caret work;
status eviction, observer failure or protected stop cannot make it fresh. Producer
retention/reservations remain separately accounted; logical byte checks do not
prove physical peaks. Clipboard task disposition is outside these pure adapters;

with the provider.
