eight omissions, 36 argument boundaries, twelve argument mutants, three native
frame-oracle cases/three mutants, 25 gateway controls, 108 permission cases, 24
capture/parent boundaries, twelve gateway mutants, six faults and six hidden-I/O
cases. F18/context/observer coverage has 38 forms/twelve kinds, 9,842 traces/27,588
edges with all prior mutation identities retained. Existing INS-01/02/05/06/07/10/13
cover admission/publication, query evidence, history/mapping/views and separate
charges/discharge; native input and external-effect boundaries remain at adapters.
F05 context issuance/async lifetime, actual host/policy/reservations, complete
public/result/event/wire/multidocument products, hostile reflection, physical/
global/concurrent/crash and independent gates remain. Full frozen verification
is required; no whole family or decision row closes.

### 6.5.2.4 Explicit source batch native facade binding

Bind existing F11 exact-batch through exact-source-batch/1 and
bounded-explicit-source-batch/1. Its exact request has contract, operation,
invocation, profile, sources, reads and scopes. Source entries have document,
expectedSource and edits; edits have complete lo/hi/expected/ins records. Use
original-source UTF-8 byte coordinates and existing closed /5 read/scope contracts.
There is no public annotation-set stamp, authored annotation field, implicit
focus/selection dependency or public execute-anything compound constructor.

Normalize complete public intent through shared grouping/order/read/scope rules
before capture/comparison. Reserve canonical capture against actual owner headroom;
only then validate actual live source and capture engine-owned annotation-set
dependencies once. Matching retries reuse that plan, even if private annotations
have changed; they cannot refresh dependency evidence. Preparation remains private.
Current service authority and source/read/scope/private-companion guards precede
one common publication, including bounded all-current-view mapping and history.
Protected retirement discharges pure plan/capture once without issuance refund.

The [binding and conditional argument](formal/exact-batch-binding.md) retain exact
typed/dynamic identity, limits, existing terminal/outcome/discovery and instrumentation
contracts. This source-only binding does not satisfy the separately required atomic
F11/F13 authoring composition under §13.9; sequential calls are not its substitute.
No new operation variant, provider effect, network path or Rust/wire layout is chosen.
Full qualification/installation and physical/native/independent gates remain.

### 6.5.2.5 Explicit atomic source and annotation authoring binding

F11/exact-batch may use the distinct atomic-source-annotation/1 contract and
bounded-atomic-authoring/1 profile. Its exact fields are contract, operation,
invocation, profile, sources, annotations, reads and scopes; operation is
exact-batch. Source/read/scope fields retain §6.5.2.4's explicit records and closed
native `/5` vocabulary. annotations is a nonempty ordered vector of components,
not a script or arbitrary command list. The older source-only contract refuses
annotation fields; this profile does not silently change its meaning.

Each component has operation, document and dependencies, plus the existing F13
variant fields: create has body/target; update-body has annotation/expectedContent/
body; reattach has annotation/expectedTarget/target; delete has annotation/
expectedContent/expectedTarget. The outer invocation and execution context supply
the native invocation/profile; callers cannot supply provider grants, private
annotation-set stamps or fresh create identities. Exact scalar, identity, version,
dependency, UTF-8 boundary and both point-profile rules remain mandatory.

A before target has exactly basis, sourceRevision and target and is validated
against the explicit starting source. A candidate target has exactly basis and
target; its owner is the component document and its candidate is this same
proposal's staged source. Do not accept a descriptor string, guessed future live
revision, foreign proposal, fuzzy repair or current-focus lookup. Capture the
actual source meaning at first preparation even when no source component writes
that document; a later source change cannot reinterpret an admitted target.

Normalize repeated source records/read conjunctions under existing rules and retain
the complete canonical public intent. Capture private source companion stamps
once. Annotation order remains original; body and target fields may combine under
independent versions, but duplicate same-field or create/delete identity conflicts
refuse rather than acquire sequential/last-wins meaning. Ordinary body authoring
does not gain an unnecessary source-revision dependency: compatible current
source/target mapping remains eligible unless an explicit dependency forbids it.

For every component, use the existing native F13 preparation/currentness checks,
retaining its actual owner, recipient/profile, limits, required dependencies and
original create allocation. A current host binding names the original component
index, invocation, document and operation; it is separate from caller data.
Source read/write/scope grants never replace annotationWritable or membership/
target/allocation checks. Source participation additionally needs current F11
read/write/all-target scope. An annotation-only proposal needs no source-write
grant merely because its outer family is F11. Supplier/policy truth remains a
premise, not something established by a caller's matching string or Boolean.

Before native staging, debit 3C + 2M + 2R logical bytes against actual invocation
headroom, where C is the canonical public capture size, M=maxIntentBytes and
R=maxRootBytes. Bound the complete source-plan/component/native-value/final-plan
metadata by M. Then fund §13.9.6's complete component receipt hold from remaining
headroom before accepting execution. Checked arithmetic and full capacity checks
must refuse without spending the ticket or retaining provisional charges. No
physical allocation/copy-peak claim or independent extra pool follows.

At service, recheck actual F11 grants, all original native component bindings and
their current owners/versions/dependencies/allocations against the actual before
root or same-proposal source candidate. Final compound validation composes every
source, read, annotation, current view, history and resource limit. The complete
final candidate must also fit every captured annotation component's root/document/
record limits. Publish once with the retained coarse facts and receipt vector, or
leave the whole current root unchanged. Known refusal and unexpected Unknown/
faulted protocol failure retain their distinct §6.5.1/13.9.6 meanings.

Matching typed/dynamic retries reuse the original capture, private dependencies,
native handles, allocations and receipt ceilings. Changed caller intent cannot
replace a prepared claim. Retention/drain forgetting and owner-controlled drained
retirement preserve spent issuance; only provisional refusal or actual protected
retirement refunds the corresponding logical charge. The public submit response
does not disclose the private plan, captured companion stamps or create allocation.

[Binding evidence](formal/atomic-authoring.md) covers the actual shared coordinator,
cross-document source/declared reads, both target bases, separate current rights,
original allocation, stale private dependencies, independent body/target behavior,
strict input capture, complete candidate limits, capacity, replay, stop and fault.
Current discovery/enablement, cross-family result/event assembly, U01 retrieval,
actual identity/policy/host truth, hostile native-code containment, physical/
concurrent/crash refinement and independent assurance remain separate gates.

### 6.5.3 Acknowledged clipboard continuation and joint local disposition

This section is an integration composition contract, not a clipboard-specific
kernel command or mandatory kernel task registry. The combined executable
reference co-locates integration and engine logic; it does not prove production
package separation. Integration retains workflow/task/receipt state, while engine
capture, exact validation, atomic source/annotation/view/history publication and
generic effect/evidence authority remain engine contracts. The joint observable
decision below is still required; moving ownership cannot permit a partial
task/root/outcome report, direct integration mutation or fabricated acknowledgment.

Join an already accepted uncontested cut/paste task to the existing invocation
issued for its original request. Preserve that task, original request/registration/
target/payload/receipt and complete bounded semantic descriptor in one owned capsule.
Copy has no source-edit continuation. Preparation before acknowledgment refuses;
quiescence is not acknowledgment. Claim the capsule for one owned ledger ticket
only after scope, intent/envelope and terminal-capacity validation. Matching retries
require original capsule identity and value. Pin the task and exclude standalone
publication while the continuation owns it. These are private normalized composition
facets, not a completed public clipboard admission/dispatch retry protocol.

Stage actual current ordinary-edit source/annotation/view/history publication without
changing task disposition. Bound one stage per task and its held capacity; a full
stage charges four declared root maxima in addition to reserved terminal bookkeeping.
Guard exact before/candidate roots, original receipt and current eligibility. Before
committing the task, check the outer engine root bound and reserved outcome. Outer
capacity refusal discards the candidate and stages known local nonpublication,
without retaining an oversized root. Minimal refusal uses reserved bookkeeping.
Then commit task disposition and install root/terminal facts/done in one serialized
trusted decision with no callback, provider I/O or telemetry between them. Actual
native/concurrent/crash installation and physical accounting remain separate gates.

Record Applied, Unchanged and known NotApplied distinctly. Known stop, stale target,
current denial or capacity refusal spends local eligibility; it cannot retry an
old target later. Unexpected private/protocol failure preserves the prior root,
records Unknown/faulted, fences the domain and retains unknown local obligations.
Control or ledger retirement cannot erase them. Drained ledger retirement releases
the capsule pin, not provider work, origin issuance, evidence or retention obligations.

An accepted export followed by refused cut has confirmed external acceptance under
its named profile and local NotApplied, never effect None or compensated disclosure.
Contested evidence yields unknown effect. Reserve confirmed/unknown effect variants
for every supported terminal shape/policy ceiling before acceptance. Retained outcomes
describe the local decision then; authentic later contradiction remains current task
evidence without rolling back source or rewriting delivered facts. Live aggregation
remains separate. Report copied-not-cut only with uncontested accepted export and
known local nonpublication. Preserve independent quiescence/drain/session/retention gates.

[Clipboard invocation evidence](formal/clipboard-invocations.md) covers 512 admission/
1,024 publication/256 release combinations, 1,440 traces/8,640 edges, sixteen controls/
eighteen mutants and conditional ownership/installation/halting arguments. It includes
actual structured equal-byte annotation mapping and competing shared-root continuations.
Decoded request/dispatch replay, copy/provider gateways, full execution/event products,
native truth and concurrent/crash/physical/decoder/production/independent refinement
remain. Existing PATH-01/06, DF-11, INS-01/02/03/04/06/11/13 distinguish stage, local
result, external acceptance, current release and retained work without private labels.

## 7 Execution relation and refinement obligations

| Control state | Admitted activity | Required disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Received | Bounded validation of supported identity/schema/profile | Reject invalid input unchanged, stop on accepted cancellation/deadline, or enter preparation |
| Preparing | Bounded candidate/mapping/history staging | Remain private; become ready only when all required staging exists; resource/validation failure rejects unchanged |
| Ready | Final serialized validation and disposition | Return validated unchanged success for identity under §6.4, publish meaningful local change atomically, or reject/stop unchanged; rebuilding stays within validated request preconditions |
| Applied | Status observation or postpublication notification | Preserve committed facts; later delivery failure/cancellation cannot relabel publication |
| Validated unchanged | Bounded status observation or notification | Preserve the no-publication fact; later delivery failure/cancellation cannot manufacture a commit or rejection |
| Rejected or stopped | Status observation | No later publication for that invocation; resubmission is not an implicit restart |
| Faulted | Supervised isolation/status handling | No further unissued work in the affected scope; preserve trustworthy known facts and contain uncertainty |

Context/authority changes during preparation invalidate affected assumptions;
they never authorize mutation. Unknown external input is rejected under its
declared input contract; an unrecognized admitted internal transition is a
protocol fault, not a new verb. The complete public event/replay table remains a
companion specification, not a claim that this table covers every API byte.

Implementation refinement must preserve publication projection, identity and
dependency validity, scope, frame conditions, outcome facts and bounded progress
assumptions. An allocation strategy, lock or closed verb list alone is not that
refinement. Local termination needs declared finite work and host service; no
numeric response-time or arbitrary native-preemption theorem follows here.

## 8 Conformance and current proof coverage

| Contract obligation | Present abstract evidence | Conformance evidence still required |
|---|---|---|
| Explicit identity/dependency/current authority | PS-TX context/read-dependency checks and PS-EC scope/discovery gate | Real incarnation reuse, policy/read-only/scoped permissions and non-text dependency fixtures |
| Simultaneous replacements and expected bytes | PS-EC finite splice/strictly separated batch laws; symbolic splice/batch VCs and adjacent composition; three finite byte-edit oracles (§27.7) | General finite-list/canonicalizer and actual backend refinement, independent Unicode/profile review, insertion ties, complete malformed/overflow/budget cases |
| All-or-none source and companions | PS-TX/BR/EC restricted coherent publication and observer invariants | Actual selection/attachment/history profiles, arbitrary participants and implementation refinement |
| Rejection preserves current publication state | PS-TX/EC unchanged rejection properties | Interleavings including unrelated commits and staging/allocator failure; no rollback of concurrent work |
| Applied is not persisted or later rejected | Existing execution/save/recipient evidence separation | Public outcomes/current-gated metadata release and notification-failure integration |
| Cancellation and bounded service | Execution control/rank and PS-UP conditional closed-backlog progress | Actual publication/cancellation linearization, open-load service and deadline/resource profiles |
| Diagnostics cannot govern publication | PS-TX diagnostic isolation plus observation-index/assurance structure | Actual capture on/off/full/fault/reentrancy conformance and bounded overhead |

The present models do not yet prove this entire specification slice. In particular,
PS-EC batch exploration excludes touching edits and uses representative symbols;
its scalar UTF-8 conditions do not prove every public coordinate/profile algorithm.
Conformance tests need independently derived oracles, not only the implementation's
own change-application and mapping functions. Current hashes establish artifact
identity and existing check execution, not automatic prose-to-model refinement.

Minimum reference scenarios include two-document success; changed read-only
dependency with unchanged write targets; revoked authority or narrowed scope
after preparation; stale selection/context; partial staging allocation failure;
unrelated commit preserved on rejection/publication; cancellation on both sides
of publication; unsupported cross-authority guarantees; invalid UTF-8 endpoints;
and notification/diagnostic failure after successful publication.

## 9 Observation and threat obligations

Use existing IF-01/03, PATH-01/02 and INS-01/02 placements; companion read/release,
history, lifecycle and diagnostic contracts retain their own placements. Separate
offers, admissions, logical publications, participants, retries and record counts.
Measure preparation, queue and final-boundary duration separately, retaining
pending/censored age and declared clock domains. RED reuses these request views;
USE tracks staging/history/reservation pressure in declared units.

Observe applied/unchanged conflict/denial/capacity/stopping separately from faults
and unknown observation. A high rejection rate can reflect correct enforcement;
shedding or hiding pending work is not improved useful service. No numeric SLO is
selected, and correctness/disclosure cannot be spent as an error budget.

STRIDE covers forged context, stale targets, partial/tampered publication,
attribution limits, private participant disclosures, adversarial batch/fan-out
and diagnostic privilege. LINDDUN additionally covers activity linkage, existence
and attribution in IDs/counts/conflicts. Keep payloads, paths, raw host errors and
identity-valued metric labels out by default. Current recipient policy governs
returned detail; allowed operational disclosures follow requirements §15.6.

## 10 Decisions needed to complete this slice

These choices are collected as D01–D06 in
[the consolidated review register](specification-decisions.md). They will be
reviewed after the pass, not treated as blocking questions during drafting.

| Decision | Options and tradeoff | Recommendation for the next review |
|---|---|---|
| Empty and content-neutral batches | D01 adopted: validated unchanged success for genuine semantic identity; equal bytes alone are insufficient | §6.4 governs; concrete bounded per-operation predicates, companion completeness and API/status refinement remain |
| Adjacent edits and insertion ties | PA-02 and D02 adopted: accept unambiguous unsorted input, normalize order once, preserve complete records/boundaries and reject unresolved ties | §4.2.1 governs; actual canonicalizer, caller-resolved tie lowering, profiles/budgets and implementation refinement remain open |
| Invocation replay and status retention | D03 adopted: bounded incarnation-scoped deduplication and explicit retirement; fresh-only calls burden agents and durable replay adds recovery obligations | §6.5 governs; actual admission encoding, intent equality, finite capacity/retention and conformance remain open; no crash-durable or exactly-once external-effect guarantee |
| Scope and mapping profiles | D04 adopted: purpose-specific closed profiles over shared mapping, content-range boundary exclusion and point treatment of collapsed ranges; universal clamping can misidentify targets, universal detachment disrupts navigation | §4.3.1 governs; concrete replacement/point-context profiles, schemas, history/geometry and coordinator refinement remain; D45 owns caret/selection defaults |
| Public results and resource profile | D05 adopted: typed authoritative dimensions with recipient-safe explanations; all internal detail leaks protected state, while one generic failure loses recovery meaning | §23.1.1 governs; concrete outcome products/codes/fields, operation-specific precedence, disclosure profiles and resource defaults remain D05/D06/D09/D12/D23/D33 refinements |

These choices affect admission, no-op revisions, replay, mapping or disclosure;
they are not silently finalized by writing the successful-publication contract.

## 11 Document identity and lifecycle

This slice refines requirements §§3.4, 3.7, 3.4.2 and 15.5, with IF-10,
PATH-10 and INV-01/03/16. Operation-family names below describe semantic actions,
not assigned stable public command IDs. Source, annotations and outstanding
effect evidence keep their separate lifetimes and authority.

### 11.1 Logical state and identity evidence

A live document has one owner under one authority. Represent at least document
identity/incarnation, source revision, optional binding/generation, residency,
view references, workspace memberships and outstanding obligations as distinct
state dimensions. An unbound scratch document is valid. Closing the last view
does not make it disposed; removing a membership does not transfer ownership.

Independently usable document primitives support an embedding without a
multi-document host, but cannot remain a second live write interface to a
coordinator-owned root. An ownership attachment, detachment or transfer, if
exposed, must validate the current owner, preserve exclusive mutation and
invalidate incompatible outstanding handles/work before the new owner accepts
mutation. Do not confuse ownership attachment with attaching another view.
This is an invariant on any supported transfer, not a new mandatory transfer
API, per-document engine, process singleton or thread requirement. D43 must
preserve this distinction in the crate/type ownership boundary.

A resource binding names a host identity domain, a resource-equivalence key,
a locator, binding generation and the declared identity/continuity evidence.
Keys are comparable only under the same declared host domain. A pathname,
physical identifier, content digest or identical source is not a universal key.
The host contract must distinguish known equivalence, known distinction and
insufficient evidence. Do not turn insufficient evidence into known distinction
when satisfying a required uniqueness or write-safety guarantee depends on it.

For each admitted resource key within its host domain, at most one live writable
binding owner exists in the authority. This does not require discovering every
alias that an ordinary host cannot identify. The supported identity guarantee
and any uncertainty must remain explicit in admission and persistence contracts.

### 11.1.1 Adopted identity and continuity baseline

D07 adopts the separation above: a logical incarnation, current resource binding
and provider evidence describe different facts. A locator change is not a new
document incarnation; equal source bytes are not resource identity, and resource
identity alone is not proof of continuity across a captured write attempt.
Declare comparison domain, evidence validity and requested guarantees. Unknown
or incomparable evidence cannot satisfy a required stronger uniqueness/continuity
guarantee and cannot be relabeled known distinction to admit a second owner.
Retain the agreed ordinary-host best-effort profile where its weaker declared
guarantees suffice; this does not require an unavailable universal alias oracle.

Serialize final owner/binding activation against the current registry and grants.
Known aliases join the existing authorized owner without overwriting its source
or annotations; they do not create a second mutable root. Recheck stale prepared
activations. Incarnation and binding identifiers must not become confusable on
reuse or exhaustion: refuse before unsafe reuse rather than wrap into validity.
Opaque handles and known aliases grant no authority by possession or equivalence.
Actual host identity/continuity profiles, handle encodings and alias/replacement
conformance remain evidence gates, not consequences of this baseline.

### 11.2 Lifecycle operation relation

| Operation family | Required validation | Permitted state change and limits |
|---|---|---|
| Create scratch | Current creation authority, bounded source/profile and admission capacity | Create a fresh non-confusable incarnation and unbound owner; no file effect or borrowed existing mutable identity |
| Resolve and open | Host-declared identity evidence, requested access, current ownership/admission and required guarantees | Join an authorized existing owner for a known alias, or admit a fresh owner only when uniqueness can be satisfied. Load may precede admission but cannot overwrite an existing unsaved owner |
| Attach or detach view | Current view/document identity and allowed access/lifecycle | Update view association/generation, not document identity or source revision. Detaching the last view does not authorize discard or cancel unrelated work |
| Change workspace membership | Current membership authority/context and declared dependencies | Update membership/context only; no duplicate source owner, implicit disclosure grant, rebind or document disposal |
| Rebind or Save As binding activation | Explicit source/destination intent, destination authority, uniqueness, provider continuity and safe treatment of pending effects | Activate a new binding generation after required validation; do not redirect an already captured effect, merge another owner or silently change source identity/revision |
| Request disposal | Current incarnation and disposal authority; authorized discard or satisfied retention/persistence contract; all required obligations accounted for | Invalidate mutation handles and stop later mutation admission for that incarnation. Refuse if safe disposal cannot be established. Retained snapshots/effect evidence need not be immediately reclaimed |

These operations must report successful state change, unchanged conflict/refusal,
unsupported guarantee, stopped execution or scoped internal fault under the common
outcome contract. Their final enum and recipient projection remain open; an alias
conflict must not reveal an inaccessible existing document or its contents.

Resolution/loading and candidate preparation may perform declared host work
outside authoritative publication. Activation revalidates current ownership,
incarnation, policy and capacity in its serialized local boundary. Two concurrent
opens cannot both activate writable owners for the same admitted resource key.
A stale prepared lifecycle change rejects or rebuilds within its declared
preconditions; it cannot restore an old source/view/binding state over newer work.

Rebinding is not a disk rename, copy/export or successful save. Any associated
external effect keeps its separately captured destination, binding, attempt and
revision. An incompatible rebind or subsequent destination use must wait for or
establish the required safe disposition; a timeout/cancellation is not that
evidence. An old receipt remains attributable to its old binding and cannot mark
the current binding saved.

### 11.2.1 Current initial source activation

source-resource-read-reference/1 composes §16.1.2's owned successful source read
with F17 activate-loaded-candidate. Require the authority's current serialized
root, complete relevant writable-binding coverage, unchanged resource registration,
current authority/identity/continuity/liveness/stop, companion/version capacity and
recipient reply readiness. Resource keys are comparable only under their declared
domain; unknown identity/coverage is not known absence. A key owned by a different
artifact role is not silently admitted or joined as a source root by this profile.

At final activation, resolve the actual current live binding owner. A known source
alias joins that independently authorized owner unchanged, even if new bytes were
read or another open won during staging. Preserve dirty source/comments/history,
views and workspace membership; neither old capture nor file contents can replace
them. Joining grants no later mutation authority and needs no fresh identity or
creation capacity. A current loaded-owner lookup may avoid new I/O altogether.

When no owner exists under sufficient identity evidence, validate creation/root/
binding capacity and fresh allocation. The normalized reference uses an authority-
scoped namespace/counter, checking live/retired identities and safe increments;
this is not a selected public handle encoding. Build source revision 1, independent
serialization generation/BOM, explicit generated-newline policy, empty initial
annotations, binding/owner entry and loaded-capture baseline in one bounded new
root. Advance allocation/publication once; do not implicitly attach views/workspaces
or create ordinary edit history for materialization. Provider/host root installation
and every production companion still require refinement.

The baseline owns original received bytes/profile/BOM, binding/source/serialization
versions and attributed read origin/provider/version/coherence. It is historical
loaded evidence, not successful write, current external contents or durability.
An active created binding pins that provenance record; quiescence alone cannot
retire it. Ordinary later edits do not alter captured baseline identity. A trusted
late contradiction contests baseline eligibility but never rolls back published
or subsequently edited source, deletes comments/history or rewrites a delivered
activation result. Repeated activation cannot resurrect a disposed/rebound target.
Safe disposal/rebind/retention transfer remains separate from this initial-load
construction; source replacement/reload and annotation loading are not inferred.

[Read/activation evidence](formal/resource-read.md) includes actual codec/serializer/
identity/source-publication composition, 2,048 admission/2,048 submission/2,048
activation/eight intake masks, 60 controls/twenty mutants and authored conditional
trace arguments. The reference constructs a whole-root transition under serialized
current-root premises, not actual concurrent host installation or real identity/
permission/snapshot truth. INS-08/04/07/02/01/03/09/13 observe identity/read/codec/
activation/provenance/retention and scoped release without content/ID metric tags.

### 11.2.2 Retained lifecycle products and current mutation fences

document-lifecycle/1 under retained-lifecycle-reference/1 specifies scratch,
registered-view attach/detach, workspace membership and retained disposal. Binding
and provenance release are internal disposal substeps, not additional public
cleanup verbs or rebind/SaveAs. Require explicit identities/Boolean liveness,
unique current document identities, bounded root/relation/request/source/tag
inventories, exact variant fields and current authority/scope/continuity/stop,
resources/companions/versions/reply, lifecycle permission and complete coverage.
Actual host policy/coverage and serialized installation remain premises.

Scratch validates logical scalar UTF-8 through the actual codec table without
file-signature interpretation or normalization. Preserve valid literal U+FEFF
authoring even when current absent-signature settings would refuse serialization.
Allocate fresh identity against actual live/retired inventories and safe counters;
construct unbound source/settings/annotation generation 1, empty annotations and
no persistence baseline. No implicit view/workspace, edit history or I/O occurs.

The native Rust scratch kernel now supplies this logical birth through
`create_scratch_document_v1`: strict scalar UTF-8 preserves every leading U+FEFF,
mixed delimiter and other valid authored byte. Output serialization and generated-
newline intent are explicit and independent; currently unencodable absent-signature
output does not justify refusing or rewriting otherwise valid logical content.
Scratch source/annotation/lifecycle/pair and serialization birth generations are
one. Existing privileged byte-import constructors retain their revision/set/
lifecycle-zero baseline and one-signature decoding; this slice neither changes
that compatibility API nor selects a wire/reference-counter mapping for it.

Both inputs use one actual bounded source-owner allocator/root publisher. Check
live/retired lifetime capacity, actual logical-root headroom and publication/promise
floors before identity installation. All fallible checks/allocation precede the
callback-free row/generation assignments; fence the owner across installation.
Unexpected unwind, including final-write/before-acknowledgment, remains Unknown,
preserves other responsibility, records bounded content-free optional timing and
propagates the original panic. It is not known nonapplication or retry permission.
The logical validation, scratch service and shared birth publication have distinct
diagnostic boundaries.

Native owned scratch adds `submit_scratch_v1`, `run_scratch_v1`,
`scratch_result_v1` and `retire_scratch_v1`. Admission reserves actual parent
capture capacity before copying the complete immutable context, logical text,
serialization/newline intent, limits, publication epoch and independent result
ceilings. It neither allocates a document identity nor pins an old source root.
Fresh service checks creation/lifecycle authority and actual birth capacity; the
shared publisher binds one exact generation-one candidate to the original ticket
before its first row write. Matching retry observes that ticket, never another
allocation. No caller-chosen document identity or host allocation handshake occurs.
Result release returns only original invocation/document identity under captured
and current disclosure rights, including historical-document readability; it does
not reconstruct from a later document row or claim current liveness. Forgetting
does not rearm execution or refund capture responsibility. Protected retirement
requires owner control, retention release and delivery drain, refunds only the
original hold once, and leaves interrupted Running/Unknown and issued identity
spent. Four distinct optional content-free timed boundaries observe admission,
service, result release and retirement. Explicit native F06 V6 composes the scratch
result under original observer ownership, the captured lifecycle capability and
complete conservative wrapper funding. Common original/captured/current publication
and current receipt rights meet the native original/current disclosure ceilings.
Historical delivery does not execute work or reconstruct an allocation. V1–V5
exhaustive profiles do not change or upgrade; nested old grantless lifecycle forms
remain unavailable. A native receipt integrity fault closes only receipt delivery,
preserving protected status and independently authorized cleanup. Private V5
delegation preserves existing native checks without duplicate outer receipt timing.
Complete public decoder/discovery, full load activation and crash/physical/performance
qualification remain separate obligations.

Attach an existing registered view only under current view-write/source-read
authority, exact source/association generations and actual positional selection
normalization. Do not take a view from another document silently. Attachment and
detachment advance association, selection and viewport generations, preventing
same-view/same-document ABA from reviving owned selection/scroll plans. Membership
updates only the explicit current workspace identity/generation/member relation;
independent workspaces/source remain unchanged. Already satisfied membership is
unchanged. Last-view detachment or last-membership removal does not dispose.
Relation changes do not add a coarse global source/lifecycle write dependency.

Disposal checks source/annotation-set/serialization/binding/lifecycle generations,
independent source and annotation retain/discard authority, supported complete
effect/history/snapshot/provider retention, all current view/membership detachment,
observer fencing and binding coverage. Publish live=false, a fresh lifecycle
generation/retained-disposed phase, retained binding and identity tombstone while
detaching views/memberships with fresh generations. Preserve source/settings/
annotations/history/baseline/unrelated owners and peer work/evidence. Explicit
discard permits ending mutation admission, not inferred physical or secure erasure.
Retained data remains accounted in the same bounded authority root/peer owners;
no automatic durable-ledger migration or effect cancellation is supplied.

The native retained-disposal publisher and disposed binding/provenance substeps
now fence the coordinator before the first root installation and clear the fence
only after the complete normal publication. All expected refusal precedes that
installation boundary. Unexpected unwinding anywhere in these service bodies
fences the owner, records an optional content-free Unknown attempt and resumes the
original panic. It does not return known nonapplication or attempt rollback. A
failure after the final root write but before acknowledgment remains uncertain to
the caller; subsequent mutations fail fast instead of treating a retry as fresh.
Known pre-install refusal and already-satisfied cleanup retain their existing
non-faulting dispositions. Retained tasks, responsibility and holds are not refunded
or made quiescent through this fence; existing protected control remains separate.
These are Rust unwind checks, not process-abort/crash durability or operation-receipt
construction. Complete lifecycle invocation/receipt binding remains required.

The existing native view attachment/detachment and workspace membership publishers
apply the same owner-fence rule. All expected refusal, normalization, bounds and
allocation precede installation; validated detach/membership no-ops return without
consuming generation or entering installation. Fence before the first row write
and clear only after every row, membership counter and publication generation is
installed. Unexpected unwind anywhere in service records an optional bounded
Unknown attempt and resumes its original payload without placing that payload in

### 11.2.3 Explicit source destinations, SaveAs and pure rebind

### 11.2.11 Native view and workspace container lifecycles

Logical container birth/retirement refines §§3.4/3.7 of the requirements and
§11.2.7's registered relation operations. The trusted native control accepts
exactly {kind: view | workspace, action: create}, or {kind, action: retire,
target, expected}. View retirement expects current attachmentGeneration,
selectionGeneration and viewportGeneration; workspace retirement expects its
current generation. Missing/foreign targets, stale expectations, unknown fields
or caller-assigned creation identities refuse. There is no implicit current target.
Public invocation, reference encoding, discovery and event products remain separate.

Create through the existing bounded identityAllocation namespace/next/last. Validate
safe increment, scalar UTF-8/tag bounds and collisions against active document,
view/workspace and retired-document identities. Consume next once; never skip to
a free name, wrap, rewind or recycle after retirement. A new view is detached,
with sourceRevision 0, empty selections, primary 0, explicit-positional-selection/1
and attachment/selection/viewport generations 1. A new workspace is live with
generation 1 and no members. These are known-empty birth values, not inferred
state for imported rows. Creation does not attach/select/focus a document or UI.

Retirement removes the addressed row and its attachment/membership edges atomically,
including an attached last view or populated workspace. Preserve documents and
their text, annotations, histories, ownership, bindings, saved baselines, producer
evidence and charges, plus all peer containers and unrelated metadata. Do not save,
dispose, move focus, recall disclosed copies, stop workers or release retained
resources by inference. Missing targets refuse rather than bypass authorization
as an idempotent success; invocation replay is independently governed.

Twelve strict shared facts cover authorization/scope/continuity/liveness/stop,
resources/companions/versions/reply, owner/preparation control and complete relation
coverage. Creation additionally requires creationAllowed; retirement requires
retirementAllowed and retainedConsumersSafe. The latter attests current fencing
and retained ownership, not that all providers stopped. Existing exact lifecycle,
membership and binding profiles bound requests, root/rows and labels. Recheck
actual native root/reply caps and current annotation-baseline promise floors.

Owned certificates bind actual owner/domain/before-root and immutable request/
profile. Reconstruct the exact candidate and copied result at final validation.
Commit a frozen root and consume the certificate at one synchronous callback-free
boundary, advancing publication once and allocation only for creation. Carry actual
source journals. Return only internal {status: created | retired, kind, target};
do not expose raw state/certificate descriptors through public interfaces.
Rejection leaves root, allocator and producer accounting unchanged. Current native
attach/membership operations accept new containers; old selection/membership
publication refuses after retirement. Independent old work/evidence retains its
own owner and discharge contract; absence is not completion.

Within the known initial native lifetime, existing native creations never decrease
the allocator and retirement never changes it. This supports conditional identity
nonreuse and per-call bounded halting, not imported lifetime recovery, durable
identity, global categorical closure or a replacement/removal lattice. Authored
conditional arguments and scoped reference evidence are in
[formal/relation-lifecycle.md](formal/relation-lifecycle.md): 42 stages, 252 native
publications, 49,152 fact vectors, 162 strict refusals, thirteen controls and twenty

host/retention truth, imported recovery, installed measurement, physical/concurrent/
crash refinement and independent assurance remain gates. No requirement, public
verb, native job, component, network path, numeric default or SMT condition changes.

Initial preparation requires the actual issued ticket and current full invocation

Preparation captures immutable meaning, not a replacement root. Service constructs

Final commit rechecks the exact owned stage/before-root/candidate/receipt and

A trusted protocol contradiction faults conservatively to unknown publication with

The result contains only invocation, created/retired status, kind and target.
Release requires admission's relationResultIdentifiersAllowed exactly true, complete

The target is historical engine-local identity, not proof of current existence,

Forget clears retained outcome/receipt without reopening execution; authorized

and view/workspace container result. Construction and current release share
immutable exact-field declarations, UTF-8 identity/value guards and closed
discriminators. Source-load activation and annotation phase/disposition constrain
their applied/unchanged statuses. Basic document status shape does not establish
that every operation/status pair is natively executable.

The result envelope remains exactly result with receipt, or unavailable without
one. Original native domain/ticket, captured identifier ceiling, current scope,
whole-outcome availability, operation-specific release facts and complete result
byte ceiling remain independent. Structurally valid copies or foreign identities
grant no authority. Internal discharge receipt vocabulary does not add public
cleanup commands, queries, wire codes or new result fields.

Before installing a stage or committing its native producer, construction checks
the receipt. Malformed construction discards the native preparation before raising
a protocol fault through the existing invocation fence. Root and external producer
history are not rolled back; the original ticket retains protected retirement,
and issuance/start history stays spent. Current release refuses malformed retained
values without rewriting authoritative outcomes.

Six controls cover 48 native results, 1,136 malformed refusals, 56 release cases,
six whole-envelope boundaries and 178 structural positives. Twenty-four targeted
mutants and 28 fixed malformed-construction cases include native discard witnesses,
zero calls at the targeted producer commit sites, unchanged roots and original
ticket retirement. See formal/lifecycle-results.md. Import/tool errors are not
semantic mutant detections; existing native regression banks remain obligations.

The selected graph is 96 modules without frontend imports; clean-entrypoint
coverage expands with it. Components/interfaces and the 76/11 partition are
unchanged. IF-01/03/08/10 and INS-01/02/03/08/12/13 retain preparation/publication/
release/fault/discharge distinctions without raw receipt/identity labels.
Public operation-specific result access, complete discovery/events, additional
profiles, shared-parent temporary/physical, host/measurement/independent and full
frozen adoption gates remain open.

#### 11.2.13.7 Actual parent funding for lifecycle envelopes

Both existing F17 data-envelope adapters reserve temporary logical workspace from
the actual invocation parent's remaining capacity before normalization. For parent
intent bound M, reserve four M-sized serialized frames: bounded whole-envelope
capture, bounded context capture, bounded canonical record and producer
reconstruction. Each copied record is independently limited by M; the producer
request is contained in the canonical record. The activation path may reuse that
request rather than copy it; the common reservation is conservative.

Check finite arithmetic and headroom before the first capture, then debit the
actual parent. The existing slot preparation guard spans capture, original native
authority validation and native preparation. Insufficient capacity refuses without
native preparation, publication, spent issuance or faulting the owner. A finally
path refunds exactly this temporary reservation on success, ordinary refusal or
unexpected fault. It does not release a native retained preparation, another
registry's reservation or lifetime issuance, and does not reopen a faulted domain.

This supersedes only the temporary-parent accounting exclusions in §§11.2.13.2/5/6
for the five basic and nine activation forms. Existing request fields, native
profiles, opaque authority roles, job kinds, publication and receipt semantics are
unchanged. It does not establish physical allocation, hostile reflection costs,
complete F17 discovery/events, U01 result retrieval or F18 shutdown fencing.
[Scoped evidence](formal/lifecycle-workspace.md) covers both routes, exact remaining
capacity boundaries, temporary refund and retained native obligations.

### 11.3 Disposal and retention predicates

Let `Live(d)` mean that a document incarnation still accepts managed mutation.
Let `Obligations(d)` identify required authored-state, history, snapshot, worker
and external-effect obligations under their respective contracts. `CanDispose`
requires current authority, a permitted disposition of unsaved authored state,
and a supported retention/disposition contract for every obligation that disposal
would otherwise invalidate. The precise profile is not inferred from saved text.

Successful disposal sets `Live(d)` false and invalidates its mutation references.
Later opens use a non-confusable incarnation; old tasks or tokens cannot resurrect
the disposed owner. Pure late computations cannot publish to a new incarnation.
Necessary late effect evidence remains accepted at its trusted operation/host
scope under its evidence contract, even if the document or original observer
has gone away.

Disposal does not imply zero remaining allocations, worker quiescence, physical
erasure, completed external effects, revoked bytes already disclosed or crash
recovery. Where an obligation cannot be safely preserved outside the disposed
owner or discharged under a supported contract, disposal is refused rather than
silently dropping it. No automatic migration to a durable ledger is supplied.

Published retained snapshots remain immutable. A live root and worker may share
storage; cloning a handle cannot manufacture quota, and cancellation intent cannot
refund live retained obligations. Dropping eligible derived caches must not erase
unsaved authored state, split a retained history group or lose required effect
evidence. Exact accounting/reclamation units and admission policy remain §11.5.

### 11.3.1 Adopted residency and disposal baseline

D08 selects retained admitted owners with explicit disposal for base v1. Neither
last-view detachment, workspace removal, optional cache pressure nor a request
cancellation implicitly disposes an owner or discards authored source/annotations.
Under pressure reclaim only eligible derived data whose retained obligations allow
it; refuse new atomic admission under §17.2.2 instead of silently evicting authored
state. Existing explicitly bounded queue contracts remain unchanged.

Evaluate disposal against current authority and source and annotation dispositions
separately. Saved source does not establish saved annotations or consent to their
discard. Required history, snapshot, worker and external-effect obligations must
either have a justified discharge or remain owned, accounted and addressable by
their supported retention contract after mutation admission stops. If that cannot
be established, refuse disposal unchanged. Disposal never itself proves physical
reclamation, worker quiescence, effect completion or secure erasure.

Post-disposal retained evidence uses its historical identity/binding and current
release rules; it cannot mutate a reopened incarnation. Reopening requires fresh
identity, current admission and any required safe destination disposition.
No durable recovery service, automatic unload or new ownership-transfer API is
introduced. Complete-group/pin/floor details remain D14; actual retention ownership,
discharge witnesses and resource accounting remain implementation obligations.
formal/identity-residency.md records scoped guard/frame checks and their limits.

### 11.4 Conformance and observations

| Obligation | Required reference scenario | Existing evidence and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| One binding owner | Concurrent alias opens/rebind activation under a host identity oracle | INV-01/SCN-07 intent; full identity/activation refinement remains open |
| Independent lifetimes | Close last view or remove membership with unsaved text/history/pending work | SCN-07; no last-view-implies-discard default |
| Safe disposal | Refuse unsatisfied discard/retention obligations; permit only a declared safe disposition | Existing history/effect/retention slices are partial, not a general disposal proof |
| No resurrection | Reopen after disposal, then deliver stale edit/parse/effect results | Incarnation/result gates and historical-binding models are partial; actual handle reuse requires a separate oracle |
| Honest resource identity | Unknown alias evidence cannot satisfy a requested stronger guarantee | Provider/domain contracts and ordinary filesystem conformance remain inputs |

INS-08 observes resolution/admission/activation/refusal, binding changes and
retention pressure; INS-04/05/13 retain effect, worker and shutdown boundaries.
Separate offered opens from created owners, joined views and physical attempts.
No raw paths, resource keys or document/principal identities become default
metric labels. STRIDE covers alias spoofing, stale activation, owner duplication
and unsafe disposal; LINDDUN covers existence/linkage through join/conflict detail.
Fault detection or telemetry cannot establish provider truth or authorize discard.

### 11.5 Remaining lifecycle decisions

Section 11.2.2 supplies normalized same-authority post-disposal retention/key/
provenance release. Concrete reference/token encodings, provider resource-equivalence/
continuity profiles, native retention ownership and measured release budgets remain
specification/refinement gates. D07/D08 baseline contracts are §§11.1.1/11.3.1; §17.2.2 rejects new
atomic proposals that cannot fit and preserves explicitly bounded queue contracts.
Actual lifecycle accounting and provider conformance remain open. No automatic
unload, durable recovery, filesystem alias oracle, confirmation dialog or new
persistence guarantee is introduced here.

## 12 Mediated reads and recipient projections

This slice refines requirements §§3.4.2, 15.5–15.6 and 12.8 with IF-02/08/09,
PATH-02/11 and INV-08/09/12. It governs headless and UI delivery equally, including
historical reads, annotation/derived metadata, accessibility/surrounding text,
clipboard or diagnostic export where the corresponding capability is provided.
It does not introduce a remote transport or model service.

### 12.1 Logical request and retained context

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Recipient access context | Host-established actual recipient/executor and accepted policy context; author labels and trace IDs do not establish permission |
| Operation and target scope | Logical operation, document incarnation and requested source revision/range, version set or historical scope |
| Data and projection scope | Requested source/history/annotation/derived/metadata/diagnostic classes and the profile's allowed field projection |
| Destination or purpose | Required disclosure destination/purpose where the supplied policy distinguishes them; reading for editing is not automatically permission to export |
| Context and retention reference | Exact captured snapshot/version set, relevant producer generations and retained availability; neither a token nor retention is a grant |
| Delivery profile | Declared bounded release unit, current-policy/lease validity contract, pending-work handling and resource bounds |

Preparation may retain internal immutable state or build a candidate response.
Producer acceptance and recipient release are separate transitions. A trusted
owner may accept necessary late effect evidence even when the original caller
cannot receive it. Do not discard authoritative evidence to hide it from a
recipient; keep it internally and deliver only the permitted projection.

A raw immutable snapshot or unrestricted memory reference is already disclosure
of the reachable content to its trusted recipient. Only an actually mediated
interface can promise later current-policy checks. A token for such an interface
does not itself disclose its payload or acquire mutation authority. The supported
API must distinguish these contracts rather than call both revocable snapshots.

### 12.2 Release predicate and ordering

For an actual delivery `r`, `ReleaseAllowed(S, r)` requires all of:

1. Its recipient and requested target incarnation/context match the admitted
   request and a supported current lifecycle state.
2. Accepted policy permits the actual data fields, scope and destination/purpose
   at the declared local release boundary.
3. Required policy/lease validity evidence is available and current under its
   explicit contract; no assumed network consultation repairs missing evidence.
4. The retained requested snapshot/context is available, and the delivery's
   source and derived-coverage claims accurately identify it.
5. Its projection and resource/delivery profile are valid; any continuity or gap
   prerequisite for an incremental stream is satisfied.

Serialize each bounded release decision against accepted local policy/lifecycle
updates at its declared ordering point. Admission or response preparation does
not authorize a later release. Queued responses must be discarded or reprojected
when their scope is no longer permitted. This ordering is distinct from source
publication and does not hold the publication boundary across recipient callbacks
or host I/O. Concrete handoff ownership/lease mechanics remain §12.6.

When allowed, deliver the bounded permitted projection with its truthful
version/scope/coverage meaning. Otherwise deliver no forbidden payload. The public
unavailable/denied/expired shape follows the disclosure profile, not the richer
internal cause. A permitted source revision alone cannot authorize private
annotation/history/derived fields or a different outbound destination.

Revocation limits future releases. It cannot recall already disclosed bytes,
completed exports, unrestricted snapshots, allocator/OS state or backups. Retained
data availability, visibility loss and author deletion are different facts.

### 12.3 Publication handoff and incremental streams

A known successful publication supports a handoff to its identified resulting
snapshot/version set under current release and bounded retention. Rendering or
an index need not catch up before authoritative source can be read. If the exact
requested context is no longer retained, report unavailable/expired rather than
substitute a newer root under the old receipt. Derived results may remain pending,
partial, unsupported or unknown despite available authoritative source.

| Stream state or event | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Initial request/admission | Validate recipient/target/data scope and establish only the declared bounded context, not a perpetual grant |
| Prepared or queued delivery | Retain internal obligations under bounds; release only after the current release predicate succeeds |
| Incremental delivery | Identify authorized source context and continuity; recheck each declared batch/lease boundary |
| Missing delta, invalid context or visibility gap | Expose an authorized gap/invalidation disposition and stop treating subsequent deltas as a continuous baseline |
| Revocation, expiry or disposal | Prevent later unauthorized deliveries; discard/reproject pending responses and cancel/release only safely disposable work |
| Regrant | Do not silently resume the old stream; establish an authorized resynchronization baseline/continuity before new incremental delivery |
| Snapshot resynchronization | Use current permitted projection and exact available context, not unfiltered historical replay or implicit disclosure of hidden records |

Gap/cursor/baseline identifiers are projection-scoped data, not raw global event
sequence numbers or grants. Their concrete retention and token schema remain
open. An end of caller waiting is not a producer cancellation or deletion of an
unresolved effect obligation.

### 12.3.1 Recipient publication observation reference

Existing F19 stream/stop/resync products observe post-publication projected state,
not raw coordinator ticks or subscriber callbacks inside editing. An exact owned
context fixes recipient/purpose/destination, policy/continuity epoch and explicit
source, named-annotation facets and view scopes. Host reference/visibility truth
remains a premise. Project actual permitted source/revision, selected annotation
facets and current view state; omit global publication/annotation-set generations.
Named-record scope does not imply automatic collection-wide discovery.

If permitted state is equal, issue no generation and queue no event. A changed
projection queues a bounded full-state replacement with exact preceding/following
recipient generations. Bound projections, envelopes, queues, reports and lifetime
issuance before admission. On overflow/unrepresentability create a gap and clear
queued frames; require authorized fresh baseline resync before further progress.
Resync clears old queued data and cannot overcome exhausted issuance. Never claim
a complete suffix after silent loss or expose missing global counts/cursors.

Current release rechecks context/epoch, rights, continuity/liveness, retention and
transfer. Observed context/authorization invalidity at release or root observation
permanently fences the old observer; regrant needs a new observer/baseline. Protected
owner stop closes only observation. No observer failure rejects an already committed
edit or proves producer/effect discharge. Local opaque references select no wire
format or native queue implementation. Logical charges are not physical costs.

[Reference evidence](formal/publication-observation.md) composes actual publication,
annotation and outcome helpers: 768 gate/24 release decisions, 256 selected paired
worlds, two chain traces, ten controls/twelve mutants and conditional arguments.
All-family/collection/lifecycle events, actual host policy/reference truth, full
invocation/replay/F06 integration, native/concurrent ownership, hostile decoding,
physical/timing/resource noninterference and independent assurance remain gates.

#### 12.3.1.1 Original claim binding before trusted observer release

Two fixed native composition ports bind event and existing minimal publication-
outcome release to the actual observer's retained original scope before invoking
the trusted /2 helper. A malformed, foreign or wrong-role native claim returns
unavailable without applying its context as loss evidence, changing the queue,
spending issuance or changing producer state. The native claim is a bounded
first-party lowering after original reference resolution, not a public payload
requiring disclosure of private annotation identities or retained scope internals.

Resolve the actual opaque observer owner. Validate the existing bounded native
scope structure, its original outcome epoch and every fixed scope field against
that owner's retained scope. Outcome-permission flags in the claim establish
neither authority nor current disclosure policy. Independently attributed trusted
current context/facts for this exact observer then govern the existing native
release, including absorbing accepted loss, captured/current outcome ceilings,
temporary pressure, bounded copied frames and owned outcome handles. Claimed
currentness cannot replace those ports; their physical identity/policy truth is
not proved by Boolean values. The existing trusted helpers remain unchanged.

No new retained context copy, token, job, invocation, result hold or public verb is
created. Event release and minimal-outcome release are separate decisions, not a
joint delivery transaction. This does not select U01's operation-specific receipt
route, a public context schema, hostile decoder, actual root/domain binding,
heterogeneous F19 dispatch or establishment/resync/grant-control assembly.

The existing normalized bounded inert-input, truthful complete current-port and
serialized non-reentrant premises apply. Fixed scope comparison followed by the
existing bounded native traversal terminates conditionally. Refusal precedes all
observer writes; after a successful guard, the native owner's current release

| --- | --- |
