installed discovery routes are described in §12.3.9.

An interrupted native acknowledgment retains a Faulted command with started work
and no invented result. Its actual publisher refuses new ordinary establishment,
sampling, resync and event delivery; protected native stop/retirement and inspection
remain available where their original guards permit. Do not heal the authored
engine, infer nonexecution or refund the command. Every retained command pins its
original document even after the stream retires. Final document reclamation must
recompute those pins. Known supported command retirement requires current original
scope/control, retention release and delivery drain, does not stop its stream, and
does not erase lifetime issuance. Parent publisher retirement additionally requires
the command table's actual protected discharge. Unknown started commands cannot be
retired by asserting a caller cleanup Boolean. Facet/collection adoption, F06 and
whole C1/C4/C5 assembly remain open; native tests are not complete formal proof.

### 12.3.8 Native source-command historical receipts

The actual source command table optionally owns a separately parent-funded receipt
pool. It prepays bounded context slots, original scope copies and complete reply
frames. Context issuance is lifetime-bounded and never recycled. Opening a receipt
requires a settled original command, an allowed complete-original-result ceiling,
separate receipt admission/disclosure authority and exact original-result/current-
root authorization correlation. Command control or ordinary source-read permission
does not supply those rights. A successful baseline and a known returned native
error remain distinct original products; neither is an outer authorization refusal.

Privileged authorizer input identifies the original source version or native error
and an opaque basis bound to command/result identity, current native root and, at
delivery, exact receipt context. Admission and delivery bases are not interchangeable.
The basis uses weak allocation identity, grants no authority and creates no managed
payload hold. Root equality alone does not prove external policy truth: the host
must independently affirm current authorization for that exact basis at each call.
An authorized reply is the complete original result, not a filtered replacement or
current source projection. Returning its immutable snapshot is explicit disclosure;
later revocation cannot recall the recipient's copy.

Validate original roles/root before applying loss. Stale/foreign bases or missing
authorization fail closed without stopping an unrelated context. Explicit current
loss under a valid basis closes only that receipt, absorbingly. Capacity refusal
does not revoke it. New positive delivery also requires healthy native ordinary
service and a complete frame fitting both the actual pool and caller reply bounds.
It does not rerun the original command, resync a stream or alter authored content.

Every native receipt, including stopped ones, retains a real claim on its original
command. Command retirement refuses while claimed; the command table cannot retire
before receipt-pool discharge. Original command and receipt incidences participate
in actual document reclamation. Orphaned claims or lost funding fault rather than
becoming zero pins. Protected stop and stopped-context retirement retain their
original scope/control/discharge guards without ordinary data rights or spare
capacity, including under an editing fault. They neither heal that fault nor cancel
or retire the producer. Only actual retirement removes the claim; parent pool
discharge is separate and once-only.

Optional bounded capture covers configuration, basis capture/validation, admission,
release, explicit closure and cleanup. Basis rejection and confirmed policy closure
are distinct events; nested service episodes overlap and are not additive latency.
No native identity, policy label or source text enters those records. This supplies
native source receipt behavior, not heterogeneous receipt stop/revocation or
facet/collection integration. Host policy
truth, physical memory/erasure, release-workload qualification and full formal
refinement are not proved by the focused Rust scenarios.

### 12.3.9 Source publication native facade and installed discovery

Closed typed/dynamic native envelopes lower to the existing source command and
receipt owners. Commands use fixed 2/4/4 objects; receipt queries use 2/4/5/1,
including the sole `source-baseline` facet. Original opaque command/operation/
stream/context matching precedes any native execution or observed-loss effect.
Receipt output validation checks the actual original result allocation/error and
complete reply bounds before disclosure; invalid producer output closes that
receipt without erasing claims or faulting unrelated authored state.

The installed discovery source declares both command variants and the F06 receipt
query, with outer-structure-only schemas. Its private origin requires actual
configured publisher/command/receipt ownership and matching authority/engine;
copied generic metadata cannot install handlers. Fixed metadata staging is prepaid
by the discovery parent. Original selectors and current discovery release precede
independent native authorization. Protected direct replay/control does not require
discovery headroom. This introduces no wire codec, HTTP, UI or policy evaluator.

### 12.4 Field projection and cache validity

The host policy profile declares the existence, body, target/quote, authorship,
status/time and aggregate/activity distinctions it enforces. This requires honest
field coverage, not a particular user-role product or policy engine. Enumerations,
counts, navigation, search, events, export and accessibility consume that same
authorized projection. A complete count means complete for its declared visible
scope, not all stored records or semantically complete discovery.

Tokens, pagination, caches and event contexts must include valid projection/policy
scope in their contracts; document source revision alone is insufficient. Do not
reuse a richer response for a less privileged recipient. Policy/membership change
invalidates or rebuilds affected recipient caches. Hidden-only annotation changes
cannot drive exposed source revisions, annotation events, raw coordinator sequence
gaps or participant lists for an unauthorized recipient.

Where existence is not permitted, nonexistent, denied, stale and conflicting
causes use the common caller-facing unavailable projection specified by that
profile. Internal authoritative causes stay truthful. Blocked/capacity responses
may expose only the declared operational interference; perfect timing/resource
noninterference is not implied. Removing displayed data after visibility loss
must not claim that its author deleted it.

For fixed recipient policy and equal authorized source/annotation projections,
changes only to inaccessible annotations must preserve protected functional
outputs: visible bodies, counts, identifiers, source revision and annotation-
specific events, except the operational disclosures expressly allowed by the
profile. This is the bounded paired-state observation obligation, not constant-
time behavior or secrecy against shared memory/resource contention or the trusted
host. D12 specifies the protected fields and allowed operational outputs; the
existing paired models cover selected profiles, not every API/sink or all privacy.

Diagnostic/support/health recipients have independent scope; hashing or aggregate
counts do not establish safe disclosure. A remediation action enters the ordinary
validated command path and cannot gain authority from an observation.

### 12.5 Conformance and present evidence

| Obligation | Required scenario | Present evidence and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Current delivery, not historical grant | Prepare; revoke/expire/dispose; attempt release, including queued batches and exports | PS-DI/RB/PV and EC release checks cover restricted profiles; not every API/sink |
| Exact historical handoff | Publish; retain or evict that revision; request by its publication context | Snapshot immutability alone is not receipt-named historical lookup; this composition/refinement remains open |
| Gap handling | Lose a delta or revoke/regrant; require authorized baseline before further delivery | PS-EC selected event-gap and PS-DI/PV regrant evidence; general stream queues/order/tokens remain open |
| Field-safe projections | Vary hidden bodies/existence and cache privilege while comparing authorized bodies/counts/tokens/events | Paired PS-DI/RB/PV checks are partial; all fields, timing/resources, native UI and actual exports need independent scenarios |
| Lifetime separation | Dispose owner while a disclosed raw snapshot/worker still retains bytes | PS-DR source-cell retention is partial; no promise to recall memory or count all native/result allocations |
| Optional diagnostics | Disable/overload/lose capture while current policy and authoritative outcomes remain correct | Existing isolation/structural checks; actual capture/drain and host-sink conformance remain pending |

INS-03/12 observe current release/denial, policy freshness, pending age,
gap/resync, retention pressure and diagnostic loss with safe bounded fields.
INS-04/05 retain producer/effect milestones rather than infer them from recipient
records. STRIDE and LINDDUN cover spoofed contexts, stale cache scope, record
tampering, private existence/correlation, floods and diagnostic privilege. Health
off, unavailable, unknown, dropped and observed zero remain distinguishable.

### 12.6 Adopted scoped reference and local release baseline

D09–D12/D42 adopt the following baseline within the approved direction. References
are bounded opaque selectors for retained contexts, not bearer grants, raw global
sequence counters or promises of indefinite availability. Their validity relation
binds the relevant authority, recipient, document incarnation, exact requested
snapshot/history scope, destination/purpose, projection and continuity context.
Only actual dependencies need be encoded or retained, but none may be replaced
by source revision alone. Retirement/exhaustion must not make an obsolete reference
valid for a different context. Missing/expired/unavailable retention never means
empty content or permission to substitute a new snapshot under the old reference.
Actual encodings, retention periods and capacity profiles remain specified separately.

The base profile has no release lease. Each bounded delivery requires current
accepted grant and scope evidence, exact retained availability and valid continuity.
If the relevant policy/lifecycle context is invalidated, a prepared delivery is
unavailable until newly authorized preparation/resynchronization establishes a
valid context. A regrant is not proof that a visibility gap never happened.
Current projection may only narrow the authorized capture ceiling; a broader
grant/request requires newly authorized preparation before releasing more fields.
Permitted source, annotation existence/body/target/provenance, counts, events,
history, derived evidence and diagnostics are distinct disclosure dimensions.

Choose the local ownership-transfer point as the release linearization boundary.
Final validation and transfer of one bounded permitted owned value occur in the
same serialized local decision relative to accepted policy/lifecycle changes.
An engine-owned queue stays internal: a prior enqueue decision does not authorize
its later recipient handoff. Conversely, a queue or memory reference already
readable by the actual recipient is disclosure at that earlier boundary and
cannot be described as a revocable internal queue. Transfer does not wait for
rendering, recipient execution or physical export. Do not invoke arbitrary
recipient/provider callbacks under this decision; preparation, bounded trusted
transfer mechanics and eventual recipient execution have separate responsibilities.
Queue capacity, exact lock/channel mechanics and outbound effect contracts remain
implementation/provider gates, not a new mandatory message transport.

Apply one declared recipient-safe projection to payloads and related envelopes:
identifiers, token validity/errors, counts, pagination, events, caches and recovery
guidance must not contradict its existence/activity rules. Where existence is
withheld, use the profile's common unavailable envelope for nonexistent, denied,
expired/stale and conflicting contexts, preserving the real causes internally.
Build projected counts/cursors from the permitted domain rather than filtering a
globally indexed result afterward. A cached richer candidate must be reprojected
within its capture ceiling at current release or refused; it is not a grant.
Exact public fields, allowed operational interference and independent diagnostic
profiles remain D12/D36–D38 refinement; no constant-time or anonymity guarantee is added.

The supported local access baseline is a trusted embedding host establishing actual
logical recipients and accepted grants. Mediated APIs honor distinctions among
data classes, operations and destinations/purposes that the supported profile
declares; paths, producer namespaces, labels and document content confer no rights.
This permits one trusted-host context or multiple mediated logical recipients,
without adding accounts, federation, a policy engine or network consultation.
No claim protects against a hostile host or hostile code with unrestricted shared
memory access. Raw snapshot APIs must explicitly identify their trusted disclosure
contract; bytes already transferred remain outside future-release revocation.

formal/scoped-release.md records conditional arguments and finite reference checks.
They do not prove actual authentication, policy truth, historical lookup, native
export, transport security or whole-implementation refinement.

### 12.7 Remaining release refinements

Concrete read/historical/cursor encodings and implementation of §§12.8–12.9's
lifetime/retention rules; actual
bounded batch sizes and transfer implementation; field/error/operational-disclosure
profiles; and subscription ordering/resynchronization schemas still need specification.
The adopted base profile has current per-batch checks, no lease, and serialized
owned-value handoff without arbitrary callbacks. Additional supported profiles
require explicit contract/evidence rather than inheriting this baseline's claims.
Unknown required policy evidence fails closed, but its safe public reason and
resource accounting must follow the selected profile. No hidden service, secure
erasure, globally ordered history or universal timing guarantee is selected.

### 12.8 Version 1 mediated read context acquisition

The existing F02 `snapshot-handoff` has a mediated native product labeled
`read-context/1`; formal/read-contexts.json records its exact fields. It acquires
a read context for explicitly requested source, annotation or combined data.
This refines the handoff variant, not the four execution categories or a new
verb/service. F02's bounded source reads and trusted raw source snapshots do not
implicitly gain annotation access. F03 consumes a context with annotation scope;
annotation-only acquisition does not require permission to read source bytes.

The request contains `contract`, `operation`, `document`, `selection`, `data` and
`profile`. `document` is one explicit live authority/document/incarnation reference.
`selection` is one closed product: `capture-current` with no additional fields,
or `retained` with a scoped exact `reference`. `data` is a nonempty bounded set
drawn from `source` and `annotations`; duplicate/unknown members reject, not an
arbitrary field-path language. `profile` resolves supported finite projection,
preparation, delivery and retention rules. It identifies an exact accepted
interpretation/profile context, not a mutable display name; relevant context
change invalidates the base context. All requested data classes require
current accepted authority. Unsupported or unauthorized requested scope refuses
the request; do not silently return a narrower successful acquisition.

`capture-current` chooses one coherent published root at the owner capture point,
not a promise of latest state at later delivery. `retained` resolves the exact
named available snapshot/publication context under its historical contract; it
never substitutes current content. Reference possession, a source revision, or an
old receipt does not authorize lookup or expansion beyond an available projection.
If the reference only retains a narrower projection, it cannot reconstruct missing
fields by being relabeled richer. A broader authorized capture needs actual
available authoritative data and a new context. No file read or provider discovery
is launched implicitly to repair missing historical state.

Reserve bounded preparation/retention before pinning or copying a root. Prepare
an owned immutable projection with exact source/annotation association, permitted
record domain/fields, owner incarnation, actual recipient, destination/purpose,
accepted policy/continuity and interpretation. New ordinary publications need not
invalidate it. Revalidate all relevant current identity/policy/profile/lifecycle,
capacity and stop conditions at installation and selector handoff. This serialized
decision installs the bounded registry entry and transfers the permitted result
coherently, or exposes no selector/data and installs no partial entry. An internal
prepared/enqueued value is not public acquisition. Do not hold this boundary
across I/O, arbitrary code, rendering or recipient execution.

The successful mediated product contains `context` and the admitted `data` set.
The context is an opaque non-grant selector, usable as F03's `snapshot` or the
matching F02 mediated source context. It does not expose raw global publication/
annotation-set generations, storage addresses or hidden counts. Public permitted
version facts accompany actual content under the owning query contract, not an
unrestricted root handle. Failure uses the base common `unavailable` product;
internal cause, acquisition versus content delivery and authoritative mutation
outcomes remain separate. Copying a selector neither copies authority nor buys
retention quota. Raw snapshot handoff remains an explicitly different trusted
disclosure contract; its readable extent is disclosed at transfer.

This product selects a single-document coherent source/annotation context.
Required multi-document coherent version sets retain their explicit shared-
publication contract; independent acquisitions do not create that guarantee.
Section 12.10 supplies their native acquisition/ownership products; complete
native adapters and actual shared-root acquisition still require evidence.

### 12.8.1 Current read acquisition following observation

Event generations and observer-local annotation references identify their stream
products; they are not F02 retained snapshots, F03 record selectors or read grants.
A client can use existing F02 `snapshot-handoff` with `capture-current` and then
F03 enumeration to obtain independently issued query selectors. This adds no public
request field, reference conversion, transport or historical event lookup. Current
capture can be newer than the delivered event; do not attribute its values to the
event's generation. Exact historical capture requires its own actual authorized
retained snapshot reference, without fallback to current content.

The normalized trusted-host composition reuses the live owned observer's scope,
current root and fresh owned visibility preparation. Recheck current scope/grant,
liveness/continuity/stop, projection, coverage, resources and release. Source access
requires its captured source ceiling; annotation access requires complete collection
mode rather than a named subset presented as a complete document collection.
Intersect row body/target permission with the capture ceiling. Combined requests
refuse a denied class instead of returning a narrower success. Annotation-only
access does not require source-read authority or expose privately retained source.

Prepare using the actual shared projector, then acquire through the existing read
registry with exact document/recipient/purpose/destination/policy/continuity/profile.
The read selector and immutable capture have their own bounds and lifecycle.
Check read preparation completeness/reservation before copying its capture or
consuming visibility preparation, independently of later registry admission.
Temporary projected references do not install observer bindings, advance its
generation or queue events; failed read installation installs no partial context.
This conservative reference uses existing observer staging bounds and refuses a
gap until recovery. Ordinary independent F02 acquisition is not made conditional
on having a subscription. Single-use visibility preparation remains consumed on
a validated projection attempt even if read admission later refuses.

F03 enumeration mints its own record/continuation selectors. Neither a stream token
nor a stream annotation reference is accepted in their place. Future query release
rechecks current authority and cannot expand captured facets. Observer stop prevents
new composed captures but does not silently close an already acquired read context;
its own closure retires its dependent selectors under §12.9. Current policy and
liveness checks remain mandatory for both independently retained products.

[Composition evidence](formal/observation-reads.md) includes 512 read-gate/2,048
release combinations, 16 facet cases, 64 paired worlds, twelve controls/ten mutants
and conditional arguments through actual observer/read/query helpers. Host root/
policy/order/reservation/retention truth, historical event lookup/direct selector
conversion, all lifecycle/event/multi-document profiles, invocation/replay, native/
concurrent/physical/timing/resource/hostile-decoder and independent refinement remain
gates. INS-03/08/13 distinguish current acquisition, read-registry installation,
query release, retained snapshots and protected closure without raw IDs/content/token
metric labels. Read installation is not INS-02 authored-publication traffic.

### 12.8.2 Native annotation edits and independently retained current reads

The §12.8.1 current-read path composes with actual normalized F13 creation, body
updates, reattachment and deletion, and same-ledger F14 undo/redo. This uses the
existing F02/F03 contracts; no reference conversion, new verb or historical event
lookup is introduced. All six native document/range/explicit-profile point target
forms participate without selecting their unresolved on-disk point representation.

A fresh authorized capture reads the actual root at its own serialized capture
point, not the last delivered event or original writer receipt. Source-driven
mapping and independent authored-field merges use the current record placement and
versions. Deletion removes current visible membership; restoration uses fresh
authored version floors. An older independently retained read preserves its original
permitted values/membership, including through deletion/restoration. Every release
still rechecks that read context's current scope and authority. Historical values
do not claim current liveness or provide a fresh write precondition.

Writer result authority, recipient stream authority and read authority remain
independent. Neither receipt publication/native identity nor event generation/
annotation reference is an F02 context or F03 record selector. Enumerate the new
context to obtain its own query selectors. Selectors cannot cross retained contexts;
body/target facets cannot widen. Annotation-only capture grants no source access,
and combined capture cannot silently omit a denied class. Current read preparation
does not install observer bindings, queue events or count as authored publication.

Read admission or query capacity refusal cannot revert an applied edit. Receipt
eviction, observer stop and read closure affect only their independently owned
products; current permission checks remain mandatory. A stream gap refuses captures
through that observer until explicit recovery, without invalidating an independent
read or claiming the edit failed. Ordinary F02 acquisition remains independent of
subscriptions. Public wire/alias bridges are not implied by this separation.

[Native composition evidence](formal/annotation-reads.md) includes 448 combinations
of native operations, targets, captured/current facets and visibility, 896 history
stages, 2,048 read-admission/8,192 observer-release combinations, 32 hidden-world
pairs and thirteen controls/fourteen assertion-rejected
mutants with a passing dynamic baseline. Conditional preservation and finite-loop
arguments use actual producer/ledger/history/projector/read/query helpers. Existing
205 SMT conditions/thirteen manifests are unchanged. Actual issuer/policy/visibility/
order/retention truth, public wire, all lifecycle/multi-document products, full
retirement/general mapping/point storage and physical/concurrent/native/decoder/
timing/resource/production/independent refinement remain gates. INS-01/02/03/06/07/
08/12/13 distinguish edit success, receipt/event/read delivery, gaps, admission,
query latency, retention and independent closure without raw content/identity/token
metric labels. MELT/RED/golden/USE and STRIDE/LINDDUN apply at those boundaries.

### 12.8.3 Observed invalidation in owned retained readers

The selected native discovery, history and invocation-observation readers record
observed context loss as an absorbing delivery transition. This extends the
settings/resource profiles in §§22.2.1.1/22.2.2.1 without assigning every gate the
same meaning. Bind an actual issued context and exact caller scope before recording
loss. Recognized query envelopes precede query-induced closure; malformed envelopes
and foreign scopes cannot invalidate another context. Discovery additionally checks
the outside-publication guard before any private invalidation or cut consumption.
These checks assume inert normalized input, not hostile getters/proxies or a sandbox.

| Owned profile | Observed context loss | Refusal that does not establish context loss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F01 discovery | Explicit false authority, scope, continuity, liveness, notStopped, discoveryAllowed or interpretation facts; native owner fault; explicit retention loss; changed captured permitted metadata or narrowed metadata facets | Unknown/non-Boolean facts, transient transfer/reply/resources, foreign or malformed envelopes, stale/foreign cuts and advisory-only target or advice refusal |
| F04 history inspection and trusted alias resolution | Explicit false grant, retention, liveness, continuity or current-history facts; mismatched actual scoped history basis | Unknown facts, transient transfer/reply, foreign context/scope and malformed query envelopes |
| F06 invocation observation | Explicit false matching policy grant or authority/scope/continuity/liveness/retention facts; actual original invocation/reference/policy binding no longer available | Unknown facts, mismatched caller policy recipient/epoch, malformed/foreign requests, transient transfer/readiness/resources, and missing/forgotten outcome data while actual phase/policy remain available |

Closed delivery never resumes through regrant, equal metadata or restored flags.
Fresh authorized acquisition may establish a new frontier. Discovery drops captured
delivery data/selectors; invocation observation clears delivery references and ends
all its waiters. History marks the owned inspection context nonlive while retaining
its bounded capture until discharge. No closure refunds lifetime issuance, releases
charged context capacity early, changes authored roots/history, cancels a producer
or reverses an already prepared independent operation. Retained delivery/wait records
remain subject to their explicit owner-control, retention and drain gates.

Invocation readiness, wait admission, clock validity, stop and discharge require
exact true facts, not truthy values. Validate owned wait selectors and finite budgets
before query-induced context closure. A denied poll can end its one waiter without
invalidating an otherwise live context; a bound context loss ends every waiter.
An invalid clock ends that wait without claiming elapsed-time progress or producer
completion. Protected control capacity never substitutes for current observation
rights. Write revocation, authoritative outcome retention and observation rights
remain distinct; Applied facts do not become nonapplication when observation closes.

[Read-lifetime evidence](formal/read-invalidation.md) adds three actual-owner
checkers and 29 assertion-killed mutants with passing unmodified baselines. Legacy
release vectors now acquire independent contexts and discharge them, preserving
their original case coverage without assuming revival. Existing conditional solver
laws remain unchanged; these checks do not prove automatic policy-event delivery,
all reader families, actual global/physical accounting, public codecs/Rust,
concurrent/crash refinement or independent assurance. Each bounded call terminates
within its declared reference work limits; arbitrary caller retries and real wait
service still require their separate progress assumptions.

These query rules do not retype an internal accepted-host-current-state argument
as an untrusted caller scope claim. Publication observers deliberately fence on
accepted current context change under §12.3.1. Shared geometry/analysis artifacts
are also not complete recipient-owned frontiers: a recipient refusal does not
itself invalidate a shared layout or reusable parse fact. Their own producer and
recipient-release contracts remain separate, with actual wrapper/lifetime
integration still required where promised. See the profile audit in
formal/read-invalidation.md; no all-reader closure follows from the selected fixes.

### 12.8.4 Selected native current source context owner

The selected native reference connects existing F02 `snapshot-handoff`, current
source capture and source range/line queries to the actual invocation owner. Its
current route accepts exactly `capture-current` with `data: ['source']`;
§12.8.6 additionally accepts exact retained source-context selection. Unsupported
data/selection products refuse, not a narrower success. Annotation/combined
contexts use §12.8.5; broader historical and version-set native integration under
§§12.8–12.10 remains required.

Keep one privately bound pool per actual owner/domain. Validate and capture its
finite profile, then reserve the declared fixed envelope against both pool limits
and actual remaining parent headroom before capture. The profile separately bounds
context/hold counts, spent issuance, root/capture/scope/request/reply/selector bytes,
copy nodes/depth and the existing source-product profile. Reserve input/copy
workspace independently of retained-context count, including zero; the actual
parent retains its separate declared root frames. No numeric default or
new public pool/pin/renew verb is selected. Logical reservation is not physical
allocation or complete host/global accounting.

Acquisition derives its immutable source/revision only from the actual current
owner root and exactly one live document. No caller-supplied root or candidate
can redirect it. Recheck scope, source validity, capacities and complete selector/
reply envelopes before installing one opaque context. Refusal installs nothing
and spends no context identity. Later source publication alone neither refreshes
nor invalidates the capture; new acquisition sees the newer revision.

Native handle identity and caller scope binding precede accepted loss. Reject
unknown fields, accessors, wrong operations, invalid byte/line boundaries, copied
selectors and foreign scopes without poisoning another context. Matching scope
strings are not grants: current policy/profile/continuity eligibility is supplied
through separately accepted bound release facts. The host must report loss; a
different caller claim is not a policy-change notification. Actual host identity,
policy/profile interpretation and complete loss notification remain premises.

For a valid bound query, accepted exact-false authority/scope/continuity/liveness/
retention/source-read observations, actual owner fault or actual owner disposal
close delivery without resurrection. Unknown facts/truthy substitutes deny without
establishing loss; ordinary resources/reply/transfer refusal alone does not close
the context. Disposal also fences new holds from the actual root, independently
of stale supplied grants. The selected reference records private invalidation on
valid observation, not through a newly claimed eager bulk lifecycle event.

Existing F19 owner stop remains protected and independent of ordinary read grants.
Internal holds retain the actual stopped snapshot until separate protected owner/
retention/drain discharge. Retire no held row, refund no other owner, and never
refund spent issuance. Retiring a row does not refund the fixed pool reservation;
empty-pool retirement releases it once, without reopening the same issuer to reset
its lifetime. This does not recall previously transferred data or prove erasure.

disposal with two mutants and three selected hidden-I/O cases. A separate finite
oracle checks 4,681 native traces/18,056 edges up to four steps, with three

The selected native path extends current F02 capture to annotations or combined

reuse equivalent live selectors on retries. Never expose raw indices or turn a

Bound request shape, caller scope, selector kind/identity and source coordinates
before observing accepted loss. Relevant exact-false loss, actual disposal or

context continues to require both admitted classes. Ordinary newer publications

### 12.8.6 Retained source context acquisition

The selected native source pool additionally accepts §12.8's retained selection
when its reference is an original available source context in that actual owner,
