tag. The exact stored source/revision and immutable source-product profile supply
the new owned capture. Never substitute the current root, use a revision number
as lookup authority, or launch filesystem/provider discovery to recover a miss.
This profile supports existing retained source projections, not arbitrary
historical publications, annotation/combined projections or coherent version sets.

Require the same exact captured caller scope and current eligibility for the
original retained context before new admission. Validate recognized data/selection
and scope binding before observing accepted loss; foreign or malformed requests
cannot poison another context. Accepted exact-false authority, scope, continuity,
liveness, retained availability or source-read loss is absorbing even when new
context capacity or lifetime issuance is exhausted. Unknown facts and transient
resource/refusal conditions withhold acquisition without establishing loss.
Actual disposal and owner faults fence reacquisition under stale positive facts.
All preparation gates remain independently required.

Prepare a bounded immutable copy under the existing context/copy/source/reply
limits. New context count, original identity, complete request envelope and
nonrefunding issuance remain separately checked. A successful acquisition issues
a distinct context and consumes one slot/issuance unit in the same reserved pool.
It does not add a hold on the original context or share that original context's
future stop state. Each issued context independently requires current release
authority, actual document liveness and protected retirement. Retiring the original
does not erase a copy still owned by the new context. These logical reservations
do not prove physical allocation or global resource bounds.

Existing source queries and all three F05 variants consume the new context's exact
retained cut. F11/F12 still validate original managed result ownership and current
use at preparation and service; read retention does not make stale edits safe.
[Retained source evidence](formal/native-retained-source.md) records ten controls,
eighteen loss/twelve unknown/four transient cases, nine exact boundaries, two actual
lifecycle cases/eighteen protected denials, thirteen mutations and twelve consumer
cases/seven mutations. A selected post-import substrate probe detects three hidden
read/rename/process calls with no partial context installation. IF-02/05 and
INS-01/03/05/06/08/13 separate reacquisition, evaluation, release, current use and
protected discharge; no authored publication, UI policy, public verb, transport or
numeric default is introduced. Broader historical/combined/version-set/public,
host/measurement/physical/global/concurrent/crash and independent gates remain.

### 12.8.7 Retained annotation and combined projection acquisition

F02 retained selection additionally resolves an original available context in the
actual annotation/combined owner, domain and pool. Copy its exact permitted source,
annotation and facet projection; do not consult the newer root for content or
reconstruct absent fields. The selected data must be a nonempty unique subset of
the retained data classes. Annotation-only, source-only and combined copies remain
distinct admitted projections, not a new execution mode or public verb.

Validate recognized request/data/selection, original identity and exact captured
caller scope before observing accepted loss. Require current whole-projection
authority for the original context before considering new admission, including
both classes when the original is combined. Relevant loss is absorbing despite
new capacity/issuance exhaustion; unknown facts and transient resource refusal
withhold without establishing loss. New preparation reservation is an independent
exact-true gate. Actual owner fault/disposal fences delivery and reacquisition.

Narrowing removes excluded raw values and their private query projection. A
source-only copy retains no annotations, rejects F03 before observing out-of-class
loss and requires only its admitted source class on subsequent release. An
annotation-only copy retains no source and needs no later source grant. Narrowed
copies cannot widen by reacquisition; a fresh broader authorized capture needs
actual available data. Scope/interpretation and lifecycle authority remain required
for every copy. No class grant substitutes for another.

Stage bounded owned value/scope/projection, reply, new context and complete registry
candidates before installing anything. Fresh selectors bind the new context;
original record/continuation references cannot cross it. Refusal installs/spends
nothing. A staging surprise fences the owner without a partial live registry.
Consume one context/selector/issuance unit on success within the existing parent
reservation; preserve nonrefunding issuance and separate protected hold/context/
pool discharge. Original retirement does not erase an independently owned copy.
Logical envelopes do not establish physical/global allocation bounds.

The retained source cut supports F02/F05 and existing dependent F11/F12 current-use
checks after newer publication and original retirement. Retained bytes do not make
stale writes valid. [Retained projection evidence](formal/native-retained-annotation.md)
records fifteen controls, 27 loss/eighteen unknown/four transient cases, twelve
exact boundaries, two actual lifecycle cases/eighteen protected denials, 21
mutations, three old-cut search variants and twelve consumer cases/seven mutations.
The selected 143-callable post-import probe detects three hidden read/rename/process
calls during staging with owner fencing and unchanged original registry/charges.
IF-02/03/05, PATH-02/07 and INS-01/03/05/06/08/13 distinguish acquisition, query,
evaluation, current use and protected discharge without authored publication,
network I/O, UI policy, sensitive metric labels or numeric defaults. Arbitrary
historical publication lookup, coherent version sets, async/full public products
and host/measurement/physical/global/concurrent/crash/independent gates remain.

### 12.8.8 Retained class isolation in reference projections

Single-document and version-set member candidates retain only their admitted
classes. Annotation-only candidates retain no source bytes, source revision or
source-product profile; source-only candidates retain no annotation projection.
Installation preserves that separation. A delivery gate that denies source access
does not justify retaining unrequested source inside an annotation-only candidate.

The abstract reference's declared retention units count source bytes only when
source is admitted, plus projected annotation rows only when annotations are
admitted. Its source-byte ceiling likewise applies to the admitted source class,
not annotation-only retention. Independently declared root/preparation/input-copy
bounds still apply where their owning contracts require them; this is neither
unbounded preparation permission nor physical/global accounting.

The corrected reference has three single-document class cases, one mixed-class
version set and three assertion-killed regressions. Existing registry and coherent
set lifetime banks retain their scoped horizons. [Read-context evidence](formal/read-contexts.md)
records the correction; native one-cut version-set acquisition/ownership remains
an integration gate, not a consequence of this abstract projection check.
IF-02/03/PATH-02 and INS-01/03/08 keep class admission, content release and retained
obligations distinct; no raw content/revision is added to diagnostic labels.

### 12.8.9 Native current coherent version sets

The selected `read-version-set/1` current-capture profile resolves all explicit
participants from one actual immutable published owner root. It does not join
independently captured current documents. Preparation retains only each member's
admitted source/annotation classes and permitted facets. Actual annotation
identities remain private; recipient paging follows attested source order rather
than sorting by those identities.

Installation stages a complete parent, every member alias, private registry and
reply before consuming the original prepared cut once. Ordinary refusal consumes
nothing. Parent/member selectors control the whole set; record and continuation
selectors do not. Foreign, copied, wrong-kind and malformed requests cannot mark
an unrelated set invalid. A recognized current loss in any required member fences
the whole parent before capacity refusal. Unknown facts withhold without proving
loss. Later ordinary publication neither refreshes nor alone invalidates the cut.

Bounded source range/line and annotation enumeration/inspection/location products
use the same all-required-member gate. Native aliases wrap private registry
identities, remain scoped to their parent/member and cannot change meaning when
reused. Complete replies and pending selector state must fit before publication.
Staging surprises fence the owner; they do not publish partial native registries.

The existing synchronous F05 service has a closed first-party version-set member
issuer alongside its source and combined issuers. Only source-admitted members
can supply search values. Each result holds the entire coherent parent. Stable
recipient scope is distinct from current host authority: the private accepted-facts
port carries the existing complete per-member currentness frame. Retained search
release and dependent F11/F12 preparation/publication revalidate it. Neither a
member token nor a retained result grants source, annotation or edit authority.

Context slots, aliases, holds and spent issuance remain distinct. Preparation
reserves workspace against the actual parent root bound, even when a smaller local
input ceiling will refuse that root. Installation reserves complete candidate,
registry, metadata, reply and selector stages. Discharge requires exact protected
facts; a held parent cannot retire, spent identities are never refunded, and pool
retirement releases only its own declared charge. These are logical envelopes,
not measured heap/global resource guarantees.

[Native version-set evidence](formal/native-version-set.md) covers selected
preparation, handoff, installation, queries, search, dependent consumers, actual
disposal/fault and staged-fault/substrate cases. Arbitrary historical-cut selection,
complete public codecs/events, asynchronous lifetimes, actual host/policy truth,
concurrent/crash refinement, measurements and independent assurance remain gates.
IF-02/03/05 and PATH-02/07 reuse local engine ownership; no transport, filesystem
mechanism or UI behavior is added. Full frozen verification is required.

### 12.8.10 Retained coherent version set projections

Existing F02 `read-version-set/1` retained selection can resolve an original
available parent in the same actual engine owner, domain and pool. The scoped
parent reference selects its owned coherent projection, not the current root,
an arbitrary publication label, independent member selectors or a joined set.
The request retains §12.10's exact fields and explicit ordered participants.
Each requested member must exist in the original projection with the same
document incarnation and a nonempty subset of its admitted data classes.
Duplicate owners, unknown members/classes and widening refuse without observing
loss against an unrelated parent. A copied, foreign, record, cursor or borrowed
member selector is not a retained-parent reference in this profile.

The original whole parent must pass current authority, continuity, dependency,
lifecycle and retained-availability validation before new capacity admission,
including when the request names fewer members or classes. Observed original
loss cannot be hidden by narrowing or a full pool; an invalidated parent cannot
revive through copying. Unknown/transient facts withhold without establishing
loss. Current host truth remains an independently accepted premise.

The fresh context owns a bounded copy of the selected old projection. Preserve
request order and exact old source revisions/bytes, annotation facets and common
cut provenance. Remove excluded members and classes, including private annotation
identity/facet inventory for source-only members and source-product revision/profile for
annotation-only members. Subsequent release requires all members/classes of the
new explicit context, not removed peers. A copy chain cannot restore excluded
data. No provider or file read repairs missing historical values.

Stage the complete new registry, scope, parent/member aliases and reply before
publishing any of them. Record/cursor aliases are fresh and cannot cross copies.
The new copy borrows no hold or stop state from the original, whose later protected
retirement cannot erase the copy. Groups, aliases and spent issuance consume the
existing pool reservation independently. Bound new private registry/alias frames
even when issued-ID width grows; do not assume their size equals an earlier frame.
Ordinary refusal installs/spends nothing. Protected cleanup releases only actual
owned obligations and never refunds spent identities or another owner's charge.

The same F02/F03/F05 and dependent F11/F12 current-use paths apply to the copy.
Search holds retain its whole parent until protected discharge. Actual disposal
or owner fault fences retained delivery and use, including when search release
is the first observer. Staging fault checks preserve the original registry and
root without partial aliases; they do not establish crash/concurrent refinement.

[Retained version-set evidence](formal/native-retained-version-set.md) records
selected controls, exact boundaries, semantic mutations, lifecycle, consumer and
substrate checks. IF-02/03/05 and PATH-02/07 remain local engine paths;
INS-01/03/05/06/08/13 distinguish acquisition, validation, staging, handoff,
dependent use and protected release without sensitive labels. No new public verb,
execution mode, transport or numeric production default is introduced. Arbitrary
historical-root lookup, complete public codecs/events, asynchronous lifetimes,
host truth, physical/global accounting, measurements and independent assurance
remain gates. Full frozen verification is required.

### 12.9 Selector registry, retirement and retained obligations

The base native registry distinguishes context, record and continuation selectors.
They bind their issuer/authority session, exact owner incarnation, retained
projection and recipient/destination/purpose context. Record selectors additionally
resolve one exact annotation incarnation; continuations bind the query/limit and
next position within the permitted ordered domain. Wrong-kind, cross-context,
foreign-recipient, unknown and retired selectors cannot be reinterpreted as one
another. No selector is a bearer grant or public global sequence number. Trusted
host identity and actual current grants are established independently.

The state vocabulary is `prepared`, `active`, `invalidated`, `retired`.
Prepared candidates are internal and own their declared reservations. Successful
installation alone makes a context active. Relevant policy/continuity change,
owner disposal, explicit close or permitted eviction invalidates further delivery
and all dependent selectors. There is no transition from invalidated/retired to
active for the same identity. Reauthorization/resynchronization creates a fresh
context; it cannot erase an earlier visibility gap. A new source publication alone
does not rewrite the captured snapshot or require invalidation. The base context
does not promise post-disposal mediated access; any separate supported retained
profile must declare its lifecycle and current-release evidence explicitly.

F19 `stop-observation` uses the read-context product `contract`, `operation`,
`context`. Validate the actual host-established observation owner and issuer,
not permission from token possession. A recipient can close its own context even
after its content grant is revoked; protected control admission must remain usable
when ordinary read capacity is full. A successful `stopped` product establishes
no further handoff through that context after the close decision. Already
transferred bytes remain disclosed; close neither retracts them nor proves workers
or external effects quiescent. Unknown/foreign/already-retired selectors use
common unavailable without resurrecting entries. Repetition has idempotent state
effect, not a promise to retain a distinguishable public close receipt forever.

Stop/eviction invalidate all aliases of that context. Selector copies are not
independent owners or leases. Internal worker/staging/handoff owners retain their
actual obligations separately. Invalidation cannot refund a still-held root or
erase an effect/history obligation. Retire the context-owned retained row only
when all its required holds have discharged or transferred under a supported
ownership contract; other allocation owners/metadata may remain. Repeated hold
release cannot refund another owner. Dropping a selector, accepting cancellation
or timing out is not evidence of physical reclamation. No public pin/renew verb,
secure-erasure claim or automatic durable migration is introduced.

The base context is bounded and evictable, with no minimum availability lease or
mandatory clock TTL. Owner closure and relevant invalidation need no clock. A
supported timed profile must explicitly bind clock/suspend/expiry semantics;
arbitrary timeout constants are not selected here. Capacity eviction may remove
only eligible read-context availability, never unsaved authored state or another
required retained obligation. Subsequent reads report unavailable, not an empty
snapshot or invisible resumption on a new root.

Bound input/preparation work and prepared reservations, retained contexts and
actual allocation ownership/units, selectors, hold records, page/row/reply bytes
and issuance domain. Reserve all missing record/continuation selectors and reply
capacity before one complete page handoff. Reuse equivalent still-live selectors
for repeated identical pages; never leak a raw next offset or partially install
one page's selectors on refusal. Final registration/issuance and delivery obey
§12.6's current serialized boundary. IDs must remain non-confusable after row
removal: exhaust/refuse before unsafe reuse and use a fresh non-confusable issuer
across authority restarts. Do not require an unbounded tombstone set to compensate
for reusable identities. Actual native/wire encodings, issuer implementation and
restart evidence remain integration gates, not cryptographic guarantees from
opaque syntax alone.

formal/read-contexts.md gives conditional lifecycle/accounting/termination arguments,
registry-to-query reference composition, bounded action exploration and sensitivity
controls. The numeric fixture is not a production capacity profile. Host root/
historical lookup truth, complete resource charging, real token constructors,
native ownership/concurrency and all adapters still require implementation evidence.

### 12.10 Coherent multi document version set contexts

F02's existing snapshot-handoff additionally supports the native semantic product
`read-version-set/1` in formal/version-set-contexts.json. It is one bounded coherent
read context spanning explicit documents under one local authority, not a new
family, transaction mode, distributed coordinator or per-document engine. The
single-document `read-context/1` product remains supported. Neither product can
join independently captured contexts by relabeling them as one version set.

The exact request fields are `contract`, `operation`, `authority`, `participants`,
`selection`, `profile`. `participants` is a nonempty bounded ordered vector of
unique logical owners, each containing exactly `document` and `data`. Document
references carry the authority/document/incarnation; every member must belong to
the declared authority. Repeated logical owners, including conflicting incarnations,
refuse rather than multiply retention or silently merge different requested scopes.
Each `data` is a nonempty set of source and/or annotation classes under §12.8.
There is no path, focus, implicit workspace membership or arbitrary discovery query
in this product. Selection is exactly `capture-current` or `retained(reference)`
with the meanings in §12.8. Unknown fields/variants/versions do not execute.

Capture one immutable coherent published authority root or supported equivalent
version-set witness, then resolve all declared document incarnations, source and
annotation projections from that cut. Preparation may traverse that same retained
root outside publication; it must not recapture current state independently per
document. Current capture means the owner capture point, not latest at eventual
handoff. Retained selection resolves exactly the named available cut, never a mix
of historical and current members or a latest fallback. Missing/incomparable common
cut evidence refuses. Actual root lookup and ownership remain implementation gates;
equal per-document bytes/revisions or a claimed common label alone are not proof.

Versions remain domain-scoped per document incarnation. They need not be equal,
advance together or equal the authority publication generation. The common-cut
witness stays internal or recipient-scoped; no raw global ordinal, hidden member,
unrelated change count or world inventory is added to the result. The guarantee is
consistency for the explicit named participants, not complete semantic discovery,
all workspace members, absence of newly matching references, a remote snapshot or
cross-authority atomicity. Those guarantees require their separate explicit scope
and evidence contracts. Explicit targets acquire only actual dependencies; they
do not gain accidental focus/workspace-membership dependencies.

Prepare immutable owned per-member projections with their actual data grants,
incarnations and relevant context stamps. Validate shared actual recipient,
destination/purpose and interpretation plus each member's accepted current policy,
lifecycle, continuity and required dependency evidence. Policy/version domains may
be distinct; the complete accepted access context must cover every member without
substituting one member's grant for another. Source and annotation grants remain
independent even within a coherent set.

Reserve preparation work, parent/member registry metadata/selectors, complete
aggregate retention, holds and the whole reply envelope before handoff. Final
current validation, parent/member installation and bounded owned envelope transfer
form one local serialized decision under §12.6. If any required member, lookup,
interpretation, grant, stop condition or capacity fails, expose/install none of the
set; no successful subset or public failing-member index is returned. A private
staging loop is permitted, not a series of publicly committed child acquisitions.
Uncommitted private IDs have no public validity; a real allocator must not recycle
any identity already issued outside that private candidate. No arbitrary callback,
host I/O or provider consultation belongs inside this decision.

Success contains `context` and ordered `participants`. Each participant result
contains exactly `document`, `snapshot` and admitted `data`, in request order.
`context` is the opaque owning version-set selector; `snapshot` is that document's
opaque member selector for existing F02/F03 queries. All named members are required.
Unavailable, denied, stale, missing and conflicting causes use the common base
unavailable product without a partial roster or failing identity; richer internal
causes retain independent diagnostic authorization. Capacity/timing interference
is limited by the declared profile, not claimed perfectly noninterfering.

A member selector is a facet of the owning context, not an independently leased
child. Before every source/annotation page/record/location handoff, validate current
access, availability, incarnation, actual dependency/continuity and parent validity
for all required members, then the requested member's fields/query. A member cannot
bypass that parent gate through a lower-level source or annotation entry point.
Any internal parent-validation result is produced and consumed in that same local
decision, not accepted from a public request or cached across policy updates.
Record and continuation selectors remain bound to their exact member as well as
the parent; equal local annotation IDs across documents do not identify one record.
Ordinary newer publications do not rewrite an available captured set.

Relevant loss of any required member's access/incarnation/continuity/dependency or
retained availability invalidates the owning context for further delivery, not a
smaller result. Explicit F19 stop using the parent or one member context closes
that entire owning context after actual owner validation; the lower-level member
close path cannot detach one required facet behind the parent. Merely dropping a
borrowed selector does not close the set. Stop remains protected after content
revocation and ordinary-capacity saturation. Already disclosed bytes are not
recalled. Regrant/subset recovery requires a fresh explicit authorized acquisition
and a new context identity; it cannot revive the old context or hide a gap.

Retire all dependent delivery selectors together. Release eligible unheld member
rows while retaining each actual internal hold/root charge and bounded parent
ownership metadata. The last required hold discharge permits final parent
retirement; neither invalidation nor repeated release refunds another owner or
proves physical erasure. Parent metadata, member contexts and complete selector/
reply issuance all consume bounded profile resources. The base lifetime/eviction,
non-reuse and issuer rules of §12.9 continue unchanged; no public pin/renew API,
mandatory TTL, durable ledger or network service is added.

Using the returned source contexts for F11 still requires every relevant current
read/write revision, grant, scope, history and companion at publication. A changed
read-only dependency can refuse an edit to an otherwise unchanged write member.
Read coherence does not grant mutation authority or make a stale proposal safe.
formal/version-set-contexts.md records conditional arguments, actual source/
annotation reference composition, a mixed-read witness and bounded sensitivity
checks. Real atomic root acquisition, policy/history truth, native token/ownership
and complete resource/adapter refinement remain evidence gates.

## 13 Authored annotations and attachment evidence

Requirements §3.8 governs this slice, with §§5.8/15.6 and IF-03/08/12,
PATH-03/04, INV-05/06/08/09. A required comment is bounded plain text associated
with a document-wide, point or range target. It is authored state, not text
inserted into the source, a transient parser diagnostic or a UI decoration.

### 13.1 State and operation contracts

Keep annotation identity/incarnation, document association, authored body/content
version, target/reattachment generation, mapping evidence and presentation state
distinct from source revision. Claimed author/provenance is data; host-verified
identity and permissions are separate. Producer namespaces prevent collisions,
not unauthorized reading or writing. Identity/deletion evidence must support
bounded history without confusing a recreated record with an old one.

| Operation family | Preconditions and transition |
|---|---|
| Create comment | Current document incarnation/source target context, supported point/range/document target, bounded body and current annotation-create authority; atomically introduce the record and its attachment evidence |
| Update authored content | Current annotation identity/content version, allowed fields/kind and current update authority; change authored version without pretending source text changed |
| Delete authored record | Current annotation identity/version and deletion authority; preserve any required deletion/history/effect evidence under its bounded contract |
| Explicit reattachment | Current annotation and source context plus supported mapping/target evidence and current rights; update attachment intentionally, not through fuzzy quote identity inference |
| Read, enumerate or export | Current recipient projection under §12; include identity/body/target/provenance/count/history detail only where permitted |
| Source-driven attachment mapping | The validated source change and applicable attachment profile determine mapping evidence in the same coherent publication; do not author or delete comment bodies |

Read-only source can permit comments when the declared policy grants annotation
mutation separately. Source access alone never grants private annotation access.
All mutation families enter the ordinary version/current-authority/budget path;
a compound source-plus-annotation operation names its real atomic participants.
Independent generations cannot be presented as one coherent result if they were
not read/published under the claimed version-set contract.

### 13.2 Attachment and history boundaries

An attachment identifies document incarnation, source revision, typed point/range
or document scope, required affinities and profile-defined mapping/deletion
disposition. Location evidence distinguishes an intact/mapped location, affected
or stale context, and detached/unresolved targets; it is not proof of semantic
applicability or the author's review status. Exact state names/profile fields
remain D04/D19 refinements under adopted §4.3.1, rather than equating all of
these dimensions. Nonempty content ranges use its boundary-exclusive insertion
default; complete original-target removal detaches without deleting authored body
state. Collapsed ranges use one point affinity, not independent opposed endpoints.

Deleting target text must not delete its authored annotation body or silently
attach it to unrelated neighboring text. Missing mapping history, external reload
or ambiguous quote/context matching yields explicit affected/detached/unavailable
evidence under the profile, not automatic reattachment. Quotes may support a
suggestion; applying it is an explicitly validated action. Storage chunking and
mixed-language regions do not change document ownership or these mapping laws.

Source undo preserves later authored comments and explicit reattachments unless
they are actual eligible participants of the reversed group. Automatic mapping
does not enter annotation-content history. Any restoration through source undo
must use current validated mapping evidence, not restore a stale annotation body
or overwrite a later explicit target choice.

### 13.3 Persistence and presentation

Unsaved annotations are retained authored state during lifecycle/disposal. Source
copy/export does not automatically copy annotations, provenance or permissions.
Document identity—not whichever path/view is current—governs association across
view closure/rebind. Cross-process reattachment needs the host's stable identity
and source-version evidence; a session handle does not provide it.

Source and annotation saves capture separate snapshots and have separate modified
state, attempts and receipts. Source-driven attachment updates can require
annotation persistence even when bodies did not change. Source-save success never
clears annotation changes; joint persistence is claimed only with an actual host
capability. D20 defines the concrete reference-host format; no sidecar/database
or source-markup representation is mandatory.

Both adapters provide basic discoverable/accessible indication and comment text
access through the same authorized projection. Hidden bodies must not leak through
gutter counts, quotes, navigation or accessibility. Bodies/metadata are untrusted
data: no instruction execution, implicit URL fetch, rich-body evaluation or remote
exfiltration. Threading, mentions and approval/assignment workflows stay excluded.

### 13.4 Conformance and observations

Required independent scenarios include conflicting content versions, read-only
source with permitted comments, target deletion, later reattachment followed by
source undo, atomic source/comment publication, deleted-ID reuse, hidden fields/
counts/warm caches, rebind/reload and independent source/annotation save failures.
PS-HI/BR/DI/RB/EC provide restricted preservation/coherence evidence; they do not
define the complete attachment/profile/serialization implementation.

INS-02/03/06/07 observe admission/mapping/reversal/release/persistence separately;
INS-10/11 consume authorized presentation. Bound bodies, counts, mappings, versions
and history together. Do not log bodies/quoted targets or use annotation/author
IDs as metric labels. STRIDE/LINDDUN include forged attribution, stale targeting,
content loss, private existence/linkage, body/metadata floods and embedded actions.
D04, D12, D19 and D20 remain the material profile/field decisions.

### 13.5 Managed comment record and mutation products

The base managed comment is one authored record associated with one document
incarnation, not a parser node or a source-code region owner. Its logical fields
are annotation identity/incarnation, document association, plain valid UTF-8 body,
authored content version, authored target descriptor/generation and distinct
mapping/applicability evidence. Any supported authored metadata belongs to the
content/version and projection contract; declared provenance is data, while
host-verified actor/grant attribution is separately established. Public field
names/encodings and optional metadata keys are not selected by these products.

The target is a tagged document/point/content-range value under §13.2/§4.3.1,
with the exact source context, required affinity and mapping profile. Source-driven
mapping changes evidence, not authored body/content or explicit-target generations.
Body and target state may be independently current; no single source revision
stands in for all annotation freshness. An empty body is a valid authored value,
not deletion or absence. Unsupported body formats cannot silently become executable
markup or remote references. No threaded workflow or rich-body runtime is added.

| Mutation | Required captured inputs and frame |
|---|---|
| Create | Explicit document/source target context, accepted target/body/metadata profile, identity issuance and current create authority; no reuse of a retired incarnation; introduce record plus required attachment/history state atomically |
| Update content | Annotation identity/incarnation and expected authored content version, complete supported content-field intent and current update authority; preserve current target/evidence unless they are explicitly declared participants/dependencies |
| Reattach | Annotation identity/incarnation and expected authored target generation, exact new source target/context and current rights; preserve the current body/content version unless explicitly changed; no fuzzy quote-based authoring |
| Delete | Annotation identity/incarnation and expected current authored content and target generations, current deletion authority and complete retained-history/lifecycle disposition; delete cannot overwrite an intervening authored edit |

These version requirements cover the fields used or destroyed; actual permissions,
mapping, history and compound changes can introduce additional declared dependencies.
Do not restore another field from an old prepared record merely because its version
was not required by this mutation. Revalidate and stage actual history/attachment/
source participants under the shared coordinator. Equal-field requests still
validate authority/dependencies/bounds and use the complete §6.4 identity predicate;
text equality alone cannot elide a required companion change. Deletion retains
required history/evidence rather than claiming physical erasure or unlimited storage.

The [Web Annotation model](https://www.w3.org/TR/annotation-model/) supplies precedent
for separating annotation/body/target and contextual selectors. It does not select
Vellum's persistence format or coordinate units. Its character-position selectors
are not canonical UTF-8 byte ranges; interchange needs an explicit conversion and
source-state association. Quotes may help propose recovery, never silently authorize
reattachment. Section 29.4 selects reference-host JSON; concrete encoding fields,
location/binding and migration remain D20 technical/integration work.
formal/annotation-records.md records authored-field reference evidence and its limits.

### 13.6 Version 1 annotation authoring requests and results

F13 retains four closed variants. The semantic contract label is
`annotation-authoring/1`; formal/annotation-operations.json records its exact
product fields. These are native semantic products, not JSON commands, assigned
transport IDs or selected Rust memory layouts. Typed and dynamic entry points
resolve the same captured descriptor and §26.5 preparation. Unknown executable
variants, fields and versions do not run.

Every request contains `contract`, `operation`, `invocation`, `document`, `profile`
and `dependencies`. The invocation binds complete intent under §6.5, not a grant
or source revision. `document` is an explicit live authority/document/incarnation
reference; no focus default exists. `profile` resolves a supported finite execution
profile. `dependencies` is a bounded vector of typed `(domain, identity, generation)`
conditions in addition to mandatory engine-derived dependencies, never a replacement
for them. Equivalent duplicate conditions are idempotent; conflicting generations
for one identity reject regardless of ordering. Missing, ambiguous or stale current
evidence cannot satisfy the union. Bound input and complete merged cardinality.
Authority, selected interpretation, fresh identity/version issuance and complete
companion eligibility come from engine/host context, not caller-authored flags.
Resolve only a currently live document incarnation. A fresh create identity is
bound into owned preparation; changing it creates a different candidate, not a
replacement behind an existing selector. Cancellation cannot recycle an issued
incarnation into a different meaning.

| Variant | Additional exact fields | Required effect |
|---|---|---|
| `create` | `body`, `target` | Engine-owned fresh annotation identity allocation; introduce body, authored target and required placement/history atomically. No caller-supplied live identity or initial version counters |
| `update-body` | `annotation`, `expectedContent`, `body` | Compare the current authored content version and update only that authored field/version plus actual declared companions; preserve the current target/generation, not an old prepared copy |
| `reattach` | `annotation`, `expectedTarget`, `target` | Compare the current authored target generation and exact new source context; preserve current body/content version unless explicitly included in a compound plan |
| `delete` | `annotation`, `expectedContent`, `expectedTarget` | Validate both authored versions and retained-history/lifecycle disposition before removing the record; no deletion by absence or empty body |

`LiveAnnotationRef` includes its owner document reference, annotation ID and
annotation incarnation. It must agree with the request document and actual current
registry entry. A stored namespace/value/incarnation tuple is not this live ref.
Versions are typed engine versions; JSON decimal strings in §29.4.1 are not cast
into current admission tokens. `ScalarText` is bounded valid UTF-8 scalar text,
including empty text. Version 1 has no arbitrary metadata/policy fields.

`LiveSourceTarget` is a closed document/point/nonempty-content-range sum over an
exact live source reference: authority, document incarnation and source revision.
Point has a canonical byte offset and explicit before/after affinity; range has
nonempty half-open byte endpoints with §4.3.1 behavior. Target resolution must
validate owner, bounds, scalar boundaries and relevant profile/mapping context.
Its actual source must be current for create/reattach; stale targets are not
clamped or rebased. A body-only update does not accidentally depend on source
revision, geometry, target freshness or source-write permission. Actual policy,
history or explicit read dependencies may legitimately require more conditions.

After a confirmed local decision the terminal factual result is exactly one of
`applied`, `unchanged`, or `not-published`. Admission/pending execution, lost status
or an unestablished decision remains explicit under §§6.5/17/23; it cannot be
converted to not-published merely because a terminal result is unavailable.
Applied identifies the one coherent publication and relevant resulting live or
removed/retained-absent annotation/version facts, not final identity retirement.
Section 13.6.4 defines their bounded decision receipt and protected release.
Unchanged requires §6.4 complete semantic
identity after all current checks and keeps publication/history/annotation-set
versions unchanged. Equal body or target fields do not establish that identity.
Not-published confirms no authoritative local publication for this decision;
rejection, stop, unavailable proof and resource pressure use §23.1.1's protected
explanation layer. Do not expose internal state, raw causes, bodies, set counters
or protected identities merely because the evaluator knows them. Current release
still governs replies and later status lookup. Later notification/diagnostic failure
cannot turn an applied fact into not-published; physical save outcomes are separate.

Maintain one non-confusable annotation snapshot generation per document incarnation
for record membership, authored data and persisted placement changes. Any such
change advances it within the shared publication; an unchanged request does not.
Source revision remains separate, including when a source change alters no record
projection. Body/reattachment commands use their actual field preconditions, not an
unnecessary expected whole-set generation. Full-snapshot activation needs the set
dependency because it can otherwise overwrite unrelated concurrent comments.
Version exhaustion refuses a real transition; complete no-op validation need not
issue unused new versions. Retained charges/obligations are not cleared by refusal.

formal/annotation-operations.md records first-admission reference evidence. Section
13.6.1 separately composes native body/reattachment and all declared live target
forms with actual compound/history/shared invocation publication. Create/delete
registry issuance and decoded create-delete gateway (normalized native composition
is in §13.6.2; retained compound membership evidence is in §13.9.1), general retained mapping, full gateway/
events and actual physical/native/host refinement remain obligations; neither slice
is the complete annotation implementation.

### 13.6.1 Owned native body and reattachment publication

The normalized F13 field bridge composes update-body/reattach with actual owned
compound/history publication and the shared invocation ledger. LiveSourceTarget
binds exactly document, sourceRevision and the existing typed target sum. Preserve
explicit point position/content profile and affinity; document and nonempty range
forms retain §13.9 semantics. Reject unknown forms, invalid scalar boundaries,
stale source and wrong owner; do not clamp, infer focus or replace point meaning.
This is native semantic binding, not a public wire/Rust encoding or point-save policy.

Prepare one owned copied/frozen request/limit/profile/recipient/mandatory-dependency
descriptor with its actual opaque engine owner. At execution require that same
owner/recipient/profile, current finite limits, live unique document/annotation,
relevant field versions, annotation-write rights and complete current companions.
Union required and extra dependencies under §5; revalidate the original mandatory
set without expansion or narrowing. Matching retries retain original capsule identity
and bounded complete semantic data, not equal-looking handles or re-prepared work.

Body update preserves the current target/placement and has no incidental source
revision/read/write/target-freshness or whole-set precondition. Reattachment preserves
the current body and requires its exact original source target plus current target
generation. Compatible independent field changes and unrelated document work survive;
required source changes refuse reattachment rather than silently remap it. Source
read-only state does not prohibit independently authorized comments. All resulting
roots/descriptors remain private engine data, not reply disclosure grants.

Publish through the actual compound helper with source/view frames and authored
record history, then the existing root/terminal-fact boundary. Bound root, documents,
records, current context/dependency union, UTF-8 body, request and complete plan;
producer reservations remain real host obligations, not physical proofs. No-op
requires complete semantic identity, including placement; an explicit reattachment
may repair detached placement even with equal authored target fields. Assign fresh
changed versions/history only for actual transitions. Capacity/overflow refuses the
whole candidate. Native F14 reverses supported current body/target journals with
fresh versions, not historical source/view state or external effects.

[Native annotation field evidence](formal/annotation-editing.md) contains 1,280
admission/1,280 publication/640 release combinations, 3,600 traces/21,600 edges, 118 target cases,
sixteen controls/seventeen mutants and conditional ownership/frame/halting arguments.
Separate §§13.6.2/13.9.1 supply native create/delete and retained membership

physical/concurrent/native/production and independent refinement remain gates.
Existing PATH-01/03/04 and INS-01/02/03/06/07/09/12/13 distinguish native capture,
replay, actual disposition/history, current release and held work without private
content/identity/coordinate labels. No new family, public variant or component is added.

### 13.6.2 Owned native creation and deletion publication

Native F13 create/delete use the same owned annotation preparation, editing adapter
and shared invocation kind as body/reattachment. Public create has no caller-chosen
live ID. The trusted host supplies an already-issued current private allocation
bound to the original invocation/document. Preparation copies that allocation,
request, required dependency set and explicit lifecycle limits. Publication rechecks
the same owner/recipient/profile, dependencies, allocation and limits; it must not
substitute a different valid identity or recreate a newer intent. Construct the
private whole-plan allocation manifest only from that retained native request.
This establishes local binding, not actual issuer/reservation truth or release.

Create validates the current source revision and existing document/range/explicit
point target algebra, body scalar/byte limits and complete inventory. Ordinary
create cannot reuse a tracked incarnation or share a live local ID. A later source
change refuses the prepared create; it does not remap or rebuild it implicitly.
Delete requires exact current annotation incarnation, content version and target
generation. It needs neither source-write authority nor an unrelated target-current
or fresh-allocation flag. If source mapping advances placement while authored
versions remain current, delete retains the current mapped payload, not a prepared
copy. Unknown inventory, changed authored fields and exhausted logical capacity
refuse before any local membership/history installation.

The actual compound evaluator and invocation root/fact boundary publish once or
not at all. Stop/refusal/retry do not create a membership journal; a settled original
invocation remains spent after native F14 undo/redo. Retained membership reversal
uses §13.9.1 fresh floors and current rights. Current disclosure still governs
observation; local success alone does not grant a new record reference or emit an
unimplemented complete event/result product.

[Native membership evidence](formal/annotation-membership-editing.md) contains
512 admission/8,192 publication/256 release cases, 1,440 permutations/8,640 edges,
118 target cases, fourteen controls/fourteen mutants with passing unmodified dynamic
composition, actual shared-ledger F14 round trips and conditional ownership/frame/
halting arguments. This closes normalized native admission/publication, not actual
issuer/reservation/policy truth, legacy/annotation-snapshot activation beyond §11.2.4, full result/event
projection, general target restoration/retirement planning, point storage, decoded
wire routing or actual concurrent/physical/native/production/independent refinement.
PATH-01/03/04/10/12 and INS-01/02/03/06/07/08/12/13 reuse the existing boundaries;
no operation family/variant, component, transport or provider is added.

### 13.6.3 Native annotation outcomes and recipient collection events

Compose native create/body/reattach/delete and owned native F14 with the existing
recipient collection observer after the actual invocation root/fact boundary.
Keep writer terminal facts and independently authorized reader events separate.
Reader visibility is not inferred from authorship or write permission. Annotation-only
projection contains permitted collection references/body/target facets, not source
bytes, raw annotation IDs or authority-wide publication counters.

Filter hidden records before reference allocation and body/target facets before
visible comparison. In the supported projection, an authored change to a hidden
facet causes no visible event or generation progression. Source mapping and a later
body edit project current placement, not the prepared placement. Equal authored
target data can still require an explicit placement-repair event.

Retain an observer-scoped reference across removal and eligible restoration of the
same non-retired logical identity. Intervening creation must not reassign it to a
different record. Restored content/target versions are fresh under §13.9.1; an old
reference is not revival of an old command or grant. An absent retained payload
does not become a live collection row. Event references remain scoped to their
observer and are not automatically native write or F03 query selectors.

Native no-op/refusal and settled retries do not fabricate authored events. Missing
events cannot establish nonpublication. Queue/binding pressure, reader revocation
or failed release does not roll back a committed edit or rewrite its writer fact.
Writer outcome observation can separately be withheld. Gap/resynchronization uses
explicit current visibility preparation and baseline authority; returned projections
cannot mutate authority or later observer state.

[Native observation evidence](formal/annotation-observation.md) composes actual
native producers/adapter/kernel/F14/observer: 112 variant/facet/visibility cases,
224 reversal stages, 1,792 release combinations, eight paired histories, nine
controls/fourteen mutants with passing unmodified dynamic composition and conditional
arguments. This closes selected native current collection-event composition, not
complete F13 live/retired/version result-reference products, event/query selector
integration, real visibility/order/issuer/retention, all lifecycle/effect/event
profiles or actual concurrent/physical/timing/decoder/production/independent refinement.
PATH-01/03/04/12 and INS-01/02/03/06/07/12/13 separate writer publication, current
reader events, retained obligations, gaps and useful completion. No new operation,
