### 13.6.4 Native annotation decision receipts and current result release

Capture exact native result facts with the local root/coarse-fact installation;
do not reconstruct an old result by querying a newer row. The normalized observation
wrapper is annotation-result with one known decision, or the common unavailable
product. Its closed products are:

| Decision | Required facts | Optional fields under both captured and current disclosure |
|---|---|---|
| applied | status, invocation, operation, operation-bound publication reference, native annotation reference and historical membership | contentVersion, targetGeneration |
| unchanged | status, invocation, operation, native annotation reference and historical membership; no new publication reference | contentVersion, targetGeneration |
| not-published | status, invocation and operation only | none |

Applied/unchanged record observation needs explicit identity disclosure at admission
and release. Versions additionally need their respective capabilities. Missing
detailed authority captures no such capability; successful writing is not a read
grant. For existing annotations, exact trusted grants bind original invocation and
native owner/id/incarnation. For create, the selected grant instead binds the
original invocation, document incarnation, complete recipient/context and permitted
result fields before admission; it authorizes only the one annotation allocated by
that invocation. The engine binds this ceiling to its original private allocation,
never a caller-selected identity, another creation or an existing annotation.
No second host authorization handshake or public allocation field is required.
Malformed or substituted admission grants refuse. Copy/freeze the ceiling and
retain complete-context/current coarse-publication/epoch checks at release. The
coarse D05 details flag remains limited to its own envelope; these are separately
scoped native identity/version capabilities. Their five admissible sets form a
bounded distributive lattice under inclusion/intersection/union, not an engine-wide
completeness result.

Reserve the bounded private receipt and largest public frame before admission.
Capture current resulting versions, including independent field changes merged
after preparation; delete reports actual retained absence, not an old prepared row.
Known stop/refusal reports no candidate record facts. Unknown, pending, forgotten
or retired result bindings are unavailable, never guessed nonpublication. Unexpected
or oversized internal receipt vocabulary faults/fences before final installation.
Root, coarse fact, receipt and done phase share the same trusted serialized boundary.

Receipts hold no body/target/source snapshots or authority-wide counters. The
normalizer's publication anchor is the original once-only invocation, not a root
read selector. Native references/versions are historical facts, not grants or a
promise of current liveness; later mutation rechecks current identity/authority/
field versions. Public wire/event/query aliases are not silently converted. Cache
eviction clears both coarse and native results under retention/drain checks while
keeping execution spent. Later history or domain fault never rewrites old valid facts.

At current release, a create grant may name that original invocation/document or
the resulting exact native annotation identity; both must resolve to the same
original allocation. Existing-annotation operations require their exact native
target. Neither a later grant nor replay can add or widen an admission ceiling.
The native Rust port reserves its fixed complete result frame under the original
capture/parent funding; its typed capabilities encode exactly the five admissible
sets. This does not choose public wire/reference aliases or implement F06 policy
ownership. The older frozen reference evidence below retains its exact-target
grant premise; it does not establish the newly selected invocation-scoped create
variant. That variant has separate actual Rust binding/disclosure/lattice tests,
not a new frozen formal or independent certification claim.

[Result evidence](formal/annotation-results.md) contains eight capability candidates,
100 projection/512 release combinations, fourteen controls/eighteen mutants with
passing baseline, conditional preservation/halting arguments and six additional
local SMT conditions. The native normalized result products are no longer missing;
wire/alias/query integration, actual issuer/grant/retention, full retirement/general
mapping/point storage, other result families and actual physical/concurrent/decoder/
production/independent refinement remain. Existing pathways/instrumentation retain
admission, receipt pressure, atomic disposition, current release and useful-completion
cuts without private values in ordinary labels.

### 13.7 Persisted snapshot activation and publication boundaries

Resource reads (F20) acquire a bounded artifact and provider evidence. Decode and
stage it under §29.4.1 outside publication. Neither file presence nor decoded
identity/version/placement fields authorize an edit, reinstate an incarnation,
grant permission or advance a saved baseline. Current source and annotation-set
dependencies captured by staging remain preconditions, not a lease.

Supported activation through the existing loaded-candidate/lifecycle path (F17)
must turn the owned data into a complete declared local state plan: which current
records are preserved, created, replaced, reattached or removed, every relevant
version and history/retention obligation, and the host-established identity
continuity/association facts. A user/provider blob is not itself a list of
executable commands. Fresh authoring uses current engine issuance and F13
preconditions. A genuine restoration must establish registry/version continuity;
it cannot simply replay serialized counters as current tokens. No implicit merge,
migration, reidentification, resurrection or deletion is inferred from the file.

At final publication revalidate exact document incarnation/source, annotation-set,
identity/history, current rights and bounds for the complete plan. Any stale or
unsupported required participant refuses the whole activation unchanged. An empty
snapshot does not waive deletion authority or intervening record versions. An
activation cannot clear obligations by forgetting records missing from the input.
Explicit source-plus-annotation or multiple-object changes use one shared atomic
coordinator/invocation, not a loop of separately published F13 operations. Do not
run parsers, arbitrary callbacks or host I/O inside that boundary.

Save/export (F21) captures an immutable authorized annotation projection with its
source/annotation-set and destination/binding evidence. Dispatch and receipts keep
their effect/attempt lineage under §16; only an admissible receipt can establish
the matching persistence baseline. Newer authored/mapping changes remain dirty.
Save success, loading success, current source save and annotation save are not
interchangeable facts. No new public verb, storage mode, transport or global store
is added here. Actual load-plan/receipt/provider/history integration remains a gate,
not a guarantee supplied by a schema or this operation product inventory.

### 13.8 Version 1 annotation query products and pagination

F03 retains `enumerate`, `inspect` and `target-location` under the semantic contract
label `annotation-query/1`. formal/annotation-queries.json records exact native
product fields, not JSON commands or a frozen Rust ABI. Common fields are
`contract`, `operation`, `document`, `snapshot` and `profile`. The explicit live
document reference includes authority and incarnation. `snapshot` selects a
retained scoped annotation read context, not a caller-authored generation or raw
snapshot grant. `profile` selects supported projection and resource rules.
Unknown fields, versions and executable variants do not run.

The existing read-context acquisition path must bind one coherent source/annotation
snapshot, permitted record domain and field ceiling, host-established recipient,
destination/purpose, profile, relevant policy and continuity. No new acquisition
verb or global annotation service is added. Body, authored versions and placement
in a result come from that context, not independently current reads. The scoped
snapshot selector must not expose a raw annotation-set/publication generation
whose changes reveal hidden-only activity. A read context may remain available
after newer publications, subject to retention and current release checks; it
never claims its historical location is current.

| Variant | Additional exact fields | Successful semantic product |
|---|---|---|
| `enumerate` | `limit`, `continuation` | `snapshot`, bounded ordered `records`, and an optional opaque next `continuation`; no global total or raw offset |
| `inspect` | `annotation` | `snapshot` and one permitted `record` from that context |
| `target-location` | `annotation` | `snapshot`, record `reference` and permitted `location`, including truthful detached/affected status where applicable |

`limit` is a positive row count within the selected profile. `continuation` is
an explicit None value for the first page or a retained opaque scoped selector; there
is no current-focus, current-root or zero-as-unbounded default. `annotation` is a
scoped record selector resolved against that exact context, not a document path,
ordinal or authority claim. A disclosed record contains its scoped `reference`;
permitted content includes the plain `body` and corresponding authored content
version, and permitted location includes target generation, attachment evidence
and exact source/target context as applicable. Withheld dimensions are absent,
not empty bodies or fabricated detached coordinates. A genuinely empty body
remains empty. Quoted source, authorship, timestamps, history and aggregate counts
are not implicit extra fields of this base product. References/versions confer no
mutation rights; adapters must resolve actual live F13 identity and preconditions
through the supported typed preparation path, never cast a read token into a grant.

Order and continuation are derived from the complete permitted domain, not from
global offsets followed by filtering. The profile supplies a stable total order
within the retained context using permitted identities, without exposing hidden
allocation counters. The base enumeration has no caller-defined sort/filter or
cross-context ordinal guarantee. Cursor validity binds the context, document
incarnation, recipient, destination/purpose, profile/projection, continuity and
query interpretation, including limit. Repeating a still-valid selector reads the
same position; it does not consume editing state. There is no cross-context token
equality or indefinite retry/availability guarantee. Return no continuation only
when the end of the complete visible domain is established. An empty page with
no continuation is a successful established visible empty domain, not failure.

Every page/record/location handoff applies §12's current serialized owned-value
release, including its envelope and issued selectors. Relevant policy/continuity
change invalidates the base context; establish a newly authorized context instead
of skipping removed rows or resuming through a visibility gap. Broader grants do
not expand the old ceiling. Absent, hidden, unavailable, stale, expired and
conflicting requests share the base `unavailable` product without record facts;
actual causes remain internal. Permitted detachment is a successful location,
whereas withheld location is unavailable. Revocation cannot recall earlier bytes.

Bound preparation scans/work, captured rows/bytes, individual row/result/envelope
bytes, retained contexts, page size and selector issuance under the resource
profile. A row limit alone is not a scan bound. Stage a complete bounded projected
domain or an equivalent bounded indexed view; if complete coverage/retention or a
whole permitted row cannot be established within the profile, return unavailable,
not truncation presented as completion. The profile must account for allowed
operational interference under §12; no constant-time privacy is implied. Numeric
capacities, actual reference issuance/retention, all location products, host scope
truth, read-context acquisition and native/adaptor implementation remain concrete
gates. formal/annotation-queries.md records conditional arguments and scoped
executable checks, not whole-family or physical-transfer proof.

### 13.9 Owned compound source and annotation plans

F11/F13 preparation may compose declared source and authored annotation intent in
one immutable plan at the existing local coordinator. The design label
`owned-annotation-plan/1` and formal/annotation-compounds.json describe that owned
product, not a public execute-anything verb, JSON command language or callback
list. The common invocation/descriptor binds the entire candidate and complete
required companions under §26.5. Its source components retain exact source and
engine-derived annotation-set dependencies; a newly created/private annotation or
changed attachment cannot be missed merely because the source revision is equal.
These private dependencies do not require granting the source caller body access.

Authored target intent has two closed bases. A before target names exact starting
source evidence and maps through the staged edits. A candidate target names the
owned immutable descriptor and is validated against that candidate's resulting
source. It is not a guessed future live revision; final publication materializes
actual source context. Document-wide targets remain document scope; point targets
declare one affinity and supported position/content profile; ranges are nonempty
UTF-8 byte ranges under §4.3.1. Unsupported profiles, invalid boundaries, unavailable
candidate/source evidence and wrong descriptor reject without clamping or guessing.
Candidate target authority is no broader than the actual current command grants.

The user-approved §29.4.1 snapshot format explicitly preserves both named point
profiles, separately from offset and affinity, in authored and located targets.
Missing/unknown profiles reject without default, coercion or implicit migration
from earlier draft profileless points. The approved decode/stage and later native
capture evidence do not promote this compound field-journal reference to a native
restoration, complete persistence or provider guarantee.

Distinct body and target field intent for one logical record may be combined using
their respective current versions. Normalize repeated field wishes to one
unambiguous final intent before owned publication; this product refuses duplicate
same-field components. One logical annotation contributes one authored history
scope even when both fields change. Whole-plan replay/intent identity still follows
§6.5; commutative field effects do not by themselves select a wire canonicalizer.
Automatic source-driven mapping changes current evidence, not authored body or
explicit target generations and not annotation authored-history frontiers.

Stage complete source, current placement, authored field and history effects, then
validate/publish them once or leave current state unchanged. Current source-write
rights and explicit annotation-authoring rights remain separate from required
internal mapping eligibility. A missing required companion refuses the whole plan;
its private identity is not an incidental public error field. Complete semantic
identity under §6.4 preserves publication/history/version state and does not
require an otherwise unused new version counter. Equal source bytes alone cannot
erase meaningful mapping or other companion intent.

The body/target reference in formal/annotation-compounds.md supplies scoped
publication and reversal composition. Section 13.9.1 separately extends normalized
compound membership and linked reversal. Native issuance/routing, lifecycle-profile
activation, complete retirement planning, general retained mapping-history and actual
native/physical refinement remain gates. No source/annotation save milestone is
conflated with this local publication.

### 13.9.1 Retained membership and identity restoration

Separate present membership, retained absence and final retirement. Authored deletion
removes the current collection row but retains its logical identity/payload while
history or other obligations require it. Eligible owned undo/redo can reintroduce
that same non-retired entity, not allocate a different meaning under an old identity.
Final retirement is absorbing. Normal create never reuses a tracked identical
incarnation, and restoration cannot coexist with a newer live incarnation of that ID.
Neither historic authorship, possession of an identifier nor restoration revives grants.

The normalized profile carries explicit bounded per-document lifecycle inventories.
Missing/inconsistent inventory is unknown, not empty, and is not silently activated.
Private create components bind already-issued identity/body/target to the complete
owned plan and complete create list under current trusted allocation evidence.
Those checks do not implement an issuer; public F13 create still has no caller-ID field.
Reject mixed membership and body/target wishes on one incarnation before staging;
preparation must normalize one unambiguous final intent. All actual source, membership,
field, history and current-view participants share the existing root/outcome boundary.

Removal retains current field versions as monotone floors. Restoration validates the
retained entity and authored wishes and assigns both field versions strictly above
their retained floors, never old numeric versions. Thus pre-absence body/target commands
remain stale. Counter or retained-resource exhaustion refuses the whole operation.
Body/target/source paths also honor activated lifecycle root/record bounds; payload
retention cannot be bypassed through another operation kind.

Restore current placement only with supported current source/target evidence. The
reference checks unchanged relevant source context or its own linked source journal
with valid restoration evidence. Equal bytes after unrelated history do not suffice.
Unavailable general mapping proof refuses the whole group, not silent coordinate
relabeling or a newly invented detached-restoration policy. Source/annotations across
documents reverse atomically at all actual participant frontiers. Later work on any
authored participant blocks the whole linked reversal until explicitly undone.

Internal final retirement requires retained absence, current authority, satisfied
authored persistence/discard, history/retention/session release, drained delivery and
version/resource/bookkeeping capacity. Check the actual root as well: no retained
journal, including invalidated groups, may still reference the record. The phase then
becomes retired, payload is released and identity/floors remain reserved; live annotation
snapshot generation/source/frontiers do not change. This is not a public cleanup verb
or a complete history-floor planner. Unexpected admitted history kinds fault/fence the
domain with Unknown, not guessed target behavior or confirmed nonpublication.

[Membership evidence](formal/annotation-membership.md) includes 4,096 publication/
8,192 reversal/1,024 retirement gates, six target forms, seventeen controls/fifteen
mutants, actual native F14/current-view/shared-invocation traces and two-document linked
membership/source reversal. Depth-three exploration covers 42 states/71 edges, not
arbitrary-length closure. Six positive SMT conditions and two controls support version/
lifetime guard laws, not issuer or mapping truth. PATH-01/03/04/10/12 and existing
INS-01/02/03/06/07/08/12/13 distinguish membership, history, current release and held
payload/discharge without private content/ID labels. Native issuance/gateway, profile
legacy/annotation-snapshot activation and full lifecycle integration beyond §11.2.4, general target/history retirement, full
query/events and actual host/concurrent/physical/decoder/production/independent refinement
remain. Point persistence is unchanged; no whole F13/F14 or D-row closes.

### 13.9.2 Declared read dependencies in native compound publication

Requirements §5.1 permits read-only assumptions outside authored participants.
The private `owned-annotation-plan/2` extends `/1` with a mandatory `reads`
conjunction; `/1` keeps its exact existing fields and rejects a `reads` extension.
This is a versioned native reference product, not a new public wire format, job
kind, operation family or user-defined predicate language.

Each read names an exact authority/document/incarnation and one closed predicate:
source revision, annotation-set revision, live annotation body version, or live
annotation authored-target generation. Record predicates also name exact record
identity/incarnation. Authored target is not automatically mapped placement;
placement-sensitive and enumeration assumptions must declare the corresponding
source/set dependencies. Required configuration, registry or semantic-provider
assumptions retain their owning contracts; these four predicates do not substitute
for unsupported dependency domains or discover undeclared assumptions.

Read order has no meaning. Reject repeated subjects, including conflicting
expectations, instead of silently deduplicating them. Admission validates finite
closed products, retains an immutable copy and canonicalizes only the read set by
UTF-8 byte order of the fixed kind/document/record identity tuple. It must not
reorder or coalesce authored edit records. The existing complete intent-byte bound
applies; final nonempty reads also require finite dependency/identifier limits.

Before candidate changes or no-op classification, validate every read against the
actual current starting root under the invocation's actual complete context.
Require exact current read/presence/equality permission facts bound to every full
predicate and that context; missing, duplicate, surplus, mismatched or non-true
facts refuse. Current host policy truth remains a supplier obligation. Missing,
disposed, foreign or reincarnated subjects and mismatched versions refuse the whole
publication without changing the current root. A source revision match is not a
substitute for body/set/target matches. An empty conjunction needs no additional
unused read permission; all existing command/publication obligations still apply.

Read-only objects need no invented write grant, receive no candidate mutation or
version allocation, and do not become authored history scopes. Same-object reads
validate before its authored change. Unrelated publications do not stale a precise
read merely by changing the authority publication counter. Subsequent reversal
still follows frontier-only authored history and separately declared reversal
dependencies; forward validation does not establish semantic invertibility.

[Scoped reference evidence](formal/read-dependencies.md) exercises the actual
native owner and coherent mutated module graphs. It is not a standalone F10
validation query, a public codec, general semantic dependency discovery, production
concurrency refinement or independent Cleanroom certification.

### 13.9.3 Configuration read dependencies

The private `owned-annotation-plan/4` retains `/3`'s exact plan fields and source
write scopes and adds two closed read kinds. Older plan profiles retain their
existing vocabularies. `configuration-domain` names an authority/target/incarnation,
one of source, serialization or analysis, and its expected semantic generation.
`configuration-state` names an authority and expected whole-configuration generation
for metadata-sensitive assumptions. Both also require the expected schema,
restriction and association generations. Every expected configuration generation
is a positive safe integer; unknown kinds, domains, fields and duplicate subjects
refuse. These are logical settings targets, not inferred document membership.

Nonempty `/4` reads require `native-read-authority/2` with the actual invocation
context and one exact read/presence/equality grant per complete predicate. This
includes authority to observe a whole-configuration predicate where selected;
visibility of one setting alone cannot establish that permission. Configuration
predicates validate against coherent settings in the actual starting owner root,
under the finite configuration profile, before no-op classification or candidate
changes. A caller context vector, reported effective value or old inspection
selector cannot replace that root. A pure coherence validator establishes neither
ownership nor actual host policy truth.

Semantic-domain counters change on effective value changes; origin-only metadata
and unrelated target/domain changes preserve an unaffected domain predicate.
The whole-configuration counter intentionally has broader invalidation. Value
restoration does not restore old generations. Schema/restriction/association
changes must also match their separate interpretation versions. Configuration
reads remain conjunctive, are canonicalized without reordering authored edits,
and add no history write participant. An empty conjunction requires no unused
configuration service, profile or read grant. Existing publication gates remain.

The same rules serve native compound publication and the F10 advisory candidate
query; advisory success grants no mutation authority or reservation and can become
stale before publication. Retrying an already completed invocation observes its
historical outcome, rather than refreshing predicates or executing it again.
[Scoped configuration evidence](formal/configuration-reads.md) covers native
interleavings, advisory agreement and five weakened-version controls. Complete
consumer dependency discovery, mutable definition/association activation, real
membership/policy truth, public wire/Rust products, physical/concurrent/crash
refinement and independent assurance remain open.

### 13.9.4 Workspace membership read dependencies

The private `owned-annotation-plan/5` retains `/4`'s exact plan fields, source
write scopes and configuration predicates, and adds `workspace-membership` with
exact fields `kind`, `workspace` and `expectedWorkspace`. The workspace is an
authority/id/incarnation triple; its expected generation is a safe natural
integer, including an explicitly represented zero. Missing/unknown generation is
not zero. Earlier profiles retain their closed vocabularies. Reject extra fields,
ambiguous or repeated subjects, conflicting expectations, invalid identities and
exceeded bounds. Canonicalize the conjunctive read set, not authored edit records.

Nonempty `/5` reads use `native-read-authority/2`: one exact current read/presence/
equality grant for each complete predicate under the actual invocation context.
Reading a document or possessing a workspace identity does not authorize observing
that workspace's membership generation. The predicate checks the actual starting
owner root for one exact live workspace incarnation with a matching safe generation.
Missing, retired, nonlive, ambiguous or changed targets refuse the whole candidate
before mutation or no-op classification. Host context vectors, value equality or
caller labels cannot substitute for that current root. Empty conjunctions require
no unused workspace/configuration service or read grant.

Use the existing native workspace generation: effective membership addition/removal
and disposal of an actual member advance it; idempotent membership leaves it
unchanged. Add/remove ABA does not restore the old generation. Container retirement
removes the target; it does not dispose its documents. Changes to another workspace,
new peer containers or unrelated source publication do not invalidate this precise
predicate solely by advancing the global publication or identity allocator.

This guards the selected declared membership set, not member source revisions,
the complete workspace registry, filesystem contents, semantic discovery coverage
or external membership truth. Declare relevant source/configuration/provider and
other footprint assumptions separately. Reading a workspace neither adds an
authored history scope nor grants mutation or reversal rights. Source and annotation
ownership remain independent of membership. Advisory validation shares the same
predicate; a successful query is not a reservation. Completed invocation replay
retains its historical result without refreshing old assumptions or executing again.

[Workspace evidence](formal/workspace-reads.md) covers actual native command and
advisory routes, membership/disposal/retirement/disjoint interleavings, mixed
configuration reads, fifteen controls and nine predicate mutants. Four conditional
BASE-WSREAD cases add three currentness/ABA/frame laws and a value-only weakened-rule
witness. They assume the declared generation step laws; native tests exercise
selected producers, not a general implementation refinement. Existing host-policy,
complete discovery, public wire/Rust, physical/concurrent/crash and independent
assurance gates remain. No new public family, job kind, UI or filesystem mechanism
is introduced.

### 13.9.5 Composition of declared read footprints

The existing `/5` read vocabulary composes conjunctively across source revisions,
annotation-set/body/authored-target versions, configuration domain/state and
workspace membership. A complete captured predicate, its current observation
grants and its actual owner-root condition must all hold. One current predicate
cannot satisfy another, and a changed read-only participant must refuse the whole
candidate before mutation or no-op classification. Read dependencies neither
become authored history participants nor grant mutation rights.

Advisory F10 validation and native publication use the same current predicate
checks. Advice must leave the root and invocation accounting unchanged; it does
not reserve future validity. Preparation/admission and an earlier successful
advice response cannot excuse later changes. Canonicalizing a read conjunction
may reorder predicates, not edits or source scopes. Typed/dynamic retries with
the same conjunction retain one intent and invocation.

For a fixed finite set U of distinct valid predicate instances and a set C of
currently satisfied instances, the accepted read sets are exactly the subsets
of C, assuming matching current complete observation grants and other required
checks. The powerset of U is a finite bounded Boolean lattice under intersection
and union; the successful sets form the powerset of C with top C and bottom the
empty set. This describes this explicit predicate-selection guard only. It does
not make document execution, permissions, provider semantics, automatically
discovered dependencies or the whole engine a categorically complete lattice.
Changing the selected set is a different intent, not permission to drop a stale
dependency from an already admitted request.

[Composition evidence](formal/mixed-reads.md) fixes nine predicate instances in
one owner: four source/annotation footprints, three configuration domains, whole
configuration and workspace membership. It checks all 512 captured-version
mismatch patterns against all 512 selected sets (262,144 cases), plus 5,120
single-mismatch subset cases, 81 selected permission refusals, forty native
changed/no-op cases, 28 actual interleavings and 96 advisory observations. Thirteen
targeted mutations must fail semantic assertions after coherent graph construction.
Read-only documents, configuration and workspaces remain value-framed; only the
declared authored participant enters the new history group.

This adds evidence for existing contracts, not a new predicate, generation, host
service, job kind, public wire codec or solver law. Automatic complete dependency
discovery, other provider/semantic domains, actual policy/membership truth,
physical/concurrent/crash refinement and independent assurance remain gates.
INS-01/02/03/08/09/12/13 retain admission, advice, current validation, publication,
retention and interpretation observations. MELT/golden/RED/USE distinguish query
work from publication and useful applied/unchanged work from refusals. STRIDE/
LINDDUN and STPA/FMEA include missing/substituted predicates, stale-grant replay,
early success and accidental writes to read-only participants. Use bounded reason
codes, never identities, versions, predicate sets, source or grants in ordinary labels.

### 13.9.6 Owned component receipts for native compound publication

An internal first-party compound preparation may bind the existing F13 receipt
products to every authored annotation component in original component order.
Derive operation, document/record incarnation and create allocation identity from
the exact normalized private plan; do not accept a second independent list of
receipt targets. Bind the immutable hold to the actual invocation parent, domain,
ticket and original plan. Matching retries retain that hold and its admission
ceilings; changed intent cannot replace it. This preparation port grants neither
source nor annotation-authoring authority and is not a public mixed-plan API.

The selected compound create-result baseline is original-component-scoped
authority. A trusted grant names the original invocation, authority, document and
annotation-component ordinal; native preparation binds it to that component's
exact allocation in the immutable normalized plan. The ordinal is a locator,
never a credential. Freeze original order, not execution, filtered or reply order;
there is no invocation-wide sibling grant or additional preallocation handshake.
Existing-record grants remain exact-identity grants. Current create-result release
may name that original component scope or its exact allocated identity, always
under the captured per-component ceiling. The separate closed native
CompoundAnnotationResultGrantTargetV1 profile does not extend standalone
AnnotationResultGrantTargetV1 or the exhaustive F06 V1–V3 result enums.

Before accepting the hold, preflight each complete receipt/release frame under
maxResultBytes and capture its original disclosure ceiling. Let B be the logical
serialized bytes of the retained plan, component receipt descriptors and ceilings,
and n the bounded annotation-component count. Reserve 2B + 3n·maxResultBytes from
the actual invocation owner's remaining maxHeldBytes, using checked arithmetic.
B must fit maxIntentBytes. The reservation covers two metadata/capture frames
and staged, retained and release result frames. These are declared logical units,
not physical allocation peaks or additional unbounded capacity pools.

Stage the complete immutable receipt vector from the same final candidate used
for the coarse outcome, after final native validation and outer-root checks but
before trusted installation. Recheck the original plan binding. Root, coarse
terminal facts, all component receipts and done phase share one installation;
no component receipt becomes successful early. Known whole-plan refusal retains
only not-published component facts. Unexpected capture/protocol failure preserves
the previous root, records Unknown/faulted and installs no success vector.
Applied/unchanged describes the whole compound disposition: every successful
component describes the same final candidate, including combined body/target
changes on one record and unchanged fields in an otherwise applied compound.
An interruption during trusted installation can leave a partially installed,
fault-fenced native root; it must not yield a success vector or known refusal.
This fence is not crash rollback or failure atomicity under process termination.

Current result release selects an original component by checked index and applies
both its captured ceiling and current exact invocation/record grant. Read only
the retained receipt, never a newer row or a reconstructed current publication.
Neither a broader later grant nor another component's grant widens the original
ceiling. Missing original result grants may withhold component receipts without
preventing an otherwise authorized authored publication.

Under §13.8's retention/drain rules, forgetting clears the coarse result and
complete receipt vector without refunding the original preparation or making the
ticket fresh. This path requires strict Boolean retentionReleased/deliveryDrained;
it does not add owner control to ordinary annotation-result eviction. Actual hold
retirement/refund separately requires strict owner control, retention release and
delivery drain, including for a faulted owner. Release the charge once, invalidate
the hold, and preserve spent issuance and any independently retained obligations.

[Coordinator evidence](formal/atomic-annotation-results.md) exercises native mixed
source/create/body/reattach/delete publication, historical release after a later
native edit, current/captured policy, actual parent headroom, stop/refusal/fault,

## 14 Scoped frontier history and linked reversal

Requirements §5.8 governs IF-12, PATH-04 and INV-06/16. Source-text history is
scoped to a document and authored-content history to an annotation record.
Views, authors and language regions do not own independent authoritative text
histories. Navigation, focus, diagnostics, derived refresh and automatic attachment
mapping are not authored-content edits.

### 14.1 Group and frontier state

A retained group identifies its original logical operation, every explicit source
or annotation-content participant, required inverse/forward data, frontier/context
versions and reversal dependencies. A group cannot be split by grouping, eviction
or a caller selecting only one visible participant. Typing coalescing, if supported,
uses D13's bounded explicit boundaries; time proximity is not permission to merge
authors or unrelated linked plans.

For every history scope `p`, distinguish its current undo and redo frontiers and
retained eligibility data. `Participants(g)` is the actual complete linked set,
not its recipient-visible projection. An undo request names an explicit scope or
retained group. Resolve any invoking-view context before admission; never target
the most recently edited comment merely because the source view has focus.

### 14.2 Atomic undo and redo predicates

`UndoAllowed(S,g)` requires `g` at every participant's current undo frontier,
retained valid inverse data, live matching incarnations, current rights, expected
contents/frontier versions and all reversal dependencies. `RedoAllowed` analogously
requires the matching redo frontier and retained forward data. These predicates
do not require equality with original numeric source revisions: later undo/redo
produces new revisions.

| Condition | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Every participant eligible | Publish content/mappings and all linked frontier movement atomically; assign a new reversal operation identity linked to the original group and advance changed content versions |
| Later group blocks one participant | Report a recipient-safe blocked disposition and change none; do not skip, auto-undo a prerequisite or reverse only visible participants |
| Missing inverse/history or disposed participant | Report unavailable/conflict under current policy; do not implicitly reload or recreate an owner |
| Current permission or dependency fails | Reject the whole reversal unchanged; historic authorship/group ID is not authority |
| New authored work follows undo | Invalidate the affected redo continuation, complete linked groups and dependent continuation together; independent scopes retain their histories |

A reversal changes history position rather than appending an ordinary edit that
would undo itself forever. It restores supported authored content, not old revision
IDs, authority, resource bindings, old selections in other views, persisted bytes
or external effects. Map live selections normally; any invoking-view restoration
requires its current context. Redo never replays save/clipboard/tool effects.
Textual invertibility does not prove semantic rename correctness or complete
reference discovery.

For G editing A/B and H later editing B, undo G from A is blocked until H is
explicitly undone. An unrelated edit of C does not block G. Later comments on A/B
do not block source undo merely due to automatic anchor mapping; a later change
to a comment explicitly authored by G does block G's compound reversal until its
annotation-content frontier is eligible.

### 14.3 Retention and conformance

Bound inverses, linked fan-out, groups, redo continuations and pins. Consistent
history floors invalidate dependent eligibility as complete units; when promised
retention prevents safe eviction/disposal, refuse that action. Do not silently
drop unsaved authored content, leave partial linked groups or keep unlimited pins.
Empty history, blocked history and no-longer-retained history are distinct.
D14 selects concrete budgets/floors/pins and D13 the grouping profile.

Independent tests cover linked blocking/disjoint participants, fresh-revision
round trips, later comment preservation, compound comment blocking, changed
authority, disposal, linked redo invalidation and retention limits. PS-HI/BR/EC
prove restricted cases only; general inverse/mapping/frontier refinement remains
an obligation. INS-06/02/03/08 observe validation/publication, safe blockers,
availability and retained pressure. Private participant IDs/graphs do not become
public conflict previews; telemetry and history identifiers cannot authorize undo.

### 14.4 Authored field journals and mapped source reversal

An annotation record's authored history scope covers its body and explicit target
choices. Independent field versions permit compatible field updates; they do not
create independent selective-undo histories. A later explicit change to either
field can block an earlier authored group on that record. Source-driven placement
mapping alone does not add that record to source history, so later comment edits
or reattachments do not automatically block unrelated source undo.

Retain exact before/after authored fields and supported source forward/inverse
transforms with each complete group's participant/frontier evidence. Do not undo
by reinstalling a historical whole document or annotation row. Source undo maps
the currently live records through actual inverse transforms, preserving later
bodies, authored targets and their versions unless those fields are actual
eligible participants. Explicit target reversal additionally needs supported
retained target/source mapping evidence; unavailable evidence refuses, never
relocates an old coordinate under a new revision label. Source-only undo does not
automatically reattach a detached target just because equal text reappears.

Every participant must be at the required frontier even when current bytes happen
to equal an old group value after later edits. Validate current identity, grants,
expected state, retention and required companions, then reverse and move frontiers
atomically. Restore authored values with fresh changed versions, not old counter
values; reversal has its own invocation linked to the original group and is not
an ordinary new group that repeatedly undoes itself. Never reverse external effects.

New authored work invalidates complete linked redo groups and dependent redo
continuations across every actual scope. Unrelated scopes retain their frontiers.
Bound source inverse work, mapping fan-out, record journals, closure, pins and
complete-group retirement under the finite profile. Recipient-visible history is
a projection, never the source of the actual participant set. Complete native
F04/F14 products, actual membership issuance/decoded gateway beyond §§13.6.2/13.9.1, general retained mapping
profiles and implementation/resource evidence remain open. The composed reference
in formal/annotation-compounds.md proves only its stated field/source subset.

### 14.5 Scoped native history inspection

The design product `history-query/1` refines existing F04, not a new verb or wire
language. Its closed variants are frontier, availability and permitted-blocking-
detail. Every request carries `contract`, `operation`, `context`, `scope`,
`direction` (undo/redo) and `profile`. Availability/detail additionally carry
`group`: either the current scope frontier or a projected retained group reference.
Resolve these through the owner's retained history context and exact projection;
raw internal IDs and source/annotation snapshot selectors are not history grants.
Section 14.5.1 supplies selected internal native context issuance and current basis
checks. Public history acquisition and native encoding remain refinement gates;
this product does not add history scope to F02's already selected read contexts.

| Variant | Available product |
|---|---|
| frontier | Context and projected frontier group, or established empty frontier |
| availability | Context and empty, eligible or blocked frontier/evidence state |
| permitted-blocking-detail | Context and bounded permitted blocking scope/group references |

The common unavailable product contains no private reason, count or participant.
Establish empty only from complete retained coverage. Missing inverse/evidence,
invalidated group, withheld head or unknown floor is not empty. Compute blocking
from the complete actual linked participant set, never just the visible graph.
Eligible describes captured frontier/evidence state, not complete command authority
or a reservation. F14 must independently revalidate current rights, identity,
content, interpretation, bounds, stop state, retention and all companions.

Release binds recipient, purpose, destination, projection/profile, history basis,
policy and continuity. Require current grant, retention, live context and bounded
transfer; stale current advice is unavailable. A richer current policy cannot
expand captured facts, and a narrower policy cannot release the old richer product.
New acquisition can observe new history. Inspection cannot mutate content/frontiers,
issue reversal authority, imply persistence or reserve unbounded inverse retention.

Detail is the permitted projection only. Its empty list does not prove absence
of blockers. Overall blocked state is an explicit operational disclosure for an
inspectable linked group, not permission to expose hidden identities/counts or
global sequence values. Bound actual capture/registry work, linked participants,
retained bytes, detail and transfer; refuse rather than claim a partial graph is
complete. A failed capture is unavailable, not an empty history.

formal/history-queries.md records composition with actual normalized compound
publication/reversal, release gates, paired hidden-state checks and mutation
sensitivity. Context issuance, authoritative registry/coverage/policy truth,
complete reversal eligibility, physical accounting and actual native refinement
remain gates. Point-profile persistence is unaffected by this inspection product.

### 14.5.1 Owned native history contexts and current reversal preparation

The internal history owner binds the actual invocation domain's authority/engine
and exact history recipient, purpose, destination, profile, policy and continuity.
It uses the existing bounded selector pattern without adding history to F02, a
public acquisition/control variant, wire token, service or per-file engine.
Validate exact finite projection shapes, unique group/scope identities and aliases,
Boolean detail/completeness/evidence facets and actual selected group existence.
Trusted host alias safety, coverage, evidence and permission truth remain premises.

Successful acquisition copies actual history metadata, installs a fresh opaque owned
handle and advances a monotone lifetime issuance count. Cloned/foreign handles and
raw labels do not resolve. Preserve the native handle identity across copied results;
do not export private binding labels or participant internals. Public transport/Rust
encoding and externally authenticated issuance remain separate gates.

The private current comparison basis includes selected groups' identity/validity/
complete participant scopes and both frontier stacks for every actual participant
and selected scope. Normalize set-like ordering, not stack order. Do not use just
visible participants or the global root/publication counter. Within profile bounds,
unrelated work leaves scoped advice valid. Global metadata pressure may still refuse
under the declared operational-interference allowance.

Each F04 delivery and trusted alias resolution needs the exact owned live context,
current scope/grant/retention/liveness/continuity/history/transfer/reply gates and a
matching actual current basis. The explicit bound losses in §12.8.3 and observed
basis mismatch invalidate that context permanently; later equality or regrant cannot

unobserved ABA excursions, actual inverse retention, authored values/versions or
companion truth. Independent current history/evidence facts remain mandatory.

Existing F04 empty/eligible/blocked/detail meanings are unchanged. Complete actual
participants determine blocking; only permitted aliases enter bounded detail.
Eligible advice reserves no frontier and grants no reversal right. Private alias
resolution can supply existing F14 group/scope bindings, but actual preparation and
publication independently validate current rights, identity, values, dependencies,
views, bounds, retention and all companions. Refusal can occur during preparation
or publication. Closing an inspection context does not cancel an already-owned
reversal plan, whose original group and invocation remain fixed.

Reserve live/invalidated contexts, lifetime issuance, groups/scopes/participants,

bytes; check safe integer arithmetic before owner admission. Stop/closure uses
recipient-bound owner control without content grant or spare ordinary capacity.
Invalidated entries retain capacity until separate owner-controlled retirement with
actual delivery drain and retention discharge. Retirement does not reset issuance.

selector/event/codec products and operational/independent gates remain. Full
frozen verification and endpoint reconciliation are required before adoption;
finite evidence does not establish categorical or whole-family completeness.

### 14.6 Native reversal requests and owned admission

The semantic product `history-reversal/1` refines F14's existing undo/redo variants.
Requests carry `contract`, `operation`, `invocation`, `authority`, `target`,
`profile` and bounded extra `dependencies`. The closed target is either a retained
group reference or a scope-frontier reference with an expected group. Human ingress
may resolve a scope gesture before queueing; it must freeze that group as part of
the invocation, never retarget to a newer frontier at publication. Neither group
knowledge nor an F04 eligible result grants reversal rights. Command references
are owner-resolved independently of permission to inspect private participants.

Union mandatory engine dependencies with caller read dependencies under §5; callers
cannot omit, replace or narrow required scope. Capture the retained group/journals,
all actual frontiers and current document/source/annotation-set dependencies needed
for complete reversal and mapping. An unrelated document edit alone does not stale
this scoped preparation. A required current annotation-set change can stale it;
fresh preparation maps current rows and preserves later bodies under §14.4 rather
than treating them as authored source-history participants.

Owned preparation binds engine incarnation, recipient, complete invocation intent
and execution profile. A copied lookalike is not an owned plan. Final admission
requires current all-participant rights, fresh invocation eligibility under §6.5,
stop/interpretation/companion validity, retained journals and current dependency,
resource and version availability. Check that required scope has not expanded and
the prepared group/participants have not changed. Revalidate actual frontiers and
expected contents; publish all content/mappings/frontier movement once with fresh
changed versions, or leave state unchanged. Do not add an ordinary authored group
that would undo the reversal itself. Do not replay external effects.

Authoritative terminal dispositions are applied or confirmed not-published for
this first-admission product, with recipient-safe facts released under §§12/23.
An empty or unavailable target cannot authorize selecting another group. Pending,
duplicate, forgotten, retired, stopped or unestablished invocation observations
remain governed by §§6.5/17/23; they cannot be guessed from a fresh evaluator call.
Reply failure after publication does not establish nonapplication.

Bound registry scans, participant/journal/inverse/mapping work, dependency union,
owned preparation, retention and transfer before admission. Insufficient required
resources refuse rather than partially reverse or discard obligations. The
normalized composition in formal/history-reversal.md supplies source/body scoped
evidence, not general membership/target restoration, full replay/reply composition,
physical accounting, hostile native decoding or concurrent implementation proof.
Point representation is fixed by the approved §29.4.1 profiles; native restoration
and persistence integration remain separate evidence gates.

### 14.6.1 Native reversal decision receipts and current release

F14's normalized result is reversal-result with a known applied/not-published
decision, or common unavailable. Both known decisions contain the original
invocation and undo/redo operation. Applied additionally identifies its historical
publication by the once-only reversal invocation's causal anchor, not a raw root
counter or the authored group. Not-published contains no candidate target,
publication, participant, version or existence facts. Unchanged is not an F14
decision. Pending, unknown/faulted, forgotten and retired observations cannot be
inferred as confirmed refusal or evaluated again.

Mandatory result release requires exact retained invocation context, original and
current F06 publication ceilings/epoch and common current release gates. The minimal
F14 decision is useful without a target field; write authority does not disclose
that target. An optional exact trusted reversalResultGrant binds invocation,
authority, original typed target and Boolean discloseTarget. Copy/freeze its ceiling
at admission; absent means false, malformed/substituted grants refuse. For applied
results, expose target only under both captured and matching current disclosure.
An absent current grant keeps the minimal decision; an invalid supplied grant makes
the result unavailable. The Boolean disclosure subdomain forms a two-element bounded
distributive lattice, not a closure claim about editor operations.

The optional target is the original group or scope-frontier/expected-group request,
never a freshly resolved frontier, private participant graph or new F04 selector.
It is historical reference information, not current alias validity or mutation
authority. Current grant truth must permit that historical disclosure, even if
the original history context has closed. Another reversal still needs current
supported bindings and complete ordinary F14 admission. Existing F06 participant
details remain independently protected.

Owned receipt admission uses the same native producer provenance as preparation/
publication; copied frozen lookalikes refuse. Reserve the full private receipt and
maximum permitted frame before pending execution, even when target is withheld.
Reuse the existing operation-specific receipt/frame pair within the per-slot five
result-maxima charge: annotation and reversal kinds are exclusive, not two receipts
for one invocation. No public numeric default or physical accounting claim is added.

After actual candidate and outer-root validation, capture minimal confirmed refusal
or verify applied movement of the original complete group to the opposite-direction
frontiers for every actual participant. Retain copied scalar/target facts only, not
roots, contents, inverses, views or private group IDs. Validate vocabulary/size before
paired root/coarse-fact/receipt/done installation. A surprise faults/fences with
Unknown and no receipt. Later history changes or domain faults never reconstruct
or rewrite this receipt. Cache forgetting/retirement follows independent retention/
drain checks and never resets issuance, retargets or reexecutes the invocation.

[Scoped evidence](formal/reversal-results.md) includes 224 native receipt/512 release
cases, thirteen controls/fourteen mutants with passing baseline, actual two-document
source reversal, conditional preservation/finite-loop arguments and six local
conditions (217 total/thirteen manifests). INS-01/02/03/06/07/08/12/13 distinguish
publication, result withholding/loss, pressure and discharge; MELT/RED/golden/USE
and STRIDE/LINDDUN apply without raw aliases/content/IDs as ordinary metric labels.
Public wire/history-alias bridges, actual grants/aliases/retention, full retirement/
general mapping/point persistence, other result/effect gateways and physical/
concurrent/native/decoder/production/independent refinement remain gates. No whole
family or D-row is closed by this selected native result product.

### 14.6.2 Standalone annotation and reversal invocation binding

The shared IF-01 typed/dynamic tuple accepts the existing annotation-authoring/1
F13 create/update-body/reattach/delete products and history-reversal/1 F14 undo/
redo products. Preserve their exact native fields and supported targets; do not
add caller-owned plans, allocation facts, host bindings or a new operation family.
Normalize bounded ordinary data and bind the complete original invocation/context.
An identical retry observes the original preparation/decision; changed intent
refuses, and service never reparses the request against a newer history frontier.

Separate trusted annotation/history host roles supply native owner, recipient,
profile, permissions, dependencies, allocation and limits. Capture a complete finite
limit profile before native preparation and retain its original identity/values.
Require each declared annotation/membership/history/view coordinate as applicable;
missing fields do not mean unbounded. Final service checks current strict Boolean
permissions, original profile and the actual owned native capsule. Source-write
rights are not an annotation-authoring prerequisite. A no-op body update need not
consume an unused version. Preserve the original create allocation and both point
profiles; do not refresh an already prepared reversal's participants or target.

For public capture C, parent intent bound M, root bound R and the maximum captured
native plan/view/membership construction ceiling N, reserve checked logical frames
3C + 2M + 2R + 2 max(0,N-M) from the actual parent. Capture the bounded native limit
metadata under the base reservation, then reserve any extra construction capacity
before calling the native builder. A ceiling above M is not itself an oversized
intent: accept a small valid plan if funded, but require its actual retained intent
to fit M. Invalid profiles, overflow or insufficient headroom refuse and refund
only provisional holds. This is declared serialized-frame accounting, not RSS.

Native publication, terminal facts and receipts use the existing coordinator.
Captured result ceilings and current release grants remain independent of mutation
rights. Stop/fault/forget do not refund lifetime issuance or substitute for protected
drain/retirement. Section 23.1.10 selects U01's typed retained-outcome receipt facet;
these internal native receipt ports supply its operation-specific release. This binding does not activate a new discovery
profile or close cross-family events/results. Scoped evidence is in
[standalone native command binding](formal/native-local-command-binding.md).

### 14.7 Current view companions in native reversal

F14 owned preparation now includes the source participants' current attached views
under the named explicit-positional-selection/1 profile. Capture exact view/document

profile. Missing source-view inventory is unknown, not empty; a declared empty

no source-selection participants or source-view-profile prerequisite. No caller

Undo maps those current selections through the actual retained sequential inverse
batches; redo maps through the actual simultaneous forward batch. Normalize only
after the complete per-document transform. Do not replace an inverse sequence with
a sorted batch, restore historical selections/viewport state or resurrect closed
views. A fresh preparation includes views opened after the original group. New,
closed or changed required views invalidate old preparation; unrelated view state
and late viewport changes are preserved from the current root.

Final native admission rechecks the owned view part, current profile/membership/
versions, journal/work/plan bounds and view-generation capacity. Source/annotation/
frontier reversal and mapped view source contexts form one private complete
candidate before publication. Verify actual resulting bytes/fresh source revisions;
advance selection generations only for changed selections. No additional source
publication, authored group or external replay follows from view mapping. Current
source context must update even when selection coordinates remain equal.

[The native bridge evidence](formal/history-views.md) composes the actual F14,
retained source/annotation and positional selection helpers: 1,024 gate cases,
1,010 finite point-oracle cases, 14 multi-edit inverse/forward traces, 42 controls
and eight mutants. This discharges the earlier raw-helper gap for the named
reference profile, not for every view/native/provider profile. General target/

companions, replay/outcome/event, physical ownership and concurrent implementation
