### 16.5.4 Annotation baseline capacity envelopes

Before an ordinary annotation save can promise later baseline installation,
account for the complete future baseline, not merely its payload bytes or the
smallest acknowledgment frame. For a fixed captured baseline descriptor and
exact serialized bytes, only external version, dispatch serial and qualified
acknowledgment vary in this sizing contract. Binding generations, source/set,
context, origin, provider/procedure, format and captured requested strength remain
immutable. Sizing does not authenticate those facts or qualify a write.

Let S be the UTF-8 byte size of the declared compact JSON reference encoding.
Normalize the sizing template P to a null external version, the largest safe
dispatch serial and synchronized acknowledgment. If T bounds the complete
serialized non-null version object, the baseline bound is
`B = S(P) + max(0, T - S(null))`.
This includes JSON escaping and numeric-array representation; token character
count and raw artifact length are insufficient. Reject unsafe arithmetic or a
bound above maxBaselineBytes. Null external version remains possible even when
T is too small to admit a non-null version. This is not permission to invent a
version or strengthen an acknowledgment.

For the current complete root, replace the addressed annotationBaseline slot
with null, inserting the field if absent, and use the maximum publication-counter
width to obtain R0. The complete candidate bound is `S(R0) - S(null) + B`.
Require one actual remaining publication unit and the complete root bound.
Existing baseline replacement can shrink the root; field-name overhead for a
missing slot must still be counted. Only the baseline and publication fields
are substituted for sizing. Duplicate, missing, foreign or disposed targets refuse.

An envelope is a sizing value, not a grant, acknowledgment, task admission or
reservation. Recompute the complete root bound against current state. Competing
edits may proceed while sufficient space remains; never freeze the document or
assume its admission-time size remains current. Actual ordinary-save admission
must hold the required staging, retained-evidence, root-slot and publication
obligations in the shared reservation discipline, and all competing publications
must preserve them or refuse atomically. Cancellation and unknown effects do not
prove those obligations discharged. These integrations remain open; the helper
neither debits the writer nor installs a candidate root.

[Capacity evidence](formal/annotation-baseline-capacity.md) covers 42 actual native
capture/undo/redo and writer-baseline cases, 504 future-evidence combinations,
ten controls/twelve mutants with passing baseline, exact-limit witnesses and
conditional size inequalities. No new public operation, solver condition or
ordinary-save/load closure is selected. INS-01/02/07/08/13 distinguish sizing,
admitted holds, current-root refusal, acknowledgment and actual discharge.
MELT, RED/USE/golden and STRIDE/LINDDUN cover under-reservation, stale root size,
counter exhaustion, forged descriptors and equality/occupancy linkage without
content, paths, contexts, origins, identities or tokens in metric labels. Actual
installed telemetry, host facts, all-publication reservation enforcement,
engine-global/physical accounting, hostile decoding, production/concurrency and
independent assurance remain gates.

### 16.5.5 Held annotation baseline capacity at native publication

The actual invocation authority may attach one fixed bounded baseline-reservation
pool. Duplicate pools, foreign/cloned domain or pool handles and reopening after
stop refuse. Opening needs independent exact-true owner control, capacity
activation and preparation facts. This trusted coordinator facet is not a public
verb, write acknowledgment, storage backend or second writer lane.

Reserve only a validated §16.5.4 envelope for an actual current live document,
its original ordinary annotation binding/provider, source/set and authority/engine
context. Revalidate the complete ordinary pair and current known distinction under
§16.2.4. Exact-true authorization, scope, continuity, reservation and preparation
facts do not establish their own host truth. Admission copies the record and
checks fixed live/lifetime caps, complete record bounds, declared held-byte capacity
and the complete prospective root/counter floor before issuing a reservation.
Refusal changes neither root, ledger nor issuance. Finite bookkeeping is charged
before opening; each hold charges its record envelope plus future baseline bytes.

Keep staging/retained-evidence demand separate from the root slot. Every hold is
charged independently, including several holds for one document. The root has one
current annotationBaseline slot per document, so its held slot requirement is the
maximum of the current slot size and all held baseline bounds for that document,
not their sum. Different documents' slot demands accumulate. Include absent-field
overhead and maximum publication width in the complete current-root calculation.
Reserve one publication unit per hold, not merely per distinct document. Require
`heldUnits <= MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - currentPublication` with safe arithmetic.

The existing common final invocation boundary checks that floor against the actual
candidate before root/terminal bookkeeping and any clipboard-stage commit. All
eight closed native job kinds traverse it: compound, reversal, selection, line,
boundary, replacement, clipboard and annotation. A candidate that spends held
space or counter units is wholly notApplied; its root and reservations stay
unchanged. Clipboard refusal discards/restages the local continuation so its task
is not falsely marked applied; confirmed external clipboard effects remain facts.
Edits and undo/redo within the remaining envelope proceed without freezing the
document. Held binding disappearance, disposal or retargeting fails the floor.

Pool stop ends new reservations but preserves existing holds and final-boundary
enforcement. Invocation cancellation, result forgetting and quiescence do not
refund baseline holds. Explicit release requires the exact owned reservation and
independent exact-true owner control, obligation discharge, retention release and
delivery drain. Release debits its captured charge once; lifetime issuance never
recycles. Current host discharge truth remains a premise until actual write-ticket
and baseline installation/retirement integration supplies it.

[Scoped evidence](formal/baseline-reservations.md) covers 42 native annotation
capture/edit/reversal stages, sixteen positive/refusal job-kind cells, eight open/
32 reserve/sixteen release gate cases, twelve controls/twenty mutants with a passing
rewired baseline and authored conditional accounting/induction arguments. This
closes the native invocation floor subproduct, not ordinary annotation-save
admission, atomic baseline installation/hold transfer, every non-invocation
publication route or engine-global/origin/physical accounting. Actual host truth,

MELT, RED/USE/golden and STRIDE/LINDDUN cover forged/foreign holds, undercharge,

### 16.5.6 Actual annotation tickets and baseline holds

An explicit trusted coordinator operation may select guarded prelaunch capacity
binding for an existing annotation-export ticket. Only the checked shared writer
constructs its opaque claim from its actual private owner/ticket, retained artifact,
original ordinary annotation association and original native domain. Exact-true
owner control, preparation and historical artifact facts precede construction.
Source tickets, cloned handles, missing original associations, stopped tickets and
first-time postdispatch claims refuse. Repeated access returns the same claim.
No raw artifact bytes or new public token/verb are returned to ordinary recipients.

Materialize the exact captured artifact into a bounded immutable sizing descriptor,
preserving origin, source/set, context, full original binding/registration and
receipt-versus-ordinary binding generations. Preflight §16.5.4's future envelope
under the writer's actual version and baseline limits. Charge the copied claim
descriptor against the shared writer's held-byte headroom; later writer admissions
see that charge. The package-private claim facet observes the actual live ticket
record, not a copied status or a host-supplied application flag. Its sole checked
constructor callsite is the source writer; production package visibility remains
a refinement obligation.

Bind through the actual native domain's attached pool. Require that exact original
domain identity, current complete ordinary pair, whole annotation binding and
registration, unchanged prelaunch source/set and matching writer/pool serialized
version bounds. Construct the envelope from the private claim, not a caller-supplied
replacement. Copied claims and other-domain pools refuse even when their strings
match. A matching sizing-only hold is not a ticket link. A repeated binding returns
the same live hold without more issuance; stale unbound captures refuse without
recapture or relabeling. Separate claim construction and pool binding are not an
atomic ordinary-save admission operation.

Once claimed, launch requires a real link and a nonfaulted actual native authority;
positive host launch flags cannot override an actual native fault. A refused bind
cannot silently fall back to an unreserved write. Later native edits preserve the
linked historical capture rather than refreshing its bytes or attribution.
Bound claims pin actual source-writer ticket/artifact retirement in addition to
existing baseline and destination obligations.

Linked hold release requires §16.5.5's current control/retention/drain facts plus
actual ticket facts. A queued attempt must be stopped. A dispatched attempt must
have confirmed nonapplication, safe disposition, quiescence, no contradiction and
no destination-wide quarantine. In both cases its separate export-destination
reservation must already be released. Caller stop, supplied obligation-discharge,
quiescence alone, known written application or an unknown result cannot substitute.
Release ends that exact link once without recycling either writer or pool issuance.
Actual ticket retirement then removes the private claim and its writer-side charge.

Known-written attempts retain the hold pending qualified baseline installation
and safe hold transfer; those operations remain open. Claim construction does not
retrofit an export into ordinary save, install an export-reservation root, establish
whole-root coherence across supplied-root and native paths, or authorize a new
effect. Unclaimed explicitly authorized exports retain their earlier contract.
Actual provider/policy/discharge truth, atomic ordinary-save admission, all
non-invocation routes, public products, global/physical accounting, hostile decoding,
production/concurrency and independent assurance remain gates.

[Scoped evidence](formal/annotation-write-claims.md) covers 42 actual native
artifact-stage/ticket-binding cases, 8 claim/32 reserve/16 release gates, sixteen
actual application/disposition/quiescence cells, all six fact orders, sixteen
controls/eighteen mutants with a passing rewired baseline and conditional arguments.
One domain check mutant weakens both component checks; redundant stopped/disposition/
binding guards are not claimed independently mutation-sensitive. INS-01/03/04/07/08/
13 and PATH-05/12 distinguish claim creation/binding, held charges, refused launch,
unknown/written/nonapplication evidence, destination release and actual retirement.
MELT, RED/USE/golden and STRIDE/LINDDUN cover forged/cross-domain claims, stale capture,
fallback launch, quarantine bypass, premature refunds and private activity linkage
without content, paths, origins, contexts, identities or tokens in metric labels.
Installed telemetry, timing noninterference and new numeric SLOs are not established.

### 16.5.7 Qualified native baseline installation and ownership transfer

The checked writer coordinates qualified baseline installation with the actual
native authority in one synchronous serialized call. It validates the actual
claim/ticket, original native domain, current ordinary pair/full registration,
historical artifact and captured acknowledgment strength, then uses §16.5.3's
newest-eligible election. Sixteen exact-true publication/preparation/transfer/
retention facts precede preparation. Neither caller-supplied bytes nor one success
Boolean substitutes for the actual private producer and immutable artifact.

The writer creates a package-private short-lived installation certificate and
immediately consumes it through the native authority; no prepared root or
certificate escapes the supported coordinator operation. The certificate binds
the exact current before-root object, candidate, claim, pool, producing task and
actual knowledge objects. Native consumption revalidates live producer identity,
application/strength, serial, version and original descriptor; publishing/refreshing
must still select the unique newest eligible producer. Changed facts, foreign or
copied handles, native fault, stale roots and weaker or forged acknowledgment
fields refuse without changing the root or reservation ledger.

| Operation | Root/publication change | Pending hold | Producing evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publish selected producer | Only annotationBaseline and one publication advance | Consume this claim's hold | Retain its actual producer claim in native ownership |
| Transfer to already-current producer | No root/publication change | Consume this claim's hold | Existing producer remains pinned |
| Transfer to already-installed newer producer | No root/publication change; do not claim the older attempt became current | Consume the older claim's hold | Newer qualified producer remains pinned; original contexts and registrations must match |
| Refresh current producer metadata | Only its validated baseline metadata and one publication advance | No new hold or recycled issuance | Reuse the existing producer pin; current capacity may refuse |

Changed candidates must preserve every other root field, including authored
source/annotations, views, histories, bindings, source baseline and peers. Require
one safe publication advance. Recompute all remaining reservation floors after
excluding only the consumed hold, so its promised unit is usable and other holds
remain protected. Refresh has no consumed hold and cannot spend someone else's
unit. Already-current retries are unchanged and need no unused generation.

Preparation freezes the candidate and validates the metadata-only parser-journal
handoff before final bounded assignments. Existing valid committed source receipts
carry across the exact baseline/publication frame without being reissued or
relabeled as new source edits. Optional absence does not invent source evidence.
The final native transition installs the root, retained producer references,
claim transfer state and hold debit together under the existing serialized trusted
installation assumption; no effect, host callback, await or unbounded workflow
intervenes. Concurrent/native memory installation remains an implementation gate.

Native ownership must retain the actual producing claim, not only JSON origin
metadata. Precharge live/staged producer-reference sets under the pool's finite
lifetime issuance ceiling. Each successfully installed producer can add at most
one such reference; refresh reuses it. The writer keeps its actual artifact and
claim charge. Retirement checks the actual current native baseline and declared
binding history as well as supplied-root evidence, so omitting a baseline from a
supplied root cannot free its actual producer. Superseded unneeded tickets may
retire under the existing discharge gates; retained nominal references then become
nonreusable tombstones within the prepaid lifetime envelope.

Installation and hold transfer do not establish provider quiescence, destination
reservation release, external freshness, crash durability or source-current byte
equality. Those obligations and milestones remain separate. Caller stop or stopped
pool admission does not erase a separately qualified acknowledgment. Historical
artifact authority is required; current source/annotation disclosure is neither
granted nor a prerequisite for this internal bookkeeping operation.

[Installation evidence](formal/annotation-baseline-installation.md) covers 42 native
artifact/edit/undo/redo installation stages, all 65,536 gate combinations, seventeen
controls/fourteen mutants with a passing rewired baseline and conditional ownership/
counter/frame arguments. Source-claim/pool/continuity regressions remain separate
checks. No new public verb, native job kind or solver condition is selected.
Atomic ordinary-save admission, unclaimed/legacy and cross-context adoption,
failed/abandoned hold resolution, whole supplied-root routing, actual provider/
policy/package truth, public invocation/events, complete global/temporary/physical
accounting, hostile decoding, production/concurrency and independent assurance
remain gates. PATH-05/12 and INS-01/02/03/04/05/07/08/13 distinguish acknowledgment,
installation, transfer, producer retention, refresh refusal and parser evidence.
MELT, RED/USE/golden and STRIDE/LINDDUN cover forged/stale certificates, root-frame
intrusion, lost pins, counter theft and private savedness/activity linkage without
raw content, paths, origins, contexts, identities or version tokens in metric labels.

### 16.5.8 Private annotation capture preparation

Atomic ordinary-save admission requires preparation without first issuing a
reader artifact or writer ticket. The existing shared codec provides one private
annotation preparation slot per owner. Preparation validates the actual native
artifact and current exact-true capture/control grants, retains its exact root
identity and original lossless bytes, and reserves its bounded logical record,
one artifact slot and one future lifetime issuance unit. It returns only a
preparation handle, not an artifact, bytes, write permission or admitted ticket.
Preparation itself neither increments lifetime issuance nor publishes a root.

All competing source imports and source/annotation captures preserve the reserved
issuance unit; both capture kinds preserve the reserved artifact slot. Held-byte
admission includes the preparation's actual logical charge. Only one preparation
may be live; a second request refuses rather than replacing its owner or charge.
The complete preparation envelope must fit maxArtifactBytes and remaining shared
held capacity. Temporary native capture/copy peaks still require the parent
preparation premise; these logical bounds are not allocator or global-root-retention
bounds. No new numeric limit or public verb is selected.

Commit requires the actual owner, preparation and native domain, the exact same
current immutable root, a healthy native authority, current exact-true capture/
control grants and any required historical-source attestation. It installs the
exact prepared artifact once, changes the held preparation charge to the retained
artifact charge, spends the reserved issuance unit and consumes the preparation.
Unrelated codec work can proceed within the remaining headroom. Failed commit
leaves the preparation and reservation intact for explicit discard; no recapture,
implicit refresh or artifact issuance occurs on refusal.

Discard requires current owner control, including after native fault or disclosure
revocation. It releases only the unpublished preparation and reserved future units;
already-issued lifetime counters remain unchanged. A discarded/committed handle
cannot be replayed or interpreted as a reader artifact. This is not cancellation
or refund of an issued artifact, a dispatched write or unknown external effects.

[Preparation evidence](formal/annotation-capture-preparation.md) covers 42 native
edit/undo/redo stages, all 16,384 prepare and 16,384 commit gate combinations,
twelve controls/fifteen semantic mutants with a passing rewired baseline, and
conditional ownership/accounting arguments. The primitive is not yet composed
with ordinary-save writer/destination/claim/native-hold admission. That complete
transaction, current public products, host truth, package privacy, global/physical
costs, production/concurrency and independent assurance remain gates.
PATH-05/12 and INS-01/02/03/04/07/08/13 distinguish private preparation, held bytes,
reserved slots/issuance, commit/refusal/discard and later writer admission. Use
bounded reason classes, not payloads, roots, paths, identities or handles as metric
labels; STRIDE/LINDDUN include stolen quota, stale-root reuse, forgery and activity
correlation. Installed signals and timing noninterference remain unproved.

### 16.5.9 Ordinary annotation save admission

The checked ordinary-save coordinator composes private codec preparation, shared
writer admission and the actual native baseline pool before returning a task.
It takes the native authority's actual current root; no supplied replacement root
can admit work. The private normalized descriptor uses annotation-save/1 and
captured-annotation-save with the exact fields of the existing annotation-export
descriptor. The operation implies ordinary save, not copy export or SaveAs. This
is an internal semantic discriminator, not a selected public wire/request API or
new native invocation job kind.

Require the active ordinary annotation binding, known-distinct current source/
annotation pair, whole current provider registration, expected source/set/binding/
registration, current grants and the existing pinned, present-destination write
profile. Missing/absent/nonordinary targets refuse; separately authorized exports
remain separate. Derive receipt binding generation from the actual annotation
binding, not an export generation. The resulting receipt does not claim an export
reservation or binding activation.

As for ordinary source saves, ordinary annotation save uses the active document
resource owner and existing shared writer FIFO; it does not create an exportOrigins
entry, a second owner or a destination/publication root. Source/annotation writer
tickets still share destination ordering and execution headroom. This is not an
assertion that an external resource lock or distributed mutex exists.

Preparation creates no issued artifact or live writer ticket. The codec reserves
its bytes/slot/future issuance; private inspection returns only checked copies for
the trusted coordinator under current preparation/disclosure grants. Build the
exact future baseline descriptor from those bytes and original capture. Check
writer/origin/task/destination limits, separately charged claim storage and the
complete baseline envelope. Stage the hold through the existing capacity law on
a private ledger copy, including current root, original full binding/registration,
version-limit compatibility, remaining holds and publication units. Do not mutate
the live ledger during that trial.

Revalidate native health, attached pool ownership, exact root identity, claim and
pool counters/held charges before issuance. In the trusted serialized final
segment, issue the prepared artifact, install the actual writer ticket and origin,
activate its actual claim and commit the checked live hold. No callback, await,
provider effect, root publication or returned intermediate handle intervenes.
Success returns only after all are installed. Expected refusals before issuance
discard private stages without consuming writer/codec/pool lifetime issuance,
leaving the original root and live ledgers unchanged; the same origin may then be
used by a valid request. No already-issued identity is recycled.

An invalidated trusted final commit after issuance is a surprise: fault the native
domain, retain charged issued evidence and fail hard, not return a clean refusal

transition can cause that surprise between validation and commit. Production
atomic memory/crash behavior and supervisor recovery from violated premises remain
implementation gates; a JavaScript statement sequence does not prove them.

### 16.5.10 Terminally ineligible baseline holds

A pending baseline-capacity promise and the evidence of an applied write have
different lifetimes. An actual claimed annotation attempt whose captured required
acknowledgment is synchronized cannot later qualify consistently when its accepted
synchronization fact is failed or not-requested. Those are known incompatible
atoms, not unknown information: the existing join preserves either atom under
lower information and quarantines a different known atom. Captured requested
strength is immutable; a later registration or a different attempt does not
downgrade it. A write-only requirement, or ordinary acknowledgment with no captured
sync support, is not such a failure: written application can already satisfy it.

An explicit private cleanup facet may discharge that impossible future-baseline
hold only through the original actual native domain's attached pool and exact
live claim/hold through a bounded control view without reading/copying document
bodies or future-baseline payloads. Require the existing current owner-control, obligation-discharge,
hold-retention and hold-delivery-drain facts, plus actual dispatched/written
application, captured synchronized requirement, failed/not-requested synchronization,
safe disposition, quiescence, no attempt contestation, no destination-wide
quarantine and actual release of any separate export-destination reservation.
Ordinary active ownership has no transient export reservation to release. A
supplied failure label or timer cannot substitute for those private ticket facts.

Success removes only that hold and its charge, ends its link once and records
terminal-ineligible. Neither pool nor writer/codec lifetime issuance is recycled.
The actual root/publication, prior baseline, producer pins, write application,
acknowledgment facts, ticket, artifact and writer claim charge remain unchanged.
The transfer label fits the already-reserved descriptor envelope. The operation
does not label the write not-applied, mark it saved, install a baseline, upgrade
its guarantee, retire its producer evidence or authorize a retry.

Safe control cleanup is available after stopped pool admission, native execution
fault, content-disclosure revocation or provider unavailability when its own
current control/discharge facts hold. It contacts no provider and publishes no
root. Destination quarantine still refuses cleanup. Later contradictory receipts
continue to quarantine the retained write; they neither resurrect a released
capacity promise nor make the failed attempt eligible. Existing writer evidence/
artifact retirement gates remain independent. A later qualified installed producer
can supersede the retained failed attempt, after which ordinary actual-root and
retention checks may permit retirement without erasing current evidence.

| Actual state | Pending baseline capacity | Evidence and effects |
|---|---|---|
| Queued and stopped | Existing stopped-prelaunch discharge | No issued external effect; normal retirement still checked |
| Confirmed nonapplication with disposition/quiescence | Existing nonapplication discharge | Do not infer this from a synchronization failure |
| Applied, captured sync required, failed/not-requested sync, all cleanup facts | Explicit terminal-ineligible discharge | Applied-write evidence remains retained; no successful baseline |
| Qualified applied write | Qualified baseline installation/current or superseded transfer | Actual baseline producer remains pinned |
| Unknown, contested or quarantined effects | Retain pending promise | Stop, expiry, lost caller or elapsed time is not discharge evidence |

### 16.5.11 Initial native annotation restoration

The initial restoration profile composes a boundary-owned version 1 decoder/stager
with the actual managed annotation inventory and native publication owner. The
boundary seals typed native records; the engine consumer has no snapshot parser
or schema dependency and treats the attested producer proof as opaque data. It
applies only
to an explicitly active, known-empty target inventory: both live records and
lifecycle entries must be empty, with no retained annotation history participant
for that document. Missing inventory is unknown, not empty; retained-absent or
retired slots cannot be revived. Nonempty replacement/merge is a different complete
affected-set/history operation and is not performed implicitly by loading a file.

Reuse §16.2.1's explicit host document/source/record association shape. Require a
current complete basis binding the restoration context, native document, exact
decoded snapshot and full association map. Namespaces and serialized counters in
the file supply data, not authority or live edit preconditions. Current identity
continuity/registry compatibility, source evidence, target/mapping applicability,
history readiness and restoration authority remain independently attested facts.
The actual source revision/set, managed inventory and current source bytes are
checked against the actual native root; a file cannot select another document
owner or activate a binding by naming it.

The association map is injective over external aliases and native live IDs. Each
incoming incarnation must match its explicit native restoration association
exactly. Map every authored/current target source to explicit unique revision and
source-evidence rows, with exact byte counts and valid UTF-8 scalar boundaries.
The current source row must equal actual native source bytes and the snapshot's
current source evidence. Relevant historical rows and their current attestation
are mandatory for this evidence-complete profile; missing history does not cause
clamping, neighbor attachment, quote repair or deletion of the authored body.
Such input refuses intact rather than silently weakening its meaning.

Preserve accepted bodies, record order, authored target, current placement state,
independent point profiles, incarnation and positive version values. The native
reference accepts only exact values in its existing safe-integer domain and never
rounds or coerces a larger valid storage string into a handle/counter. This does
not select a product-wide integer width or make valid larger storage data corrupt;
unsupported native values preserve the input and current state. Explicitly attested
initial floors are installed in fresh managed slots, not accepted as authority to
roll back an existing live or retired record. No permission/provenance is imported.

Preparation owns immutable decoded data, source/identity associations, the finite
profile and target document dependencies within the plan budget. The normal private
entry point consumes it synchronously without exposing the plan or any raw root.
Final consumption rechecks actual domain ownership, target source/set/inventory/
binding basis, whole current proof, exact-true authorization/resource/companion and
membership facts, history compatibility and required historical evidence. Unrelated
peer changes need not stale the plan: construct from the latest root and preserve
those changes rather than reinstalling a captured collection.

For a nonempty accepted snapshot, install the complete records and present-slot
floors, advancing annotation set and collection publication exactly once with safe
arithmetic and current version capacity. Source bytes/revision, bindings, baselines,
owners, views, journals, peer documents and other fields are framed unchanged.
The actual native consumer independently checks the complete frame and existing
baseline-reservation floors. Existing valid parser-source receipt identities carry
through the metadata-only frame without issuing a source edit. Subsequent ordinary
annotation editing/reversal advances the restored floors; source undo preserves
loaded authored bodies under the existing mapping/history contract.

An empty snapshot against a known-empty inventory is validated unchanged without
requiring unused generations or publishing bookkeeping as a content change. Failed
association, syntax, numeric/profile, identity, authority, source/set/history or
capacity checks leave the input and live root unchanged. Restoration is initial
state hydration, not an authored create/delete undo group or a replay of file code.
Bodies and selectors do not execute; schema fields do not trigger remote retrieval.

PS-SA/DG/SC/SE/SB/RB evidence is restricted composition, not actual filesystem,
codec/durability/cryptography or arbitrary-attempt refinement.

INS-04/07/08/13 separate capture/encoding, queue, final launch, external attempt,
receipt, baseline applicability and unknown age; INS-03 governs recipient release.
Observe bytes and reservation/retention costs in declared units without payloads,
paths or tokens as labels. STRIDE covers wrong binding/forged evidence, stale
conditions, contradictory results and retry exhaustion; LINDDUN covers destination,
save activity and private annotation metadata. D06/D07/D15/D16/D20 retain the
concrete provider, clock, reservation, retention and receipt-schema decisions.

## 17 Execution, resources and shutdown

Requirements §§4.4/7.1–7.6/12.4 govern deterministic in-process transitions,
IF-01/04/05/13, PATH-12 and INV-07/11/12/15/16. Local publication is synchronous,
bounded and independent of executor choice. A host may run effects on its executor
or synchronously for deterministic tests; no Tokio/Rayon/runtime is required.
Moving deferred work onto a worker does not promote it into v1.

### 17.1 Effects, acceptance and supervision

An effect request identifies its originating operation, effect/attempt, typed
parameters, required capability/guarantee and relevant document/view/context
dependencies. A completion identifies the exact effect/attempt and what its
provider actually attests. Accepted event sequences determine reproducible next
state/effects/outcomes; allowed arrival orders need not produce identical results.
Time, permission change and failures are explicit inputs, not hidden I/O.

Host services use explicit requests/responses and capability inspection, not hidden
globals. Relevant enabled contracts include clipboard, file/dialog services,
timers, task spawning/cancellation, theme/accessibility preferences and diagnostics.
Language servers/other processes remain conditional or deferred under v1 scope,
not requirements inferred from this inventory. Missing services have explicit
unsupported outcomes; each supplied service declares its granted scope, guarantees,
limits, completion meaning and trusted supplier. Availability is not authority,
and a host acknowledgment cannot make an unprovided atomicity/durability true.

Keep control lifetime, cancellation intent, outcome evidence and applicability
as separate dimensions. Pure derived results require current context before
acceptance; old external writes remain historical evidence. Validate authenticity,
identity, attempt and payload bounds before protected completion service. Unrelated
or forged input cannot manufacture facts, consume an unbounded priority lane or
quarantine an honest provider by pretending to be a trusted contradiction.

For order-independent observations, evidence combination is associative,
commutative and idempotent. Contradictory trusted observations stay retained and
trigger scoped reconciliation/fault handling. Any lattice claim names its exact
evidence domain; it does not make payloads, histories or whole-editor state finite.
The concrete event/result product is D05/D23, not arbitrary flags or one success bit.

A completed caller observation retains what was known and disclosed at its stated
observation boundary. Later evidence may change currently queryable operation
knowledge, but cannot retroactively rewrite the delivered report or pretend the
caller had already received it. Access to that later evidence is a new authorized
observation. Distinguish producer evidence time, observation time and current
applicability rather than using a mutable historical success flag.

Supervision bounds restarts and escalation. Restart does not restore trusted
mutable state by assumption, authorize an obsolete attempt or make unknown writes
safe to repeat. For a confirmed provider contradiction, retain both observations,
exclude its contested baseline, stop that attempt and block incompatible destination
writes pending reconciliation. Expand isolation only when broader integrity is
uncertain, with explicit host escalation. Re-entry requires authorized revalidation
or replacement context, retaining relevant old evidence; not a silent identity reset.

### 17.1.1 Scoped native invocation cancellation

F18 cancellation resolves an existing actual invocation domain/ticket and its
complete original seven-field context. Require exact-true current owner control,
current control context, valid control scope and protected control readiness.
Native metadata-only lookup checks actual ownership and exact context, not a
caller-provided reference string. Current policy/continuity truth remains a host
obligation; tuple equality alone cannot establish it.

The Rust in-process `invocation-control/1` cancellation ingress accepts the fixed
2/4/3-field typed/dynamic envelope (`control-execution`, family index 17), operation
`request-cancellation`, and one out-of-band original opaque `InvocationId`.
Unknown/duplicate fields, wrong versions and inert/stringified tickets refuse
before native control. Installed discovery dispatch additionally requires the
engine's sealed declaration source and current discovery release; copied
descriptors confer no executable registration. Direct protected ingress does not
depend on discovery availability. Normalization and installed dispatch have bounded
optional service instrumentation; invalid input creates no native stop-service sample.

Cancellation does not require or grant content disclosure, source-write,
ordinary observer capacity, rich-result retention or capacity-administration
authority. It returns no roots, rich outcomes or participant inventories. Protected
ingress/service must remain bounded and attributable; supplied readiness is not
a proof of actual service, authentication or denial-of-service isolation.

Call the actual native pending-job stop only after those checks. Success sets
monotone stop intent; repeated pending requests are idempotent. It does not start
or settle the job, refund its reservation, retire a ticket, close an observer or
assert that external work is quiescent. Unsubmitted, foreign, retired, terminal
and running serialized entries refuse without new execution. No reentrant
preemption or interruption of native/provider work is promised.

If accepted stop precedes the selected local execution, actual scheduler settlement
preserves the root and records notApplied/stopped. If publication wins first,
late cancellation cannot change its applied/done facts or replay eligibility.
Engine faults retain Unknown/fenced handling, not a fabricated stopped result.
Useful stopped completion requires the existing reserved execution/outcome path
and actual scheduler service. Unrelated jobs stay eligible on the shared root.

Stopping observation remains a different operation. Producer cancellation does
not close observers; minimal phase remains pending until real settlement. Later
disclosure uses the observer's existing captured/current authority. Forgetting a
terminal result never reopens execution or cancellation.

[Scoped native evidence](formal/invocation-control.md) covers all ten admitted
native job kinds through fifteen forms, including selection/line/Unicode-boundary/
replacement, acknowledged paste/cut and owned container/scratch lifecycle:
240 gate/120 context cases, 30 races, 3,885 traces/10,890 edges, ten controls/twelve mutants with passing baseline and
conditional preservation/halting arguments. Existing execution/resource solver
conditions are unchanged (223/thirteen manifests), not a new engine-wide proof.
INS-01/03/04/08/13 and MELT/RED/USE/golden signals distinguish offered/accepted/refused
requests, stopped settlement, accepted-to-terminal age, protected saturation and
held/censored work. STRIDE/LINDDUN cover forged/wrong-scope/replayed control, false
quiescence, priority abuse and private activity/linkability; no raw tickets/contexts
in ordinary labels. Actual policy/protected service, all external effect gateways,
complete shutdown, remaining public schemas, concurrent/physical/production and
independent refinement remain. This does not close whole F18 or any D-row.

An acknowledged clipboard continuation preserves its provider fact/export when
scoped cancellation prevents its local edit. Local notApplied/stopped and confirmed
provider effect can coexist. Clipboard task stop is separate from invocation stop;
neither supplies provider quiescence. Keep the invocation pin through actual local
settlement and drained ledger retirement, and retain provider work until separately
attested quiescence and safe task retirement. Kind-set coverage does not prove every
payload/command variant, actual provider behavior or a global protected scheduler.

### 17.2 Independent envelopes and reservation integrity

Admission composes a host/authority envelope with permitted originating scopes
and operations. Define independent ceilings for memory/retention, processing,
concurrency/outstanding effects, fan-out and time. A scheduling cost estimate is
not a substitute for any of those ceilings. Work attribution follows parent/
origin through children, retries, aliases, document creation and workspaces;
none creates new quota or authority without a validated grant.

Preparation itself consumes the applicable processing/time/retention envelope;
work done before final admission/publication is not a free unbounded phase.
Coalesce redundant replaceable derived work where safe, preserving composed source
meaning, context and original-scope charges. Do not coalesce away exact FIFO save
captures, distinct authoritative observations or required evidence. Cancellation,
supersession and admission refusal remain explicit dispositions, not silent loss.

Before promising an atomic publication or effect submission, account for bounded
staging, mappings/history, retained captures and required completion/evidence
capacity. Use conservative bounds or explicit bounded staged acquisition when
cost is unknown. If required obligations cannot fit, reject or explicitly boundedly
defer before mutation. Never split the transaction or lower requested completeness.
Shared storage needs defined actual/estimated accounting, without whole-document
duplicate charge for an alias or invisible retention through a worker reference.

Hold reservations until actual obligations are discharged or transferred under
an explicit supported contract. Cancellation/expiry/observer loss is not release.
Separate outstanding-work release from still-retained evidence/history storage.
The existing source-cell and admission-counter models do not account for total
process RSS, arbitrary native allocation or uninstrumented provider CPU.

### 17.2.1 Resource profile validity

Each required resource coordinate declares its unit, accounting domain, applicable
scope and whether it describes reusable occupancy/reservations or consumed work.
Different units/domains are not interchangeable; scheduling cost does not replace
memory, concurrency, fan-out or deadline ceilings. A complete applicable profile
must identify the independent ceilings and inherited charges used for admission.
Missing demand evidence is not zero: use a conservative bound or bounded staged
acquisition before resource growth. Actual field names, limits and defaults remain
D06; clocks and milestones remain D22 rather than a reusable resource credit.

For each comparable coordinate and applicable scope, accounted use L, capacity C
and additional reservation D must satisfy `0 ≤ L ≤ C` and `0 ≤ D ≤ C − L` before
the added obligation is admitted. This is a mathematical validity relation, not
a selected public representation, allowance for arbitrary zero-valued profiles,
or a proof of actual memory use. The latter additionally requires actual use to
be bounded by accounted charge and actual added demand by D. Shared retention,
metadata and native/provider allocations require their declared refinement.

An eligible reusable charge R can be released only when actual discharge or a
supported transfer justifies remaining obligations within `L − R`, with
`0 ≤ R ≤ L`. Never refund consumed processing work merely because the caller
finished. A supported same-unit transfer preserves aggregate charge and ancestor
obligations while validating recipient capacity/current rights; this does not
require a transfer API. Descendant/retry work preserves inherited
`spent + remaining = quota`, not a fresh copy of the parent remainder per child.

For a fixed finite coordinate set, integer-valued occupancy within fixed finite
integer capacities forms a finite bounded product lattice under pointwise
min/max. This does not establish a lattice for editor
state or termination of execution. Context changes cannot conceal retained
obligations; adopted D06 capacity activation follows §17.2.2. Planned drain,
migration and retained interpretation contexts remain D35 refinements. Six local
SMT laws and four fault controls in formal/resource-profiles.md support these
conditional equations, not actual profile, allocator, scheduler or provider
refinement. Existing observation/security placements and disclosure limits apply.

### 17.2.2 Finite profiles admission and capacity activation

D06 is adopted: every enabled operation uses a complete validated finite resource
profile; absent coordinates or invalid/nonfinite limits do not mean unlimited.
The host may supply a supported profile, and reference applications may provide
measured defaults without exposing every coordinate as mandatory user setup.
Declare units/accounting domains and applicable host/authority/origin scopes,
including retained/accounted bytes, outstanding slots, edit/participant/fan-out
counts, declared work and separately specified time budgets. Logical bytes are
not process RSS and abstract work units are not CPU milliseconds. Actual profile
schemas and reference numerical values require their own validity/evidence.

All applicable hard envelopes constrain admission. Children, retries, aliases,
new documents or workspaces cannot create grants or reset inherited consumption.
Reserve conservative staging/mapping/history/capture and required completion/
evidence resources before promising work, or use bounded staged acquisition before
growth under the unchanged atomicity contract. Unknown demand is not zero.
Ingress/profile validation itself uses an already valid bounding context; proposed
limits cannot authorize their own unbounded parsing, validation or expansion.

For new atomic proposals, failure to fit rejects before mutation rather than
entering a generic implicit waiting queue, splitting publication or lowering
completeness. Explicitly specified bounded queue contracts remain valid, including
the adopted per-destination save FIFO; this does not change its captures, ordering,
capacity rejection or unresolved-effect retention. Optional work may degrade under
its declared partial/unavailable contract, never masquerade as complete analysis
or weaken a requested atomic transformation. Soft/adaptive targets may tune work
inside validated hard envelopes; they cannot expand capacity or authority.

Resource-capacity activation is validated against current charges, protected
reservations and applicable commitments at its serialized decision boundary.
Reject incompatible proposed profiles, including ceilings below retained charges
or a partition change that strands existing ordinary/completion commitments.
Keep the prior active profile and obligations on refusal; do not clamp accounting,
confiscate reservations, refund consumed work or silently cancel existing work.
Compatible changes preserve retained charges and inherited consumption. A planned
drain/migration, different accounting domain or clock context requires an explicit
supported lifecycle/refinement contract, not implicit activation behavior.
This rule governs proposed configuration changes, not a promise that a host losing
physical resources can always satisfy its former guarantees. Report unsupported/
unknown host service or integrity limits under the existing fault/lifecycle rules;
do not manufacture accounting headroom from physical-pressure observations.

Publish numerical reference defaults only against declared workload/corpus,
host/provider assumptions, accounting coverage and measurement uncertainty.
Measure offered/admitted work, useful outcomes, retention, pending ages, service
distribution, constrained-resource saturation and loss together. Fast refusal or
queue occupancy alone does not prove useful service, fairness or adequate limits.
Editor feature budgets are precedent, not transferable memory/latency guarantees.
D22 owns actual clock/deadline/service profiles; D35 owns separately supported
activation/drain context lifetimes. No scheduler, executor, preemption mechanism,
universal numerical preset or extra network/quota service is selected.

formal/capacity-admission.md records finite declared-charge reference checks and
conditional local laws. They do not establish actual allocator/native/provider
accounting, protected-service minima, deadline validity or measured defaults.

### 17.2.3 Shared native observation admission and discharged retirement

The selected native observation path composes §23.1.4's actual producer with the
existing complete finite capacity profile. One owned pool per actual invocation
authority charges every routed context against both fixed declared host/origin
envelopes before opening it. Do not infer a true origin hierarchy from recipient,
document, workspace or purpose. This reference does not cover all engine owners,
multi-origin ancestry or whole-host physical use. The lower-level observer is a
trusted producer primitive, not an alternate public bypass of shared admission.

Validate complete units, bounds and startup metadata; precharge worst-case fixed
profile/ledger frames and bounded reservation records in both byte envelopes.
Duplicate/foreign authority pools and cloned reservation references refuse.
Bootstrap and profile activation require explicit current capacity-activation
authority in addition to owner control. Ordinary context admission neither requires
nor grants quota-changing authority. No new scheduler, queue, service, public
reservation/acquisition variant or wire encoding is selected.

Use the actual producer's canonical local charge, including ordinary/protected
replies, phase-reference reserve, context and wait maxima. Reserve it plus one
ordinary context slot and one protected completion promise in both envelopes;
unknown/invalid demand is not zero. Each granted admission consumes one declared
admission step and child grant, not measured CPU or complete API-work accounting.
Resource refusal occurs before native context creation. The owned ledger supplies
its registry-ready premise only for this route; it does not manufacture host
retention, permission, clock or physical reservation truth.

Bind successful reservation to the exact actual context and check the resulting
producer charge. Known no-context setup refusal releases reusable occupancy only;
consumed work/fan-out remains spent. An exception/mismatch retains an Unknown
reservation and fences new pool admissions, without stopping producer work or
guessing safe release. Unknown recovery/authority teardown still requires a
separate supported actual discharge path.

Close, stop and expiry do not refund shared reservations. Require owner control,
delivery drain and retention discharge; retire the actual native context or verify
its independent retirement before releasing its bytes/ordinary slot/completion
promise. Outstanding waiter records block that native retirement. Independently
retiring a context is not an automatic shared refund, and foreign/duplicate
reservation handles cannot debit another owner. Startup metadata and consumed
coordinates remain charged. Actual allocator/drain truth is not proved by null
local lookup or host Boolean evidence fixtures.

Capacity activation uses the retained ledger and existing compatibility predicate.
Reject incompatible byte/slot/protected-floor/consumption shrink unchanged.
Compatible changes preserve spent quota; soft targets confer no rights. Preserve
the fixed clock/accounting context and original pool limits; migrations need their
own contract. Stop refuses new contexts without resetting charges, disabling
existing protected observation or cancelling/refunding native producers.

[Shared native evidence](formal/observation-admission.md) includes 30 boundary
cases, 24 retirement orderings/96 edges, twelve controls/fifteen mutants with a
passing dynamic baseline and conditional accounting/ownership arguments. Existing
capacity/resource conditions are reused unchanged (223 total/thirteen manifests).
INS-01/03/04/07/08/12/13 and MELT/RED/golden/USE distinguish offered/reserved/delivered
observations, occupancy, consumption, protected promises, quarantine and discharge;
STRIDE/LINDDUN challenge quota resets, premature refunds, wrong scope and private
attribution without raw IDs/handles as ordinary labels. Physical global accounting,
all-owner/origin hierarchy, actual identity/policy/clock/discharge, unknown recovery,
public schema, concurrency/native/production/independent refinement remain gates.
No whole D06/D35/F06/F19 or all-sections goal closes from this selected pool.

### 17.2.4 Complete parent intent preflight

Private owned preparation must check the complete normalized parent intent before
retaining a new plan or acquiring its interpretation lease. A payload fitting
maxIntentBytes does not establish that its enclosing kind/plan product fits.
For the current design-reference profile the unit is UTF-8 bytes of the complete
JSON serialization of that normalized product, including field names and wrapper
structure. This is a reference accounting unit, not a public wire format, Rust
layout, total allocation bound or new serialization requirement for hosts.
These preflights consume normalized inert data; hostile decoding remains a
separate boundary obligation.

Apply this preflight to native registration, scoped registration, relation/container
lifecycle, document lifecycle, Save As activation, completed source-load activation,
annotation-load activation and configured line preparation. Settings preparation
already checks its complete parent wrapper under §22.3.1.5. Existing per-product
request/value/profile/plan limits and scoped retained-reference-vector bounds
remain independent conjuncts; satisfying a parent byte bound cannot discharge
another limit. Submission repeats its own normalized intent check.

Section 22.3.1.8 additionally preflights a known settings candidate against the
actual parent's whole-root ceiling before retaining a new plan. This is independent
of configuration maxStateBytes and the complete intent wrapper: unrelated authored
source is not configuration state. Candidate construction precedes the reference
retention check; physical peak memory and production cost require separate evidence.

An oversized new preparation returns the existing refusal and leaves its issued
slot without a prepared plan. It preserves the native root, registration floor,
invocation accounting and existing interpretation holds; configured-line refusal
must precede new lease acquisition. The separately issued invocation remains
charged. A later admissible preparation on that ticket is not poisoned by the
refusal. Successful identical preparation retries reuse the same plan/lease;
submission retries across typed/dynamic routes remain the same pending invocation.
Capacity success is neither admission permission nor successful publication.

Keep accepted owner profiles immutable under the supported lifetime contract.
Verification may vary a generated test owner's limit to measure the exact boundary;
this is not a runtime profile-mutation API. Capacity activation and protected
retirement retain §§17.2.2–17.2.3. No new route, job kind, provider call or UI state
is introduced. F11/F16/F17 local preparation remains separate from substrate effects.

[Selected evidence](formal/preparation-envelopes.md) checks 48 typed/dynamic
boundary cases across eight paths, 32 preparation retries, 32 pending cross-route
retries, sixteen refusal recoveries, four successful configured-line lease cases
and eight assertion-killed source mutations after a coherent baseline. The scoped
registration retained-reference test independently isolates that bound from the
new wrapper check; its existing 32 mutation identities remain. INS-01/02/09/12/13
distinguish preparation refusal, held work, submission and publication without
payloads or private identifiers in ordinary labels. Existing conditional resource
laws remain scoped; no additional solver theorem, physical accounting, complete
public product, concurrent/crash or independent assurance is claimed.

### 17.3 Admission, service and pressure

The host derives allowed work classes from validated operation/access context and
guarantees—not untrusted priority labels, author claims, human/agent origin or
workspace names. Protect bounded completion/reconciliation/cancellation/revocation/
shutdown and minimal health/loss capacity from new speculative traffic. Protected
capacity is not freely borrowable unless safe reclamation/noninterference is shown.
Actual class enums, quanta and algorithms remain D06/D22.

Share remaining service by declared bounded cost and originating scope, with
progress for eligible admitted lower-class work under explicit host service and
finite/cooperative execution. Bounded queues and FIFO alone do not establish this
fairness. Do not claim native preemption or a numeric latency bound from service
assumptions; PS-UP's closed finite backlog does not prove open-load scheduling.

Target the constrained resource when shedding work: discard stale/replaceable
derived work, reduce optional presentation/diagnostics, defer or explicitly
truncate eligible analysis, evict eligible cache/history under consistent floors,
then reject/boundedly defer new work that cannot fit. This is obligation-aware,
not an instruction to exhaust every earlier step mechanically. Never erase unsaved
source/comments or required effect evidence, break history promises, promote
unauthorized work through aging or report partial analysis as complete.

### 17.4 Deadline and shutdown relation

Live deadlines use a declared local monotonic clock/epoch, separately from finite
work budgets and caller waiting. Profiles state queue/preparation/execution/end-
to-end start points, suspend behavior and invalid/unavailable clock treatment.
Check expiry at final dispatch/publication admission, not only timer delivery.
Children/retries inherit remaining limits; process instants do not survive restart
or support cross-host subtraction.

| Shutdown stage | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Unsaved-work decision | Expose structured save/discard/cancel choices for authored source/comments; no silent autosave/discard or mandatory UI dialog |
| Accepted disposition | Revalidate acknowledged versions before destructive disposal; stop new admission in the affected scope, not unrelated work by accident |
| Bounded drain/cancellation | Cancel replaceable queued work and reconcile accepted effects within the declared wait budget; retain actual unresolved obligations |
| Wait cutoff | Report outstanding/unknown effects to the host; do not infer quiescence, flushed telemetry, safe replay or completed persistence |
| Explicit forced close | Require current host authority and safe retained ownership/lifetime transfer for continuing effects; local discard does not undo issued writes |

The library does not terminate the process or promise crash/session recovery.
Bounded waiting is not bounded worker lifetime or native-code preemption. A host
decision wait need not freeze unrelated operations. Exact profiles and forced-close
result shapes remain D06/D08/D22/D23.

#### 17.4.1 Selected actual-domain ordinary-admission fence

The first-party ordinary-admission fence belongs to the actual invocation-domain
owner, not a UI, caller flag or working shutdown wrapper. This primitive is not
shutdown disposition acceptance. Its installation requires the original complete
domain context, strict current protected-control facts, exact current root identity,
no active native admission section or running/preparing invocation, and actual
parent headroom for one retained maxRootBytes frame plus the opaque fence token's
declared serialized units. An equal copied root or foreign domain cannot substitute.
Refusal leaves admission and parent accounting unchanged. Matching retry uses the
original root identity and returns the same fence without another debit; changed
intent cannot replace it. No wait cutoff, task retirement or regrant reopens it.

For the selected native paths, a fence denies new invocation issuance, first
invocation admission, source/annotation ordinary-save admission and commit of a
previously prepared source-destination admission. Pending authored publication
cannot proceed across it. Matching already-admitted invocation retries remain
observational; protected stop can settle that pending invocation without authored
publication, and its existing retirement still cannot refund the fence charge.
Actual native admission/commit sections exclude fence installation through their
fact-reading and commit boundaries and release only their original section token,
including on exceptions. A copied section token cannot release a live section.

Fault containment remains a different state. Existing eligible pre-admitted source
and annotation save tasks retain their immutable captures, current dispatch guards,
authenticated evidence and matching baseline installation. Protected baseline/
release bookkeeping retains its exact operation guards; it is not an exception
for fresh admission, SaveAs or rebind. The selected reference compares both save
completion orders without changing source, annotation bodies or their versions.
Work in another actual domain remains independent.

See [the admission-fence evidence](formal/admission-fence.md). Twelve controls,
fourteen coherent copied-module mutations, twelve strict-control cases, eleven
scope/identity cases, three exact headroom boundaries and four active-operation
reentry cases cover this primitive. These do not establish complete owner inventory,
shutdown consent/acceptance, eligibility of every retained dispatch, all native
entry/final-install paths, public F18 syntax, clock/provider/physical truth or
independent certification. Full authority shutdown must still bind those relations;
this primitive cannot report shutdown accepted or complete. IF-01/03/04 and
INS-01/02/03/04/08/12/13 retain existing admission, protected-progress, retained-
resource and effect distinctions without private identities as metric labels.

#### 17.4.2 Native owner attachments and protected progress

Native inspection additionally captures source/annotation read tasks, reader-owner
state and restoration/reader-writer attachment dependencies without acquiring new
payload pins. Actual owner-store reservations, local ceilings and operation-registry
state remain distinct. Empty task tables are not closed owners; unavailable
historical counters are not zero. Fresh reader and operation-registry acquisition
is fenced; original admitted delivery and safe cleanup remain available. These
attachments alone do not establish shutdown acceptance/drain.
Native owner reporting now also covers publication stream and retained source
command/receipt stores, catalog observation/registration-basis stores, discovery
with separately funded decoders, captured history participants, measurement pools
(including configured timing storage), and actual fence/wait retention. These are
native state/reservation/retained-entry projections, not declarations or inferred
closure from empty tables. Complete native-owner coverage is now gated by the
field census and funding reconciliation below, not a fixed false flag; this adds
no shutdown-acceptance authority.
Core invocation rows additionally expose original identity and native phase, intent
binding and retained-outcome availability under the existing work/capture bounds
and ledger profile. History journals/pins, search sessions/live results and authored
annotation records/live snapshots contribute actual owner/dependency metadata.
No aggregate parent reservation is inferred from local ceilings or entry counts.
Protected invocation stop requires the original installed fence and current domain
control, reuses native stop, preserves already-terminal results and retains original
input/effect obligations. It is neither provider cancellation nor whole-owner drain.
Native resource/root reporting additionally represents provider/codec/restorer and
catalog metadata, source preparations/export reservations, owned read/save origin
stores, continuity credit and current semantic-root size. Original shared-parent
reservations remain distinct from actual local accounting credit and logical root
payload size; none is an RSS claim or a zero inferred from missing information.
Both owned read-store families validate the exact original funded envelope before
protected retirement. Invocation reporting now reconciles all twelve native holder
families against their original ticket/capture and actual parent reservation;
per-ticket counts and bytes contribute to the invocation owner's separately funded
total. Generic outcome forgetting does not release command captures; compound and
created-layer results keep their existing dedicated cleanup ordering. Search-result
context lineage checks original issuer/hold identity, exact coherent parent and
unique consumer claims per native hold. Standalone context holds remain retained
obligations, not orphan errors. Its query-local visited-slot workspace is bounded
before allocation by existing work and capture-byte limits. Whole-domain drain
remains separate; these projections do not authorize closure.
The native disposition-acceptance entry now validates the current original cut and
acknowledged choices, binds explicit original save allocations, and returns
`NeedsSave` before fencing for missing, stopped or incompatible writers. It neither
queues a save nor infers persistence. It reserves bounded original inspection and
decision/binding metadata before accepting; matching retry retains the original
control without another debit, while changed consent/allocation/profile refuses.
The engine retains that immutable plan for subsequent document progress even if
the host drops its original handles. Fresh disposal coverage and qualified exact
baseline checks remain mandatory. Existing explicit wait initiation defines its
own host-clock origin; acceptance promises no end-to-end elapsed-time deadline.
Accepted-domain cancellation now has a fixed-size host-held original-fence cursor
and explicit per-step slot budget. Its finite stages visit original invocation
slots then original save slots once, without restarting at zero on each call.
Current domain control is required at start and every advance. Only pending local
invocations and replaceable queued saves are stopped through their actual owners;
terminal/unsubmitted tickets, original required source/comment saves and dispatched
effects are preserved. Original bindings use bounded native document lookup, not
caller-supplied readiness. Cursor completion means finished cancellation scan, not
shutdown completion or disposal. Blocked progress preserves successful prior counts
and does not silently retry unknown actions; unwind faults and blocks the cursor.
No publication, retention release, provider cancellation, wait renewal or numeric
default follows. Bounded optional actual timing covers start and advance; blocked
child errors are not recorded as successful cancellation service.
Accepted-plan retirement requires current owner control, explicit release/drain
premises and every original document no longer live. It releases only its exact
metadata reservation and leaves an absorbing tombstone: matching acceptance replay
and legacy document disposition cannot revive consent. Fence and wait reservations,
external effects, integrity faults and authored generations are unchanged.
Complete owner drain, fence retirement and public F18 assembly remain open.
Native inventory now has 38 primary roles, including logical-view rows, workspace
containers/membership dependencies, boundary captures/evidence and settings plan
lifetime references. Native gauges/limits are validated; issued floors and empty
configured owners remain distinct from closure. Boundary retained-copy bytes and
settings preparation references are not invented parent reservations. Workspace
membership reconciliation uses caller-bounded linear visited-slot storage.
An exhaustive coordinator-field classification and closed 38-role funding census
now underpin native inventory coverage. Exactly one original-owner row per role is
required. Parent-funded contributions, including decoder/context children, are
summed with checked arithmetic and compared with the actual retention ledger;
local credit, byte ceilings and semantic payload size are never substituted.
`funding` reports actual parent, inventoried and unrepresented bytes. Unrepresented
credit yields incomplete coverage; over-attribution or malformed census faults.
`all_owner_obligations` is true only for a reconciled native cut, including cuts
with unknown effects, active owners or lost-handle debt. It grants no mutation,
retirement, effect/quiescence truth or physical/foreign-owner guarantee. Historical
release preserves original funding/coverage; current validation recomputes them.
Host-owned invocation observation contexts now
register original context/ticket identity, exact declared charge and a weak private
host-object lifetime marker. Registry slot storage is included in the declared hold
bound and paid before escape. Existing service uses constant-time original-slot
checks; admission/reconciliation and retirement validate the registry's native
accounting. Explicit protected retirement refunds once and removes only its claim;
close/drop do not. Dropped-handle debt remains reported after policy/ticket retirement.
Private slot reuse cannot rebind retired contexts. Fresh opening refuses after the
domain fence; existing protected control/retirement retain their original guards.
Shared inspection storage includes its out-of-line native frame in byte
bounds; retained metadata does not hold document bodies or producer leases.
Native annotation-reader retirement now requires explicit admission stop, strict
current protected-control premises, no actual child/capture/restoration obligations,
no active owned-operation store, no reader/writer attachment and zero explained
reader occupancy. An active operation store must separately release its exact
configured parent charge; unrelated credit is not a substitute. Orphan occupancy
faults rather than being erased. Whole retirement drops native tombstones and
restorer registrations, installs an absorbing root-stamped closed state and
refuses fresh read/codec/attachment/registry acquisition. Inert host-held restorer
ports do not imply worker liveness or restore admission after closure. Semantic
editing and writer services remain independent. Protected cleanup does not consume
an authored publication generation or heal an existing integrity fault. Closed
reader inventory omits unavailable historical counters and its discharged writer
dependency; it is not whole-domain shutdown or shared-writer retirement.
Binding inventory validates the existing native provenance-release predicate
before excluding released historical descriptors from outstanding obligations.
It must not look up their legitimately retired producers as if still live. Actual
remaining producer rows are independently reported, and old reports remain as-of
metadata; this exclusion neither deletes historical content nor certifies drain.
The native shared pending-write/artifact owner additionally supports protected
retirement under its original installed funded fence and current exact domain
control. Both save admissions must be stopped. Actual tasks/artifacts, source
preparations/export reservations, binding/provenance claims and dependent readers
and operation-observer pools must have discharged through their own controls;
empty active stores do not suffice. Unexplained occupancy/continuity debt faults
rather than being zeroed. Retirement drops spent producer/origin storage and
root-stamps a closed state without refunding fence/unrelated credits, consuming an
authored counter or healing faults. Provider/encoder/catalog metadata remains owned
by the engine: this is producer-store retirement, not whole-resource/domain closure.
Fresh native-operation observer storage and context admission respect the fence;
matching configuration, existing query/reference service and protected stop retain
their original guards. Public F18/controller assembly and full owner coverage are
still required.
Native source/combined/coherent context pools, preparations, installations, retained
copies and internal holds, annotation snapshots, managed search and serialization
registration/basis/plan acquisition also respect the fence. Matching registrations,
existing reads, original invocation replay and protected stop/retirement retain
their existing guards. Retained acquisition refusal does not conceal accepted loss
in the original whole coherent context, including an omitted peer. Serialization
final admission refuses both changed and unchanged plans across the fence, without
clearing or mistaking the integrity latch.
Settings profile/retention acquisition, interpretation and write/definition/lifecycle
bases, initial installation, native/scoped plan capture and final admission now use
the same independent fence. Both changed and unchanged settings proposals refuse
without turning ordinary shutdown refusal into an integrity fault. Original
interpretation/basis reads, exact invocation replay and protected pool discharge
retain their existing guards and do not reopen admission or refund the fence.
Native catalog bootstrap, plan capture and final admission, fresh registration-basis
issuer/record acquisition and discovery owner/context establishment also respect
the fence. Matching original bases remain lookup service; retiring a record does
not permit fresh issuance across the fence. Fresh visibility evaluation remains
available for retained discovery queries. Refusing new context establishment does
not consume their prepared evaluation or confer establishment authority upon it.
Native provider/encoder/restorer registration, fresh save/continuity profiles,
artifact capture/materialization and annotation export admission are fenced.
Annotation restoration checks the fence at preparation and final admission, even
for an empty result. Already-restored read baseline adoption remains eligible
bookkeeping under its original validation and root-growth bounds; its counter
calculation preserves all other pending baseline-publication credits. Old provider
evidence, artifact reads, original write settlement and protected discard/retirement
remain available under their existing guards.

The native cut additionally records active resource associations, disposed-retained
bindings and source association history with their original opaque destinations,
provider incarnations and baseline save/read dependencies. Registry location is
not document editing liveness. Contested evidence remains visible; historical
ownership validation is distinct from fresh read/adoption eligibility. Identity-key
metadata and rows are capture-bounded; no baseline payload is copied. Other owner
families and complete shutdown acceptance/drain remain outside this checkpoint.

The Rust inspection/decision projection now captures actual document expectations,
shared writer/artifact identities and their original dependency edges under
declared record/byte/projection-work bounds. Independently authorized historical
release does not refresh the cut. Currentness also checks nonpublication writer
and technical-delivery state. Explicit source/comment choices carry acknowledged
version/policy/binding expectations, not movable IDs. Missing choices return
NeedsDecision with no fence or implicit effect. Other owner-family coverage is
explicitly incomplete; captured choices prove neither full save readiness nor
shutdown acceptance, disposition or drain. Host-held metadata is not a managed
producer lease or source-content snapshot.

Native document-disposition checkpoint: original independent source/comment
save/discard choices can drive retained disposal under their own installed fence,
with fresh disposal-coverage premises and exact acknowledged document expectations.
The discard-only route rejects save choices. The save route requires each
selected component's original admitted allocation from the original cut, qualified
acknowledgment and installed baseline for that exact capture. Matching historical
bytes/clean state alone do not satisfy it; substituted or absent allocations
refuse. The existing pending-baseline guard remains in force. No worker quiescence
or no-future-effects fact is fabricated from save readiness. Generic disposal
remains fenced, and retained history/resources and fence funding are not discharged.
Interrupted publication leaves both fences intact and emits unknown diagnostics.
Bounded post-fence native reports can now inspect represented obligations without
new producer pins. They are immutable as-of metadata, with separately reauthorized
release and explicit incomplete owner coverage, not a new consent cut or discharge
certificate. Already-activated Save As and explicitly adopted annotation-export
baselines use the same readiness checks; export acknowledgment without native
activation/adoption is insufficient. No activation/adoption authority is created
by this query. This implements document progress and partial native reporting,
not whole-domain acceptance/drain, forced close or public F18 assembly.

The native installed fence now additionally owns one cooperative wait with declared
host monotonic epoch/ticks and a finite tick budget; no elapsed-time default or
engine timer is implied. Initial report preflight and parent reservation precede
admission. Identical retries and polls do not renew the budget. Budget exhaustion,
clock loss/regression/epoch change or current authorized wait-end produce an
absorbing cutoff, not producer completion/cancellation. The original bounded report
is retained and independently reauthorized; capture failure is explicit and cannot
later be refreshed into success. Protected retirement requires current authority,
retention release and delivery drain, refunds only its original wait/report reservation,
and cannot restart the wait or reopen the fence. Native optional bounded timings
cover start, advance, report release and retirement. Full owner/controller coverage
and public F18 assembly remain open.

Rust implementation checkpoint: §17.4.1 now has an owner-local funded exact-root
primitive, with existing invocation ingress and core source/save publication
guards. Native source and annotation reservations settle in either order after
