activation; registration does not prove host callback termination or permit
mutation reentry. Every admitted event/state combination has an explicit transition,
duplicate, late-evidence, rejected-identity or fault disposition. D33 must finalize
the public identifier/schema/version and operation/outcome relation; this prose
does not pretend that the complete operation table already exists.

Results separate validation/admission, publication, effect evidence, control and
observation as in sections 1–10/17. A callback after commit cannot retroactively
reject it. Subsequent mutations reenter through a new validated request. Fail-fast
fault isolation stops unissued actions in the affected scope, not evidence about
already dispatched effects. Closed editor verbs are not a termination proof for
arbitrary registered native code.

### 22.1.1 Adopted semantic family catalog structure

D33 adopts typed contracts organized as semantic families with bounded declared
variants. The checked editor-wide inventory includes engine and optional
presentation contracts; §1.1 and formal/engine-ui-ownership.json distinguish them.
The engine facade exposes only its projection. Typed and dynamic invocation
normalize into the same semantic request and validation path; discovery describes
that path but does not authorize it. This chooses neither public identifiers,
Rust enum/struct shapes, a macro/generator framework nor a serialization format.

The categories have different responsibilities:

| Category | Permitted meaning | Forbidden inference |
|---|---|---|
| Query | Bounded reads, inspection, search/validation and recipient projection; may maintain declared derived/accounting/observer state | No authored-state mutation, provider I/O or hidden external launch; advisory validation is not later admission |
| Local command | An explicit mutation of source, annotations, view, lifecycle, configuration or control under its owning contract | Not every local command edits source or enters source undo; no implied external completion |
| Effect request | Explicit bounded authorized work requested from a named capability/provider, synchronously or on an executor | Acceptance/dispatch is not successful persistence/export, and executor choice adds no guarantee |
| Effect observation | Validated attributable provider facts or a contextual derived result under their different acceptance/retention rules | Original observer revocation does not erase necessary historical facts; stale pure results are not successful external writes |

Notifications report observations and are not another mutation entry point.
Trusted host policy and engine semantic configuration updates enter their declared
local control/context contracts. Focus and input-policy updates remain frontend
state; ordinary provider evidence cannot mint either layer's control authority.

The current semantic inventory is formal/operation-families.json: 28 families,
including 10 query, nine local-command, seven effect-request and two observation
families. The F-identifiers and variant labels are design-artifact references,
not public command identifiers or a frozen executable vocabulary. The inventory
cross-references eleven engine facade bullets and the separate presentation
paragraph in requirements §3.3, owning sections and
observation placements; that selected alignment is not whole-requirement semantic
coverage. Required surfaces remain required even when a host is absent; an honest
unsupported result does not satisfy required reference-integration evidence.

Source changes, accepted paste/composition and validated cut deletion all enter
the ordinary source coordinator, including mappings, history and other actual
participants. A compound source/annotation operation names all participants rather
than executing separate family calls as if atomic. Search navigation queries find
targets; selection commands apply them to explicit views. Resource load preparation
and local candidate activation remain separate. Save/cut workflows retain distinct
external requests, incoming evidence and later local decisions.

An incomplete query can return pending/unavailable or a bounded candidate; any
needed host work uses an explicit effect-request contract, not hidden query I/O.
Local pure preparation need not become asynchronous. Geometry/analysis families
apply only where enabled; they do not add mandatory executors or promote deferred
syntax-aware features. The host-facility family is a grouping of explicitly named
supported facilities, not arbitrary native callbacks, script execution or an
unbounded catch-all operation.

Every eventual operation descriptor must specify identity/version, argument/result
domains and limits, explicit targets/units/dependencies, authority, state/effect
footprint, admissible outcome/event combinations, duplicate/late/cancellation/fault
rules and observation/disclosure milestones. Applicable common contracts are
referenced once; variants declare material differences. Future registry activation
validates the complete affected catalog and retains admitted interpretations.
Unknown executable names/variants/versions reject before dispatch; caller-supplied
category/metadata cannot reclassify a mutation as a query.

Necessary validated historical effect evidence uses its responsible owner and
protected retention path, independently of ordinary new-work admission or the
original observer's current read grant. If protected intake cannot complete, an
explicit responsible host/owner must retain/reconcile it under the existing fault/
lifetime contract; a symbolic retention-required result is not physical storage.
Forged/misattributed inputs do not become trusted facts. Pure derived results
still require current context/rights and never directly author source.

formal/operation-catalog.md records the selected coverage/routing checks and local
symbolic support. Concrete verbs/fields, full totality, actual typed/dynamic Rust
adapters, queue/retention ownership and end-to-end execution/refinement remain D33
gates. Structure is adopted; API completeness is not claimed.

Protected service classification also survives family routing. Recognized bounded
cancellation/shutdown for admitted work, observation stop/revocation, downstream
task cancellation and reserved minimal status do not depend on ordinary speculative
capacity or current new-work enablement. Validate real target/retained contract,
authority, schema, bounds and capability before using protected service; names or
caller priority are insufficient. Preserve attribution/reservations through the
downstream request. New streams/grants, arbitrary status detail and host requests
stay on ordinary admission. Protected exhaustion reports unavailable minimal status
or retained responsible-owner control, never silently drops an existing obligation.
The catalog now has 87 variant labels, including the distinct minimal status variant.

### 22.1.2 Source reads and exact batch requests

F02 and F11 share an exact context bridge, not a transaction formed by a sequence
of calls. A source read identifies the authority, document incarnation and exact
retained source revision. A subsequent exact batch declares that context as a
dependency and must satisfy §§3–6 again at publication. A successful read,
snapshot selector or preview is neither a write grant nor a continuing read lease.

For F02 bounded-range, the request contains the supported contract interpretation,
host-established recipient context, exact snapshot selector, UTF-8 byte range,
source projection, destination/purpose and bounded delivery/retention profile.
The whole range must be valid and deliverable under the accepted profile; do not
silently clamp, round, truncate or replace an unavailable revision with current
text. Empty content is successful only for a valid authorized empty range.
Snapshot capture of current state through §12.8 first establishes an exact
reference; the read never reinterprets an
old selector as latest. Multiple independent reads do not promise a coherent
multi-document snapshot; use an explicitly identified version set when required.

Successful content results bind the exact source context, requested and delivered
range, coordinate unit and exact bytes to the currently authorized envelope.
Completeness means that range, not the whole document/workspace or semantic impact.
An owned raw snapshot handoff is disclosure of its entire readable extent at that
boundary; it cannot implement a narrower projection by convention. A mediated
snapshot-handoff returns a bounded non-grant selector and its permitted scope
under §§12.8–12.9; later content access repeats current release validation.
Source content/raw-source handoffs include no annotation bodies, hidden identities
or unrelated metadata implicitly. Mediated acquisition may explicitly request
annotation-only or combined scope with its own authority; the selector itself
discloses no annotation body.
Continuation, if a selected profile supports it, stays bound to the same exact
context and permitted domain and revalidates every handoff. Retention loss is
unavailable, not empty content or silent resynchronization. F02 line reads must
declare their line-origin, delimiter and terminator/EOF profile and resolve to
this byte contract; §29.2 selects the reference logical-line profile. Actual
conversion/API/implementation conformance remains a gate.

F11 exact-batch requests use all §3 fields, including complete per-document edit
records, expected bytes, explicit write participants, read dependencies, scope,
required guarantees and host-established authority/resource context. Variants
that derive targets (ordinary edit, replace, paste, composition and cut) additionally
supply their own validated interpretation/evidence; they cannot bypass this
contract or be admitted as exact-batch merely because they have replacement bytes.
Compound operations name every authored participant and required companion effect.
An implementation cannot treat a source-only request/result schema as permission
to omit selections, mapped attachments, annotations or history where required.

The successful publication result identifies the operation and committed local
publication context with the affected before/after source contexts and companion
disposition, subject to whole-envelope current projection. Validated unchanged
success records the decision without inventing a publication/revision/history
entry. Rejection and stopping before publication preserve the immediately preceding
authored state; an integrity fault is not proof of nonapplication. Notification,
status lookup and subsequent source handoff are separate observations: any can
be withheld/unavailable without changing a known publication fact. This operation
does not dispatch persistence, resource rename, clipboard or analysis effects.
Cancellation/deadline acceptance, replay and status loss follow §§6.2–6.5; no
automatic retry/rebase follows from a lost response. Public enum and wire names
remain unassigned; these are the semantic result alternatives under D05.

formal/source-edit-contracts.md records the field/result obligations, conditional
composition argument, private executable cases, observation placements and open
profile/refinement gates. It covers F02 bounded-range and F11 exact-batch at the
source boundary, not complete F02/F11 variant closure or concrete Rust adapters.

### 22.1.3 Scoped native contract discovery

The semantic product `contract-discovery/1` refines F01's existing list, inspect
and advisory-enablement variants. Common fields are `contract`, `operation`,
`context` and `profile`. List adds `limit` and optional `continuation`; inspect
adds a scoped `entry`; advisory enablement adds `entry`, `variant` and explicit
advisory `target`. Owner-resolved discovery contexts bind a coherent accepted
registry and permitted projection. Section 22.1.5 separately supplies a scoped
owned native acquisition/issuance boundary over attested catalog cuts; actual
registry/schema truth remains a gate. Neither extends F02 source/annotation scopes.

List returns bounded permitted entry references, versions and execution categories
in stable visible-domain order, with a context/query-bound opaque continuation.
Inspect describes permitted variants, exact versioned input fields/semantic domains,
possible outcomes, declared capability requirements, cancellation/limit profiles
and optional title, description, category, aliases and bindings. Schema references
must identify the actual registered contract and exact variant, not a similar name.
Withheld descriptive/schema fields are omitted, not empty or unsupported by inference.
Duplicate entry/variant references refuse rather than select by registration order.

Descriptive metadata is not executable registration or authority-bearing policy.
Treat its text as literal untrusted data, with no implicit evaluation, callback or
provider fetch. A displayed alias/binding does not become an invocation route unless
explicitly admitted through its executable registry contract. The artifact family
labels and fixture strings do not select public identifier encoding, Rust types or
a wire format. Required integrations remain required despite an honest unavailable
descriptor; metadata cannot stand in for complete handler/schema conformance.

Enablement is a separate target-bound advisory result, not embedded stale state
inside inspect metadata. Never relabel withheld or stale advice as established
disabled; both may use the common recipient-safe unavailable result. A changed
target can invalidate advice without invalidating unchanged
registry metadata. Positive advice is not proposal validation, admission, authority
or a reservation; invocation still validates current schema, rights, dependencies,
capabilities and bounds. Discovery cannot mutate authored state or launch effects.

Current release binds context, profile, recipient, purpose/destination, registry
basis and policy/continuity, plus current grant, retention, liveness and bounded
transfer. A richer policy cannot enlarge an old capture; a narrower policy cannot
release old richer facts. Pages advance only through the permitted visible domain.
Continuation stays with that exact context/query; loss or activation cannot silently
switch the registry, reveal hidden slots/counts or fabricate an empty catalog.
Bound actual registry scans, variants, schema/presentation values, retained contexts/
cursors and transfer before admission. Opaque reference knowledge never grants use.

formal/contract-discovery.md supplies selected native-catalog and actual routing
composition, current release, paired projection, pagination and mutation evidence.
Actual registration/schema truth, all-family type/outcome/handler correspondence,
context/cursor issuance in this normalized helper, native identifier/codec/
compatibility profiles, concurrent activation and physical accounting remain gates.
Section 22.1.5 supplies separately scoped ownership evidence. No new runtime component or
execution mode is introduced.

### 22.1.4 Native source range and logical line products

The source-query/1 product refines F02 bounded-range and line, alongside the existing
snapshot-handoff products. Common fields are contract, operation, snapshot, document
and profile; bounded-range adds lo/hi, and line adds a zero-based line index. The
document is an exact authority/document/incarnation and the opaque context resolves
its captured source revision. Unknown interpretations/fields, invalid coordinates
and unavailable selectors refuse; no clamping, latest substitution or implicit I/O
repairs a failed read. Source/annotation scope and required version-set parent gates
remain §§12.8–12.10, not another authority path.

Range content returns exact owned bytes, requested range, unit, context and source
reference. Line content separates exact body/delimiter byte spans and owned bytes,
with the requested index, context, unit and source reference. §29.2 governs empty/
trailing lines and CRLF/LF/CR without normalization. Do not add total line counts,
document length, annotations or raw root handles incidentally. Complete unit or
recipient-safe unavailable are the products; authorized internal diagnosis remains
separate. A CRLF-interior byte remains a canonical range coordinate, not a body
column. Read success grants no mutation or continuing lease.

Source acquisition owns the finite root/input-extent/content/reply profile with
the captured root. The root must fit; changing defaults cannot reinterpret that
context, while current capacity can still deny handoff. Annotation-only capture
does not require this source profile. Querying the held root uses current release,
and required parent-member validation is not bypassed by a member selector.
All metadata and bytes obey the same whole-envelope bound and current permission.
The reference scans bounded canonical source; an incremental index, exact physical
charges and real service guarantees are separate obligations.

[Source product evidence](formal/source-products.md) composes the actual registry,
version-set gate, logicalLines and readRange helpers: 1,869 line/10,819 range oracle
cases, 32 direct/64 registry/128 parent gate cases, 48 paired comparisons, 45 controls
and seven mutants. Logical/native field selection does not freeze wire/Rust codecs
or prove actual issuer/policy/root truth, concurrency, physical accounting, full
projection profiles or implementation refinement. Point persistence is unchanged.

### 22.1.5 Owned native discovery contexts and cut boundary

The owned-contract-discovery/1 reference refines F01 context acquisition, opaque
entry/variant/cursor/target issuance and protected retirement. One bounded reader
registry belongs to an actual healthy native publication domain; it is not an
authoritative command store or executable handler registration. The existing
contract-discovery/1 list, inspect and advisory-enablement products are unchanged.

The accepted registry/schema producer supplies a complete cut, bounded literal
metadata, complete current visibility and approved order, with independent strict
attestations and current authority/interpretation. Copy preparations into single-use
packets bound to the actual root and full authority/engine/recipient/purpose/
destination/policy/continuity/profile. Accepted registry/schema/handler truth and
coherent target projection/evaluation remain producer obligations, not consequences
of Boolean flags, field-name correlation or native root ownership.

Capture permitted entries/variants and schema/presentation/advice ceilings. Each
query needs a fresh root-current cut, current owner/release grants and captured/
current metadata intersection. Changed permitted values or narrowed facets refuse
the old envelope; new grants/entries cannot expand it. Hidden-only changes and
unrelated native activity need not stale unchanged permitted metadata. Projection,
acquisition and release stay outside publication guards and leave native authored
state and producer ownership unchanged.

List/inspect stage context-local opaque entry/variant/exact-query cursor references
and whole bounded replies before installing selectors/issuance. Raw command IDs,
native epochs and target bases are not envelope fields. Permitted literal schemas
are data, not an interpreter or executable aliases. Bound dense plain JSON bytes,
depth/nodes, row/packet/capture/reply sizes, contexts/preparations/selectors and spent
lifetime issuance independently. Inert producer values are a reference premise;
this is not a hostile decoder or physical-memory sandbox.

Inspect never embeds enablement. Capture a separate opaque target only with
established binding/equality permission. Advice also needs its actual issued
reference, current equal attested target data, current attested advice and captured/
current advice permission. Unknown is not false. Later grants cannot retrofit a
target into an old context; target changes may stale advice but not metadata.
Positive advice never replaces current execution router/authority/dependency checks.

Matched-scope authority/interpretation loss or native fault stops the context.
Protected owner stop clears payloads/selectors without refunding issuance; wrong
scope cannot stop another owner. Explicit retention/delivery discharge precedes
retirement, and a spent-domain marker prevents budget reset by reader replacement.
Atomic staging here is sequential reference behavior, not concurrent/crash proof.
Reuse INS-01/03/04/08/09/12/13 and existing interface/pathway instrumentation; raw
private IDs/paths/epochs/target bases/metadata are not ordinary metric labels.

[Conditional evidence](formal/native-discovery.md) covers 42 native stages,
252 traversals, 504 inspections, 924 advice releases, 16,384 preparation/32
acquisition/48 release vectors, 32 selected paired worlds, 23 controls and 32
semantic mutants in four exact banks with passing baselines. The §22.1.3 normalized
checks remain. Actual registry/schema/handler and advisory-target truth, all-family
types/products, wire/remote, host facts, measurement/packages/apps/physical/global/
concurrent/crash/independent gates remain. Only this context boundary closes, not
whole F01/D09/D12/D33/D35 or the all-sections goal.

### 22.1.6 Selected builtin handler declaration source

For the six existing annotation-authoring/1 and history-reversal/1 operations,
derive discovery descriptors inside the actual reference-handler modules from
their private request declarations. Export parameter-free immutable metadata:
common/variant fields, declared outcome forms, named execution-profile constraints
and descriptive cancellation requirements. These are logical declarations, not
complete value codecs, executable schemas or live enablement. The fixed producer
must match the engine-only variant inventory; no caller registry, factory,
ownership label, keymap or UI mode selects its handlers.

Bind internal command identities to the discovery owner's actual authority and
engine. The internal tuple spelling is not a stable public command ID. Trusted
owner inspection may obtain bounded independent rows to derive complete current
visibility facts; recipients still use §22.1.5's scoped opaque contexts/selectors.
Built-in preparation discharges only accepted-source/schema-description origin
for these declarations, not permission, current interpretation, visibility/order,
resource, retention or advisory-target truth. Those existing gates remain required.

Carry a private source marker from the prepared root/scope-bound single-use cut
into the retained context. Each current query cut must match its origin before
selector staging. Reject generic lookalikes even when projected bytes match, and
reject built-in cuts as replacements for generic contexts. Preserve the generic
producer port under its original external premise; it is not upgraded by this

### 22.1.7 Handler bound outer schema profile

The explicit owned-contract-discovery/2 profile extends §22.1.5 with a bounded
JSON Schema input description. The /1 profile keeps its original descriptor
shape and fixed F13/F14 source. Both profiles use the same owner, finite context/
selector capacities and spent issuance; switching profiles cannot reset a budget.
The full captured context, including profile, binds cuts, selectors and queries.
Wrong-profile requests refuse without stopping an otherwise valid context.

For /2, an input description may retain the legacy contract/variant/fields shape
or use exact contract/variant/coverage/schema fields. Coverage is
outer-structure-only. The schema names JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and uses oneOf
over nonempty disjoint contract-constant branches. Each branch requires its exact
outer field set, disallows additional fields and declares outer JSON types and
fixed operation/profile discriminators where the actual handler fixes them.
The descriptor contract identifies the metadata product; branch contract constants
identify the accepted request products. Neither is a newly assigned public ID.

The fixed /2 producer adds F16's existing semantic-settings and supported-registry
variants. Ten forms come from the declarations used by actual settings normalizers
and registration-wrapper guards: ordinary settings, layer lifecycle, scoped
settings, definition activation, native registration, scoped registration and
document serialization metadata (§22.3.1.6) and scoped definition activation
(§22.3.1.7), scoped layer lifecycle (§22.3.1.8) and scoped serialization metadata
(§22.3.1.9). The native serialization
expectedSerialization field is
an integer with minimum 1 and maximum Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER in this private
reference profile; nested serialization semantics remain runtime checks.
Registration is supported-registry, not a new catalog variant. Unlike the complete
selected F13/F14 variant sets, this F16 description is partial: compatible analysis/
provider activation remains unspecified here. No unknown variant may enter it.

All schemas are inert bounded metadata. Apply the existing JSON byte/node/depth
limits before finite schema recognition. This profile admits no references, custom
keywords, executable callbacks or remote loading; it adds no general validator to
the editing core. The outer schema does not specify nested values, indexed opaque
reference vectors, current authority, dependencies, capability availability or
semantic acceptance. Runtime preparation/publication remain authoritative.
Qualified internal terminal publication/control pairs come from the common
invocation machine; they are not complete result codecs or disclosure promises.

Current/captured disclosure intersection, private built-in origin, attribution,
protected retirement and whole reply bounds remain §22.1.5–§22.1.6 obligations.
No handler registration, effect dispatch, UI preference or semantic generation
changes merely because a client inspects the description. CMP-02, IF-01/07 and
PATH-02 retain discovery; INS-01/03/08/09/12/13 distinguish profile refusal,
schema coverage, capacity pressure and release without raw schemas/IDs as labels.

The handler-owned declarations use the following existing contracts and fields.

workload defaults. Runtime checks retain scalar/nested validity, actual opaque
handle identity, exact current state, applicability, authority and resource bounds.

The older schema recognizer retains its vocabulary. Only /3 additionally accepts
this fixed ordinary-edit schema, matched exactly against its known declaration.
No arbitrary schema language extension, remote reference retrieval, callback,
handler registration or executable metadata is admitted. Schemas and qualified
terminal-form descriptions neither establish enablement nor guarantee disclosure.
Public nested value/reference codecs, selector-to-invocation binding and Rust/API
signatures remain separate contracts.

The existing F01 owner/cuts/source-origin/current-release rules govern /3. Capture
and current schema permissions intersect; later broadening cannot expand a captured
ceiling. Wrong profile/context or malformed/copied selectors cannot poison another
valid context. Explicit observed authority/metadata loss stops the old context;

retention/delivery discharge and nonrefunding issuance. Generic lookalike cuts
cannot replace builtin source origin. Metadata/advice queries leave authored root

sensitivity controls do not establish handler registration truth or execution.

### 22.2 Typed scope and deterministic resolution

Each setting declares its owner, type, legal scopes, composition rule,
dependencies and sensitivity. Distinguish source/serialization semantics,
view/input preferences, analysis contexts and host restrictions. Resolve legal
preference layers separately within each owning layer under §1.1, from
library defaults to host defaults, language, explicitly applicable workspace,
document and permitted view/input overrides. Multiple workspace memberships do
not pick document semantics: require explicit association/ordered profiles and
reject incompatible equal-priority inputs. Focus/open order is not a tie-breaker.

Reject unsupported keys/types and invalid combinations before activation; unknown
authority-bearing data cannot pass as decorative metadata. Themes use framework-
neutral semantic style roles with declared provider-specific presentation choices
in frontend/view support, not theme state or widget-specific types in the core.
Hosts register supported commands, language
assets/services, decorations and event listeners through documented trusted Rust
extension points. Each public extension point states executor/thread-safety,
ownership, lifetime, invalidation, failure and resource obligations. D33/D34/D43
must define those concrete contracts; registration is neither an invariant bypass
nor permission to run a callback inside publication. Listener failure after commit
cannot change its outcome; subsequent mutation is a new validated operation.

Scalars replace. Lists/rules replace unless their schema declares stable
composition. Maps merge only at declared keys with each key's rule. Absence
inherits; removing an override reveals lower layers; reset-to-library-default is
an explicit value. Do not concatenate capabilities, providers or commands.
Host restrictions constrain resolved preferences and are not overridable layers;
forbidden requests reject rather than silently broaden authority or claim an
unsupported guarantee. Readable configuration is not trusted executable policy.

Frontend keymaps distinguish bind, block/consume and fallthrough. Removal permits lower
lookup; fallthrough bypasses that layer's applicable default; block stops lookup.
Resolve equal-rank conflicts and command/prefix ambiguity or reject activation.
No arbitrary predicates, recursive key remapping or raw-key replay is added.
D34 captures the concrete setting/keymap schemas and dependency classifications
with separate owners. Optional binding suggestions accompanying command metadata
are frontend profile data: engine command identity, discovery and admission do
not depend on a binding or active interaction mode.

### 22.2.1 Native configuration inspection and typed resolution

The semantic product `configuration-query/1` refines F07's effective-configuration,
permitted-origin and capabilities variants. Requests bind `contract`, `operation`,
scoped `context`, explicit `target` and `profile`; value/origin queries also name a
registered `key`. Return coherent permitted values, permitted origin references or
accepted capability declarations under current release. Capabilities are not live
probe results or grants. Unknown/withheld/stale data is unavailable, not a guessed
default, empty permission set or inferred unsupported implementation.

Project origin identities rather than expose raw private workspace/layer references.
The origin product declares permitted-only coverage; an empty list does not prove
absence of hidden contributions. Bind recipient, purpose/destination, target/context,
profile and policy/continuity with current authority, retention/liveness, configuration
basis and bounded transfer. Old captured facts cannot expand under later policy or
escape narrowing. Context/selector issuance and all native domains remain gates.

Registered schemas supply type, legal scopes, composition/default, dependency impact
and sensitivity under §22.2. Required incompatible equal-priority inputs reject
activation even when a higher override would mask them. Structural map equality
does not depend on object insertion order; ordered list values remain ordered.
Lists replace unless an explicit supported profile declares composition. Maps merge
only at declared keys with each key's rule. Removing an override exposes inheritance;
reset contributes the library default explicitly. A new explicit origin with equal
effective value is not automatically a complete no-op. Host restrictions remain
outside and stronger than the preference hierarchy; settings metadata cannot mint
authority. Neither focus nor membership enumeration selects workspace semantics.

formal/configuration-products.md supplies typed scalar/list/top-level map resolution
and current query/projection evidence. It does not select public keys, tab/indent/
host defaults, recursive merge/rule profiles or complete schema/sensitivity admission.

### 22.2.1.1 Owned native engine settings inspection

The selected native-engine-settings-read/1 profile connects the three
configuration-query/1 variants to §22.3.1.2's actual initial declarations and
layer-activated configuration. Typed/dynamic F07 tuples carry exact `arguments`;
arguments have exact `contract`, `operation`, `context`, `target`, `profile` and,
except for capabilities, `key`. Context and target are actual context-local opaque
references, not raw target/layer identities or copied lookalikes. Unsupported
families, versions, UI verbs, extra fields and malformed normalized arguments
refuse. This is a native product, not a remote encoding or stable Rust API.

A trusted preparation binds the actual private engine owner, current settings
basis, complete disclosure scope and bounded visibility facts. Scope has authority,
engine, recipient, purpose, destination, policy, continuity and profile. Facts name
an actual declared target and exactly one row for every registered setting, with
separate visible/value/origin/declaration permissions and an explicit permitted
subset of actual effective origin IDs. A capability-disclosure flag is separate.
Completeness, permission and policy validity are host-attested premises; schema
sensitivity is explicit metadata and never grants access. Copied roots, packets,
pool handles or references cannot substitute for actual owned preparations.

Acquisition consumes a current one-use cut and captures only the permitted
projection. Retain the captured ceiling. Current release requires a fresh cut for
the same scope/target, current grants, continuity/liveness/retention, bounded
transfer and an unchanged captured permitted projection. Broadening cannot enlarge
it; narrowing or a changed visible value/origin/declaration refuses the old read.
An observed bound authorization/scope/continuity/liveness/retention gap permanently
invalidates that context. A current cut showing narrowed permission or changed
captured projection also invalidates it. Regrant or later value restoration cannot
resume the old context; acquire a fresh frontier. Malformed or foreign requests
cannot invalidate another context. Transient resource/transfer/reply pressure or
request cancellation refuses the query without itself proving an authority gap.
Invalidated contexts retain their charged slot until retention/delivery discharge;
they may then retire without pretending they were still active.
Unrelated target changes may proceed. A stale prepared cut cannot be refreshed or
reused. Hidden differences outside the projection do not appear in its values,
origins or declaration list; timing/resource noninterference is a separate gate.

Effective-configuration returns a newly owned bounded value. Permitted-origin
returns only context-local minted origin references, with permitted-only coverage;
empty output is not proof of complete absence. Map fields retain the selected
profile's per-field origin structure. Capabilities returns permitted accepted
setting declarations with key/type/domain/scopes/composition/sensitivity, excluding
the default. Declaration rows follow accepted schema order, not visibility-fact
enumeration order. Declaration permission must cover the entire returned type, including
literal enum members. This list is not an exhaustive supported-feature inventory,
live probe, provider guarantee or grant. Unknown/withheld/stale remains unavailable.

Finite profiles bind the engine settings profile and bound packets, contexts,
origins, lifetime issuance, packet/capture/reply/request/context/selector bytes,
input nodes/depth and held logical bytes. Reserve the actual parent's remaining
logical budget before opening the pool. Packet retirement and context release do
not refund lifetime issuance. Stop prevents further reads; final retirement requires
explicit retention and delivery discharge. Faults fence disclosure but must not
block protected cut/context cleanup. Closed pool retirement releases its charge
and leaves a spent marker, not a reopenable empty registry. Reads do not publish
roots, change source/history/UI state or consume mutation invocation slots.

[The reference evidence](formal/engine-settings-reads.md) checks six products,
fifteen gate/eight scope cases, twelve budget cases, twenty-two controls and
twenty-two assertion-killed mutations after a coherent baseline. Four added
REL-SETTING conditions cover absorbing observed invalidation and the unobserved
frame, with two satisfiable weakened-rule witnesses. Totals are 274 conditions
across fourteen manifests, 60 baseline. Existing current-gate/capture-meet and OUT
projection laws retain their abstract scope; none is a solver-to-JavaScript or
actual host policy refinement proof.
INS-01/03/08/09/12/13 cover cut/acquire/query/stop/retire and safe parent occupancy.
Keep raw keys, values, identities, selectors and origin references out of metric
labels. Mutable definition/policy/association activation, actual policy/consumer/
membership truth, remaining F07/F02/F19 products/events, public codecs/Rust,
physical/concurrent/crash and independent refinement remain gates.

A selected read profile has exact `engineProfile`, `maxPackets`, `maxContexts`,
`maxOrigins`, `maxIssued`, `maxPacketBytes`, `maxCaptureBytes`, `maxReplyBytes`,
`maxRequestBytes`, `maxContextBytes`, `maxSelectorBytes`, `maxInputNodes`,
`maxInputDepth` and `maxHeldBytes`; numeric fields are private nonnegative safe
integers, not measured production defaults. `engineProfile` is §22.3.1.2's complete
finite profile. Fact records have exact `target`, `keys`, `capabilities`; each key
row has exact `key`, `visible`, `value`, `origins`, `declaration`, `originIds`.
Flags are Boolean; hidden rows grant nothing and carry no origin IDs. Context
labels are nonempty scalar-valid strings. Capabilities, like origins, explicitly
reports permitted-only coverage, including when the returned list is empty.

Derive the three existing F07 argument forms from immutable declarations consumed

The native owner retains current scope, captured ceilings, projection, actual
target, original handles, release and absorbing observed-loss checks. A refused

not a new semantic variant, public command ID, wire/Rust token format or mutation

without treating resource metadata as a document read context.

One bounded registry belongs to the actual healthy native domain/authority/engine.
Use §22.3.3's read-only catalog validator without requiring source disclosure,

preparation covers both actual catalogs exactly once, with closed provider/resource
tuples, Boolean visibility/descriptor facts and a contiguous approved visible order.
Bind the actual current root and complete authority/engine/recipient/purpose/

packet once; copied, foreign, stale or spent packets refuse. Bound abandoned

### 22.2.2.1 Observed resource read invalidation

The resource-catalog reader retains observed loss in its actual owned context,
not merely in a per-call Boolean. Once the issued context, complete disclosure
scope and recognized exact request envelope are bound, explicit false current
authorization, scope permission, continuity, liveness or retention invalidates
delivery. A current visibility cut showing loss of a captured slot/facet or a
changed permitted value also invalidates it. Clear delivery data and all dependent
entry/continuation bindings. Regrant or actual native metadata value restoration
cannot revive that frontier; acquire a fresh context under current rights.

Malformed envelopes, copied/foreign contexts and mismatched disclosure scopes
cannot invalidate another context. Non-Boolean/missing host facts refuse without
asserting an observed loss. Temporary resource/transfer/reply pressure or query
cancellation alone refuses the query without invalidating its context. Profile
specificity matters: these roles do not redefine every provider or F01/F19 stop
signal. Explicit owner stop still requires its original control authority.

Invalidation closes delivery but does not retire the context, refund lifetime
issuance, release the registry's fixed logical reservation or discharge any
provider/producer obligation. Final context retirement still requires independent
retention and delivery discharge. Supervision may count invalidated retained
contexts, not expose their identities or private ordinals to recipients. Loss of
one context's retention does not itself invalidate another context's distinct hold.
Do not infer propagation to every affected scope from one bound observation;
actual policy/lifecycle invalidation delivery remains an integration obligation.

operational truth, crash recovery and independent assurance remain separate gates.

### 22.2.2.5 Parent funded resource catalog queries

Connect the existing resource-catalog registry reservation to its actual
invocation owner before publishing the registry handle. If current parent usage
is H, the native registry's declared reservation is R and the parent ceiling is M,
require R ≤ M−H before adding R. A refusal installs no registry or spent lease;
another fitting admission may still succeed. Keep one fixed private funding lease
per domain lifetime. That lease is not a recipient selector, a grant, a generic
allocator or another public operation. Registry retirement requires all native
contexts/preparations discharged, no active decoder, and current protected owner/
retention/drain authority. Refund R once; keep the spent lifetime marker. Neither
stopping a read nor transient decoder cleanup refunds that retained reservation.

The existing typed/dynamic resource-catalog arguments now enter one actual native
owner decoder. Preserve the original context, entry/continuation and prepared
visibility packet; copy ordinary request/scope data, never opaque contents. Lazy
access to the shared native declaration avoids an initialization cycle without
introducing another declaration source or changing accepted products. The private
packet still binds the actual current root and complete scope at native dispatch.

Before input copying, borrow the fixed classification amount K against the same
parent. Let B be min(caller request-byte ceiling, parent intent-byte ceiling).
After capturing valid finite limits, reserve seven B-sized logical frames against
remaining parent headroom. They cover envelope, authority, canonical request,
limits, descriptor, current facts and reconstructed native request. Independent
node/depth limits remain. Capturing current facts reads only the fixed release
field descriptors: missing/undefined is unknown, accessors refuse without getter
execution, and unrelated bookkeeping is not traversed. Truthy non-Booleans cannot
become grants. These are in-process inert-data bounds, not hostile proxy/native
code containment or physical allocation measurements.

| Decoder phase | Allowed accounting and exit |
| --- | --- |
| Idle funded registry | Retain R; reject foreign/closed/faulted owners without borrowing. |
| Classification | Retain R+K; reject invalid limits or insufficient next-stage headroom. |
| Workspace and native query | Retain R+K+7B; exclude recursive decoding, ordinary native entry and retirement while borrowed. |
| Normal or caught-fault completion | Refund only K and any admitted 7B through the protected finalizer; retain native contexts, cuts, selectors and spent issuance. |

Under the serialized trusted-ledger premises, the sum never exceeds M: each
addition is checked against current remaining headroom, and the finalizer
subtracts its actual temporary tally rather than restoring an old absolute total.
Fixed phase transitions and finite bounded capture/native work establish
conditional per-call termination. This is not a whole-engine bounded lattice or
host service-time theorem. A violated trusted refund invariant is an internal
integrity fault, not an ordinary unavailable result or a claimed successful refund.

Dispatch only to the existing owner query and validate its existing reply against
the original request. Normal malformed/foreign/unsupported/capacity refusal
returns the existing unavailable product without poisoning another context.
An unexpected decoder fault fences that reader pool, not the editing domain or
provider. With an intact ledger, protected cut disposal, stop and actual retirement
remain available after the finalizer. A late fault after native page installation
retains the installed selectors, consumed cut and spent issuance; it cannot
pretend to roll them back. The caller's already-known context supplies cleanup
ownership. Source/annotation roots and external effects remain unchanged.

[Resource read evidence](formal/registration-reads.md) retains the original native
case populations and adds owner funding, exact headroom, typed/dynamic decoded
list/continuation/inspect, named-fact, reentry and fault controls. The reader has
28 controls and 49 assertion-detected mutations in seven banks. Four fixed decoder
fault stages include a late case with two installed aliases. The old local
issuer-marker removal is now blocked by the parent's spent lease and is recorded
as a passing guard-blocked control, not counted as a mutation detection. The
shared invocation checker has 24 controls and 34 mutations. No new module, command,
profile, solver condition or numerical production default is introduced.

IF-01/02 and PATH-02 retain the same semantic boundaries. INS-01/03/08/09/12/13
distinguish registry admission, classification/workspace charge/refund, current
release, local fault and final native discharge. MELT/golden/RED/USE reuse those
populations and logical units; STRIDE/LINDDUN/hazard cases include forged leases,
parent overcommit, premature refund, scope substitution and hidden retained work.
Raw handles, metadata, identities and fact packets are not ordinary labels.
Full frozen qualification and endpoint adoption remain required. Resource-profile
discovery, complete facade products, host policy/physical/global accounting,
concurrency/crash refinement and independent assurance remain separate gates.

### 22.2.3 Trusted host command bindings

Requirements §11's command extension point is a trusted in-process Rust binding
above the authoritative coordinator, usable headlessly as well as from a frontend.
It is not a keymap, document instruction, native plugin loader or interpreter in
the core. A binding pairs one immutable bounded command descriptor with its exact
owned handler/required assets. Activation, lookup and invocation cannot combine
a descriptor from one incarnation with code from another. The resource metadata
registry in §22.3.3 is not this command binding and does not prove it implemented.

The supported binding contract contains the following semantic products. Concrete
Rust representations and public identifier/result syntax remain L02/D33/D43;
none of these roles is an authorization token by possession.

| Product | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Binding identity | Owning host/engine domain, explicit command key and fresh non-confusable incarnation; built-in engine identities cannot be shadowed by a host registration. |
| Descriptor and handler | One retained pair with versioned bounded argument/result declarations, explicit target/dependency and effect meanings, supported refusal/cancellation/fault behavior and declared execution/resource profile. Descriptive titles/aliases/binding suggestions do not select code or grant rights. |
| Activation expectation | Exact expected prior binding incarnation, or known absence for creation. Duplicate/conflicting keys or aliases and stale expectations reject before activation; iteration, focus and registration order do not resolve ambiguity. Replacement installs a complete fresh pair, never edits a held old pair in place. |
| Execution ownership | Declared host executor/affinity with serialized calls per binding in the base profile, finite outstanding captures/requests/emissions and retained descriptor/code/asset ownership. No implicit concurrent callback, cross-thread borrowed mutable owner or blocking callback inside an engine transition. |
| Invocation capture | Original binding incarnation, explicit targets, bounded owned arguments, execution context and lifetime hold. Resolve and validate this complete capture before calling the handler; do not look up a newer same-named handler when delayed work resumes. |
| Withdrawal and retirement | Withdrawal fences new binding acquisition. A captured but not yet executed invocation must pass the declared current applicability/authority checks or refuse, without switching handlers. Existing admitted engine requests retain their original intent/outcomes. Retire code/assets only after actual handler exit and all required interpretation, task and delivery holds discharge. Cancellation/timeout/withdrawal alone is not that witness. |

Run the handler outside publication, read handoff and protected accounting guards,
without lending a mutable coordinator/root. Each emitted query, proposal, mutation
or effect request reenters its ordinary typed/dynamic facade contract with current
authority, exact dependencies and budgets. A host workflow consisting of multiple
calls is not an atomic edit; use one supported compound plan for a local atomic
multi-object edit. Callback computation and its permitted host facilities remain
trusted-host execution, not new engine verbs or a proof of arbitrary Rust halting.
No document, schema, discovery description or dynamic identifier may install code.

Thread affinity and serialization must be enforced by the host binding adapter.
Cross-thread handoff requires owned data and the actual Rust Send/Sync obligations
of the values/handler being transferred or shared; the engine interface does not
infer those properties from a descriptor. A separately supported concurrent
handler profile must define its concurrency/retention bounds and safety contract;
the base contract does not require one. Actual executor service, callback failure
containment and native preemption/isolation remain host evidence, not guarantees
from a cancellation flag or finite emitted-request count.

A failure before any engine admission produces only the binding's declared
refusal/fault. A later handler/listener failure cannot relabel an admitted engine
request as unissued, reverse Applied or erase external-effect knowledge. Preserve
each actual invocation's outcome and cleanup obligations; subsequent requests are
new admissions. Unexpected binding integrity failure fences affected new lookup/
invocation while retaining held pairs and required evidence. Replacement/restart
cannot reset identity, silently retry an unknown effect or unload running code.

Command metadata/current discovery must bind to the same original pair and current
permitted projection. Existing fixed first-party F01 profiles are not implicitly
extended with host descriptors. The supported facade/discovery integration and
native binding implementation still require L02/E01 evidence; this subsection
defines their semantic obligation, not an installed dispatcher or a new profile.
Language assets retain §§18/22.3; decorations retain frontend §§19–20; listeners
consume bounded current-authorized observations under §12, outside publication.
None gains a second mutation interface through this extension point.

The preservation argument in formal/context-handoff.md instantiates existing
capture/current-validation/retention laws and distinguishes the remaining concrete
binding evidence. IF-01/03/07, PATH-01/05/12 and INS-01/02/03/08/09/13 separate
pair activation, host invocation, facade admission/publication, withdrawal and real
discharge. Handler identity, names, arguments and asset paths are not ordinary
metric labels; optional diagnostics cannot execute handlers or grant capabilities.

### 22.3 Staged activation and retained work

Prepare/validate scope resolution, command contracts and compatible provider,
grammar/query assets outside publication. Any preparation effects remain explicit
and authorized. Validate expected scope/configuration generations and atomically
publish the coherent affected set at a bounded local boundary without I/O or
arbitrary callbacks. Superseded candidates cannot replace newer activation.
Failure leaves a coherent previous profile or declared degradation, not half a
required combination. Unrelated scopes continue; cross-scope invariants enlarge
the activation unit only to their actual dependencies.

Retain the admitted command/schema/configuration interpretation for in-flight
work, but revalidate current rights and affected dependencies at acceptance.
Accept explicitly compatible results or reject/recompute; never reinterpret old
payload under new semantics. Cosmetic changes need not invalidate unrelated work.
Dispatched effects retain original contracts and late evidence even if a command
or provider is removed. Bound retained contexts; refuse/drain/isolate where safe
reclamation is unavailable. Do not unload code in use or assume revocation stopped
external effects. D35 selects concrete retention and activation-failure behavior.

Separately, relevant frontend keymap/mode activation cancels its pending chords
explicitly; consumed prefixes are not replayed under the new map. This is not
an engine activation participant or a joint engine/UI transaction. Frontend IME
sessions follow section 20, not reconstructed key events. Inspect effective values
and origin/precedence within their owning layer, and
generation within disclosure limits. Rollback is a fresh validated activation,
not restoration of old authority/generation or source-text undo.

Conformance checks deterministic ordered resolution, legal scopes, same-rank
conflicts, workspace ambiguity, atomic failed/superseded activation, current-rights
non-expansion, chord cancellation, stale results and late evidence. Composition is
ordered, not necessarily commutative and not a global lattice. Bound depth,
registrations, listeners and retained generations. Record content-safe resolution,
activation and degradation at the registry/provider interfaces; never log raw
configuration, command arguments, capability secrets or document labels. Existing
finite gates are partial freshness/authority evidence, not a complete resolver or
extension safety proof.

PS-CH now checks a bounded reference handoff under these existing rules, including
actual finite text/mapping/inverse operations and diagnostic perturbations. It
does not define the concrete command/schema compatibility relation or retention
profile; see §27.6 and formal/context-handoff.md.

Preserve required held interpretations; insufficient retention refuses activation.

Complete identity requires no unused publication/version or retained old context.
Rollback is fresh validated activation, not reuse of old generations or authority.
