Mapped namespaced attachments reuse declared range/point transformation laws
with affinity/deletion disposition. Namespaces organize producers, not authority.
Mapping may be undefined/detached and never proves semantic target survival.
Annotations, diagnostics and proposal targets retain distinct authored/derived,
history, applicability and disclosure rules. No bookmark feature or public lens
API follows merely from those examples. Source narrowing keeps original identity
and coordinates; read context is separate from permitted writes and current
capabilities. Ambiguous/stale/cross-boundary scope rejects the whole publication.

### 26.1.1 Owned selection and literal ordinary edit products

selection-edit/1 refines F12 set-selection and line/document logical endpoints,
plus F11 literal ordinary-edit. Common fields bind invocation, exact view/document
incarnations, source revision, expected selection generation and accepted profile.
Set-selection supplies anchor/head/affinity records and primary index. Endpoint
movement supplies line-start/end or document-start/end and an explicit extension
Boolean. Ordinary-edit supplies literal replacement text and mapped/carets-after
post-selection intent. These fields do not select public wire/Rust encoding or
complete the character/word/page/visual command catalog. Section 15.5 separately
specifies owned search-result selection and current replacement view companions.

The named explicit-positional-selection/1 profile preserves §28.45's nonempty
merge, direction and primary rules. Identical same-affinity carets deduplicate;
opposing-affinity and interior/boundary carets remain explicit. Display order does
not resolve insertion conflicts. The derived source batch must satisfy §4 or refuse
wholly; explicit agent batches are never normalized by this selection rule. This
uses existing positional mapping with explicit point affinity and outward nonempty
boundaries, not content identity or an implicit global UI default.

Owned preparation captures all affected view/source dependencies and stages actual
positional maps. Source/annotation publication and attached-view source/selection
contexts form one complete private candidate; current rights, read-only coverage,
membership, source/selection generations, stop and resource predicates revalidate.
No new or changed peer view is silently skipped; unrelated current state is not
restored. Readable read-only source can still support pure selection changes.
Pure selection creates no source revision or source undo entry. An equal-byte
replacement with a selection effect is an applied view publication; full identity
still preserves generations after validation. Section 6.4.1 adds actual equal-byte
annotation mapping publication without fabricating source revisions or undo entries.

[Selection product evidence](formal/selection-products.md) checks 1,536 normalization,
1,024 gate and 48 endpoint cases, 49 controls and eight mutants through actual map
and source/annotation helpers. A deliberate bridge counterexample shows the raw
source-reversal helper does not update view contexts; §14.7 supplies its native
explicit-profile bridge. Other view/movement/indentation/native/Unicode/geometry
profiles, replay/outcomes/events,
all companions and physical/implementation refinement remain gates. No existing
source-only proof or green aggregate report closes those obligations. Point-target
persistence is not changed by this view-selection profile.

### 26.1.2 Simple line indentation and generated newline products

line-edit/1 refines F11 ordinary-edit under explicit-prefix-line-edit/1. Its closed
actions are indent-lines, outdent-lines and insert-newline. Common fields bind
invocation, exact view/document incarnations, source revision, expected selection
generation, named profile and explicit accepted settings. Revalidate current
settings and interpretation as well as ordinary source/view gates at publication.

Line shifts accept a nonempty ASCII space unit or one tab, and a positive tab
width. Each selected logical line is shifted once; reverse ranges have the same
footprint. Nonempty selections exclude a line beginning at their upper endpoint;
carets include their line, including empty EOF. Both endpoints must be valid
logical-line positions: CRLF interior refuses. Indent prepends the unit unchanged.
Outdent reduces leading ASCII space/tab columns by the unit's width, floored at
zero; emit spaces for a space unit, tabs plus residual spaces for a tab unit.
Preserve the longest common leading byte prefix and replace only the differing
suffix. This is an explicit text operation, not syntax validation/formatting or
a claim that mixed-prefix indent/outdent are byte inverses. Native history retains
the actual inverse. Tab-column measurement is not byte position or visual geometry.

Generated newlines explicitly choose LF/CRLF/CR and none/copy-prefix indentation.
Replace each selection with that delimiter and optionally leading ASCII spaces/
tabs from its starting line before the lower endpoint. Do not copy future prefix
bytes, trim existing content or normalize other endings. Origin carets finish
after inserted bytes. Literal insertion/paste remains literal. The existing
new-document LF policy and host-supplied loaded-document insertion policy remain.
No universal numeric indent preference, key binding or grammar service is added.

Derive one canonical simultaneous batch or refuse unresolved insertion conflicts.
Reuse current annotation and all-attached-view participants, exact revisions,
write scopes, capacities and one complete ordinary publication/history group.
Identity still validates without fabricating a group. Bound targeted lines, total
prefix bytes, actual before/after indentation columns, unit bytes and derived
request/edit bytes under captured finite profiles. Tabs can make a linear
current+unit column estimate wrong; validate the actual resulting prefix. Current
tightened work caps cannot expand a prepared invocation.

[Line-edit evidence](formal/line-edits.md) composes actual ordinary/native history
helpers: 256 independent prefix-oracle/96 newline cases, 512 final gate combinations,
55 controls/eleven mutants. INS-01/09 interpretation, INS-02/07 publication,
INS-06 reversal, INS-11 handoff and INS-08 pressure retain MELT/golden/USE/RED and
STRIDE/LINDDUN coverage without lexical telemetry. Full movement/Unicode/geometry,
grammar indentation, actual configuration/native/replay/physical/concurrent and
all-companion refinement remain gates. Point storage is unchanged.

#### 26.1.2.1 Owned semantic settings for line edits

The private configured-line-edit/1 product under configured-prefix-line/1 uses
the same three line actions and F11 ordinary-edit typed/dynamic routes. It binds
invocation, document/view incarnations, source revision, expected selection,
profile and configuration. Configuration names an exact registered target and
closed key map: unit/tabWidth for shifts, delimiter/autoIndent for newlines.
Only registered source-domain values with the required line types/ranges apply.
No key spelling, focus, filesystem location or implicit workspace search grants
meaning or authority. Current read/use authority binds the complete execution
context and that document/view/action/target/key map with exact-true facts.

Prepare from actual native settings; capture schema/restriction/association epochs
and the target's source-domain generation, then lower through the existing line
helper. Bound the copied normalized request and inner intent before issuing a
charged interpretation lease owned by this invocation. Retries retain the original
footprint. A settings preparation and configured edit cannot share a slot, and
another valid line plan cannot replace the captured plan at submission.

Publication revalidates current exact-Boolean producer facts, authority, retained
interpretation, epochs and actual resolved values. Supplied lineSettings cannot
override the configured product. Configuration ABA and selection changes refuse;
unrelated target/domain/document progress remains intact. Preserve all ordinary
source/annotation/view/history companions. A valid no-op checks dependencies but
does not require an unused version. Cancellation/fault does not discharge held
interpretation: protected retirement releases the owned lease without refunding
lifetime issuance. Closed pools stay closed. Explicit line-edit/1 remains supported
without semantic configuration; no public setting-key catalog or wire ABI is fixed.

[Configured-line evidence](formal/configured-line.md) supplies 28 controls,
seventeen malformed/sixteen budget/ten argument/ninety current-fact cases and
eleven mutation kills, preserving sixteen legacy editing controls. Common
cancellation covers 24 forms/twelve kinds. IF-01/03/07 and INS-01/02/03/08/09/12/13
retain existing ownership and instrumentation. Actual applicability/policy,
complete consumers, public codecs, Rust/physical/concurrent/crash and independent
refinement remain gates; existing solver conditions retain their original scope.

### 26.1.3 Unicode logical movement and deletion products

boundary-command/1 under unicode-logical-edit/1 refines F12 logical-movement and
F11 ordinary deletion. Bind invocation, exact view/document incarnations, source
revision, expected selection generation, owned exact-source boundary evidence,
unit, direction, positive count and extension intent. Units are grapheme,
word-start and word-end; directions are forward/backward. Significant words are
default UAX word segments containing Alphabetic or General_Category Number,
not punctuation/space/symbol-only segments. This separates word significance,
word-boundary segmentation and binding policy; no implicit dictionary, locale or
identifier tailoring is added to §29.2's pinned Unicode profile.

Traverse strictly directional endpoints, saturating at BOF/EOF. A first
nonextending nonempty-selection collapse consumes one count; remaining steps
traverse. Extension keeps anchor, primary association and explicit affinity.
Collapsed movement may leave a scalar position inside a cluster. Implicit
deletion from a cluster interior refuses rather than deleting a partial cluster
or guessing expansion. A nonempty explicit selection deletes its exact extent
without extra traversal; delete with extend=true refuses. Origin deletion carets
finish at deletion starts. Colliding derived deletions refuse canonically as a
whole. Explicit byte edits remain independent of these derived human commands.

Character movement uses the grapheme grid, not raw word boundaries: a degenerate
flag/ZWJ fixture distinguishes them. Significant-word endpoints must be compatible
with the grapheme grid or the inconsistent profile result refuses; do not silently
intersect/rewrite the raw segmentation or assert a universal subset theorem.
Current boundary profile/liveness/retention and exact view/source/selection,
annotation/peer and write-scope guards revalidate through the existing coordinators.
Pure movement changes no source revision/history; deletion publishes one complete
source/annotation/view group or none. Current viewports are preserved.

Bound source bytes, boundary/word counts, boundary JSON bytes, total steps across
all selections and derived JSON bytes. A cluster count alone is no byte/work cap.
Finite ordered vectors/counts give a local traversal horizon; they do not prove
provider complexity, global scheduling or categorical completeness. Retained
exact-source evidence is not a permission grant. Native/provider/issuer/policy/
retention and complete-companion premises remain distinct from vector checks.

[Unicode and command evidence](formal/unicode-commands.md) executes all 853 pinned
grapheme/1,944 word corpus cases, eight controls/five mutants with ICU4J 79.1
Unicode 18 data, a default-word rule evaluator and explicit UTF-16/UTF-8 conversion.
Dictionary behavior is distinguished by supplementary fixtures even though it
passes the official finite corpus. This is reference-tool selection, not an engine
dependency or a universal/independent Unicode proof. Actual command composition
checks 19,200 grapheme movements/4,800 deletions, 96 prose-word movements/48
deletions, 2,048 gates, 43 controls/eight mutants and native undo. INS-01/09/05,
INS-02/07/06/11/08 retain MELT/golden/USE/RED and STRIDE/LINDDUN coverage without
lexical telemetry. Production/incremental/chunked providers, page/visual/width/bidi,
native/replay/outcome/event/physical/concurrent and all-companion refinement remain
gates. No annotation-storage or global keymap policy changes.

### 26.2 Cross-object semantic claims

Plans may include unseen documents/workspaces, nonwritten dependencies and
authoritative unsaved content. Host-loaded closed-file snapshots identify their
resource/context and cannot overwrite existing unsaved state during planning.
Represent symbol identity/binding separately from spelling and object identity;
no universal symbol naming scheme is selected. Semantic rename evidence declares
scope, completeness/partial/unsupported/unknown status, collisions and unresolved
references. Literal search is not proof of a semantic rename.

Validation establishes application safety for declared dependencies and supported
host guarantees. It does not establish that an agent/provider declared every
assumption, that inferred impact is complete, or that the proposed change is
semantically correct. Read dependencies may extend beyond the write footprint;
both acquisition and final validation keep their own current access requirements.

Supplied discovery evidence identifies object incarnations/versions, query and
membership scope, relevant configuration/index/provider generations and provenance.
Its validation includes additions/deletions/renames that can change the answer,
not only previously returned objects. Conservative invalidation is allowed;
narrower invalidation needs a contract. Absence of returned edges and a snapshot
token do not establish global completeness or external isolation. Operations
requiring complete discovery cannot consume partial/exhausted evidence as if
complete; refresh/reject or admit a separate narrower operation.

Acquisition and recipient release have separate rights; relationship traversal
does not grant access. Bind exact write participants and current dependencies at
publication. D46 selects supplied-evidence query/coverage/token profiles; no
built-in graph engine, compiler, database or semantic discovery implementation is
introduced. Bound traversal/depth/fan-out/source/result/evidence retention under
section 17. Invalidated analysis may release eligible derived state, not authored
content or unknown effect evidence.

Symbol rename as text edits is not file rename. Resource create/rename/delete
requires separately declared host capability/guarantees; unsupported plans reject
before mutation. Local text atomicity is not multi-file persistence or saga
compensation. Optional Git candidate staging is evaluation only: unsaved snapshots
and preconditions still govern promotion. Git ref locks/worktree metadata are
neither live edit mutexes nor a sandbox; no atomic editor-plus-ref/filesystem
publication is inferred. Cross-authority orchestration remains excluded.

A conditional Git root update, if separately evaluated, only publishes that
repository snapshot to readers pinning its root. It cannot atomically change
editor state plus the ref, check out several paths, or coordinate repositories
without another established contract. Reused commit IDs do not replace fresh
publication identity. Extra external effects retain their normal evidence and
safe-disposition obligations; no saga is needed merely for a sole validated root
promotion. Cost comparisons remain implementation evaluation, not a claim that
Git staging is cheaper or that it adds user-facing history branching/selective undo.

Conformance covers shared explicit/selection targets, source boundary conversions,
grapheme versus scalar behavior, direction/primary mapping, scope crossing,
readonly undo, declaration/callers together, changed nonwrite dependencies, new
references, unsaved dependents and partial/unknown discovery. Existing edit and
bridge models cover only their declared subsets; semantic completeness, all
Unicode/navigation laws and concrete storage performance remain separate evidence.

### 26.3 Structural targets and transformation evidence

For a supported structural operation, the provider supplies a bounded target
description with its exact authority/document incarnation/source context, accepted
provider and grammar/schema/dialect profile, relevant region-map context, declared
target interpretation and resolved source spans. Provider-local handles are scoped
selectors, not permanent identities, grants or instructions to execute. Multiple
spans preserve their explicit ordering/relationship; do not silently replace them
with a bounding interval that includes unrelated source. Invalid or ambiguous
maps refuse the requested operation. No universal node kind, symbol ID, tokenizer,
graph representation or public target-handle encoding is selected here.

Target resolution, transformation planning and candidate validation are separate
obligations. A syntactically recognized heading is not proof of schema conformance;
a schema-valid object is not proof of reference binding or discovery completeness.
Each supported operation declares a finite required set of named claims, their
source/candidate subject, scope/query and applicability profile. Required claims
come from the operation's accepted descriptor and explicit admitted intent, not
an untrusted caller/provider list that can omit obligations. A result's claim
kind and coverage must satisfy that requirement explicitly; a success flag or
greater amount of unrelated analysis cannot substitute for the required claim.
Partial broader analysis can still supply a complete claim for a narrower declared
scope. Completeness within that scope is not completeness of the whole workspace.

Lower the proposal into the existing exact change contract: complete source edit
records and expected bytes, explicit write participants, read-only and relevant
non-text dependencies, bounded write footprint and all actual companions under
§§3–6. Structural handles must resolve against their captured context before this
boundary; publication never asks an arbitrary provider to resolve a live handle.
Resolving spans alone does not discharge annotation/selection/history intent or
prove that an agent declared all semantic assumptions. No implicit whitespace,
delimiter, formatting or newline transformation follows from a structural label.

Evidence promising candidate conformance identifies the exact prepared candidate
and applicable validation scope/profile, not merely valid starting source or a
previous preview. Changes to the candidate or a relevant source, region, provider,
schema/configuration or discovery dependency invalidate that evidence unless an
explicit supported compatibility relation justifies reuse. Revalidate all required
evidence dependencies and current authority at final publication; preparation and
advisory validation remain outside the serialized boundary. A post-commit observer
cannot retroactively establish a precondition or roll back a known publication.

Unavailable, stale, ambiguous, invalid or insufficient evidence refuses the
claimed operation or requires fresh planning under the same guarantee. Any weaker
operation is a separately admitted explicit intent, not an implicit fallback.
An ordinary exact source edit requiring none of these interpretation claims does
not acquire a provider dependency through this contract. Evidence acceptance and
recipient release remain distinct; target kinds, scope/counts, errors and provider
metadata obey current projection. Handled failure preserves source; native/process
integrity limits remain §17/§28.23, not an implied provider sandbox.

formal/structural-targets.md records the conditional claim-matching/lowering
argument and private executable boundary cases. Concrete operation descriptors,
target and claim schemas, provider trust/conformance, candidate identity/encoding,
map profiles and full companion/adapter refinement remain D26/D33/D45/D46 gates.
This specifies supplied evidence for already supported operations; it adds no
mandatory structural-edit command, schema runtime or universal semantic service.

### 26.4 Named assertions and validation reports

The following are logical product/sum types, not assigned public Rust/wire names.
Every field has a bounded supported domain under its operation/profile descriptor;
unknown executable tags/profiles reject before effects. Required assertions and
admissible issuers come from accepted descriptor/intent and current host policy,
not a caller's shorter obligation list or a report's self-declared authority.

| Value | Required semantic shape |
|---|---|
| Resolved structural target | Exact source context set, accepted interpretation/profile and region-map context; bounded ordered spans with explicit document references and UTF-8 units; provider-local selector/provenance and target interpretation |
| Source subject | Tagged exact source context set and declared target/scope; no candidate publication is implied |
| Candidate subject | Tagged prepared operation/candidate identity, exact base context set and relevant complete proposed authored change; no live or published revision is implied |
| Assertion key | Supported claim kind; namespaced assertion identity; exact applicable grammar/schema/standard identity, version, dialect/extensions and validation options; source or candidate subject; target, scope/query and relevant context/dependencies |
| Validation report | Supported report interpretation; assertion key; accepted issuer/provenance and bounded report identity; verdict; coverage; permitted bounded reasons/evidence references |

Names identify accepted definitions, not executable locations. A schema URI/label
does not authorize fetching, imports, downloads or loading code. Transitive schema/
grammar references must be resolved under a bounded authorized provider contract;
the accepted definition closure and validation options are dependencies, not an
untracked mutable name. Actual identifier/closure/candidate encodings remain gates.
Validation does not authorize rewriting the candidate; any transformation creates
an explicitly identified candidate requiring its own applicable validation.
Equality of source bytes or a document label alone cannot identify these values.
Source and candidate tags are not interchangeable, even when their bytes match.
Target/candidate construction and report decoding must enforce the declared shape
before a report is considered for satisfaction.

Conformant means the named assertion holds within the report's declared coverage
under its accepted interpretation. Nonconformant means a definitive violation of
that assertion under the same interpretation; it is not a parser crash, malformed
report, timeout or unavailable service. Indeterminate provides no definitive
answer. Coverage is independent of execution status and verdict: complete means
complete only for the declared scope/query. A required complete assertion needs
matching complete conformant evidence. A partial scan can refute an assertion
only when its accepted claim profile supports a definitive counterexample; absent
that profile it remains insufficient evidence, not an invented negative result.

For each required assertion, consider only reports with an exact applicable key,
current dependencies, admissible issuer and validated interpretation. Retain
definitive contradictory facts/provenance rather than applying last-writer-wins.
Matching complete conformant evidence and matching definitive nonconformance are
contested; neither dominates by arrival time or caller priority. Definitive
nonconformance without establishing positive evidence is refuted; establishing
positive evidence without definitive nonconformance is established. Otherwise
the assertion remains insufficient. Only established required assertions satisfy
this gate, followed by ordinary final publication checks. These are internal
satisfaction categories, not public operation enums or global health states.

Equivalent duplicate reports do not amplify support or erase contradiction;
reordering the same admissible report set cannot change satisfaction. Reuse of one
report identity with different content is an evidence/protocol fault, not an
equivalent duplicate. Excluded, stale, unknown or malformed reports are not
definitive counterevidence, and cannot acquire veto power over an ordinary edit.
A provider identity alone does not authorize a new assertion kind or change its
meaning. Reconciliation/replanning is a separately bounded current decision;
neither replacing a report nor regranting access silently clears a contested
assertion for the same captured context.
The admissible-issuer/trust interpretation is itself a relevant captured context.
Changing it invalidates or explicitly reconciles that assertion's evidence set;
do not silently remove its negative facts and reuse the remaining positive report
as established under an unchanged context. Current recipient rights remain a
separate release gate, not authority to rewrite retained validation facts.

Report validity/admissibility, validation verdict, evidence satisfaction, execution
control, actual publication and recipient-safe disclosure remain separate.
Required nonconformance/indeterminacy/contestation cannot silently lower the
operation's guarantee; non-required evidence does not create new admission
obligations. Existing exact editing remains available without optional validation
claims under its own current authority/resource/integrity conditions.

formal/validation-reports.md records conditional laws and a private finite report
reference. Public identifiers/serializations, actual definitions and standard
profiles, issuer/trust/provenance checks, subject construction, closure resolution,
resource values, verdict decoding, contradiction retention and complete execution/
companion/adapter refinement remain open. No schema validator, validation runtime
or new structural command is required by these shared semantic types.

### 26.5 Owned candidates and descriptor binding

Use an engine-owned immutable prepared value as the base candidate identity,
with bounded scoped selectors where a mediated interface needs them. Preparation
copies or immutably owns the complete relevant intent: exact changes/expected
content, base/read/non-text contexts, actual companion intent, selected descriptor
interpretation and required assertions. Mutation of caller/provider buffers after
preparation cannot change that value. A changed candidate is a new prepared value
with new applicable validation, not replacement behind an old selector.

A selector resolves within its issuing authority/session and retained lifetime;
retirement or identifier exhaustion cannot make it refer to another candidate.
Possession grants no read, mutation, retention lease or persistence guarantee.
Issue/lookup/retirement use the existing capacity/current-release contracts.
Candidate identity is not invocation deduplication, a source revision, external
effect attempt or proof of publication. D03 still governs repeated invocation
intent/status loss. Public token representation, hash choice, allocator strategy
and numeric capacity/lifetime remain concrete profiles rather than inferred facts.

Capture the selected descriptor's executable meaning/version and definition
generation, not a caller-authored copy of its required claims. Discoverable
metadata is advisory. Typed and dynamic entry points resolve to the same retained
interpretation and prepared value. Final admission must establish current authority,
exact dependencies, retained candidate availability and descriptor compatibility
before publication. Unrelated catalog/cosmetic changes are not dependencies;
an unsupported change to relevant meaning requires rejection/replanning rather
than reinterpretation. Exact selected-definition equality is the conservative
base relation; broader compatibility needs an explicit reviewed contract.

Required candidate evidence is matched through its owner-resolved subject and
retained descriptor. A caller cannot validate one value and submit another with
the same label or strip required claims by changing a facade payload. No arbitrary
provider/descriptor callback runs inside publication. Bounded trusted lookup,
current predicate checks and coherent publication must share the final decision
boundary; actual ownership/locking/adapters still require refinement evidence.

### 26.6 Required evidence intake and definition closure

Required report identity is scoped by issuer and its accepted reporting contract;
do not interpret two issuers' local IDs as one global report. Validate shape,
attribution, current applicability and membership in the prepared operation's
required assertion set before intake can affect that operation. Forged, excluded,
stale or unrelated evidence cannot poison a valid candidate. Equivalent duplicates
are idempotent. Same accepted report identity with different payload is a scoped
protocol fault; preserve the original/provenance and block the affected evidence
gate pending explicit reconciliation, not overwrite it or quarantine unrelated work.

When admitting required evidence, reserve/account its bounded retention and any
necessary contradiction/provenance. If intake cannot complete, retain responsibility
or invalidate the affected candidate/evidence set explicitly; do not drop a
negative report and leave the old positive set apparently established. Unknown
intake/storage state is not evidence of conformance. Ordinary source edits with
no such required claims do not inherit that validation failure. Retiring a selector
does not imply worker quiescence or refund still-held snapshot/effect obligations.

The base definition-resolution profile uses explicitly supplied authorized
definitions/imports and an identified version/option closure. A URI is a name,
not an automatic fetch. Missing definitions are unavailable until separately
authorized provider work makes them available. Capture imported definitions as
dependencies; changing an import invalidates relevant evidence even when the
root definition name is unchanged. Do not capture unrelated definitions merely
because they are in the same registry. Bound graph nodes/edges/bytes/depth/work,
deduplicate visited definitions and refuse exhaustion rather than claim a partial
closure complete. Finding a cyclic dependency closure is not permission for
unbounded recursive validation; supported schema semantics and validator execution
need their own compatibility/termination/resource contract.

formal/preparation-boundary.md records direct-source precedent, conditional
ownership/retention/closure arguments and private executable cases. These close
the shared semantic choice of candidate ownership and required-evidence binding,
not actual public codecs, general descriptor compatibility, hostile decoding,
physical storage, provider truth or complete companion/implementation refinement.

## 27. Accepted editor-precedent baseline and proof gates

The user accepted this bounded baseline on 2026-10-24, requiring proofs for each
adoption. These clauses consolidate requirements §19 at existing interfaces;
they do not adopt an editor wholesale or close every related decision row.
[The proof ledger](formal/editor-precedents.md) binds each item to current scoped
evidence, necessary controls and unresolved refinement/conformance obligations.

| Adoption | Contract and owning sections |
|---|---|
| PA-01 Functional state / presentation boundary | §§2, 4.3, 6, 19: immutable retained snapshots and staged candidate state; one authoritative publication path. UI/layout projections cannot independently mutate authored state. This selects neither a concrete storage backend nor a universal shared struct |
| PA-02 Explicit selection and original-snapshot batch | §§3–4, 26: explicit revision-bound targets, with UI selections resolved to the same contract. Adjacent nonempty replacements are admitted when all other checks pass; touching/coincident insertions require explicit resolution. Do not infer order from list iteration, or import Helix's modal interaction model |
| PA-03 Mapped, namespaced attachments | §§4.3, 13, 19: attachment mapping uses closed declared affinity/deletion profiles and the common change meaning. Namespaces organize attachments; authorization remains separate. No default endpoint affinity or total inverse for deleted identities is selected |
| PA-04 Atomic local groups, separate from effects/history grouping | §§5–7, 14, 16: validate/stage required local participants then publish together; abort publishes none. Neither rollback of external effects nor multi-file disk atomicity is implied. Undo grouping is a distinct contract |
| PA-05 Explicit history boundaries | §14: explicit operation groups and isolation boundaries; any bounded typing coalescing remains within its declared compatible author/intent/context. Time proximity alone never combines unrelated authors or linked plans. Concrete typing/retention profiles remain open |
| PA-06 Revision-aware discoverable commands | §§3, 12, 22, 25: bounded typed command descriptions, explicit revisions/dependencies and declared update/event/version relations; agent and UI paths share semantics. No RPC transport, scripting runtime or stable native ABI is required |
| PA-07 Independent mapped embedded regions | §18: embedded services retain explicit source-region/context maps within the single authored document. Independent fences are not silently concatenated. Delimiters remain host syntax; parsing does not grant authority or execute diagrams. Concrete precedence/assets remain open |
| PA-08 Typed composition and coherent activation | §22: each setting declares its scope/combination/dependencies; no universal deep-merge rule. Activate a validated coherent context, not a grammar/query/configuration mixture; retain admitted context only under the bounded lifecycle contract. Exact schemas and failure/exhaustion choices remain open |
| PA-09 Supported save synchronization | §16: reaffirm ordinary best-effort checks and synchronization enabled where supported. Preserve separate effect/acknowledgment evidence and uncertainty. Actual provider procedures and synchronization-failure handling still require a declared profile |

### 27.1 Proof and acceptance discipline

Every PA item requires mathematical safety properties appropriate to its scope,
non-vacuity witnesses and targeted fault controls, plus conformance/refinement
evidence for the chosen implementation. A cited editor is design precedent,
not proof that this engine satisfies its contract. An SMT encoding or bounded
TLC run establishes only the named properties under its stated premises.
Unmodeled portions must remain open; a narrow algebra theorem cannot discharge
a lifecycle, authority, Unicode, platform or physical persistence guarantee.

The ledger's open gates block proof-complete or implementation-complete claims
for the affected adoption, not further safe drafting. Existing requirements
scope and stronger authority/disclosure/history constraints remain unchanged.
The later D01 adoption (§6.4) selects validated unchanged success for genuine
semantic identity, not equal bytes alone. It is a Vellum policy choice, not a
claim of uniform upstream editor behavior; invocation/status retention stays D03.

### 27.2 Observation and adversarial evidence

Existing instrumentation placements remain authoritative: publication/mapping
and history boundaries, mediated command/event release, language-context
activation and stale-result rejection, and provider dispatch/receipt/sync evidence.
Measure accepted/rejected/stale/fault dispositions, bounded work/pressure and
phase latency under the protected observation contract (§23), without making
namespaces, raw content, target offsets or cross-recipient revisions public labels.
Record dropped diagnostic evidence independently from authoritative status.
No new exporter, metric schema, numeric target or diagnostic grant is selected.
Contract-specific tests must challenge these boundaries, not just editor-visible
text output. Exact observation schemas and implementation tests remain open.

### 27.3 Abstract proof status

[The precedent proofs](formal/precedent-proofs.md) now give general construction/
preservation arguments for PA-01–09: retained fresh roots; finite original-snapshot
batches and reverse inverses; namespace frames and conditional anchor order;
coherent root reads/abort; group append/close isolation; revision-gated shared
dispatch; valid independent-region framing; typed-setting dependency frames/
coherent activation; and synchronization-evidence accounting including out-of-order
receipts. The added 29 SMT conditions check 19 local laws and 10 faulty alternatives.

These are authored mathematical inductions supported by trusted-solver local
lemmas, not proof-assistant-checked general refinement. They do not prove upstream
editors, unspecified profiles, concrete code or physical providers. The ledger's
remaining gates still apply. In particular a collapsed range with opposed
affinities can invert, and grouping keys omitting unrelated-plan identity can
misgroup; a supported profile must resolve those cases explicitly. This proof
pass selected no default endpoint affinity, typing policy or receipt schema.
D04's subsequent adoption in §4.3.1 has separate evidence in
formal/mapping-profiles.md; these earlier proof sources remain conditional.

### 27.4 Assumption ownership and composition gates

[The assumption audit](formal/assumption-audit.md) records 18 selected premises
and 11 selected handoffs for PA-01–09, with existing architectural owners,
validation boundaries, failure constraints and residual evidence. The registry
binds those records to the proof-source fingerprints and named local conditions.
All handoffs remain open refinements; an acyclic checked support graph does not
prove that producer outputs meet consumer premises.

In particular coherent activation does not establish that command lowering and
final publication use the same relevant registry/context version. PH-09 records
this unbound concrete handoff without inventing a version schema. PS-CH now adds
bounded reference support without closing that refinement. Surface
equivalence still assumes equal canonical lowering, configuration framing still
assumes complete dependencies, and receipt evidence still assumes historical
attribution/provider trust. Current release authority is a separate gate even
for retained roots and truthful historical facts. These refine existing proof/
conformance gates, not public APIs or product-policy decisions.

### 27.5 Verification evidence freshness

The verification harness now captures source bytes before local proof-module
imports and validates the copied tree, then checks live inventory and digest
equality before publishing current evidence. Its 42 infrastructure controls are
separate from editor theorems. A signal, tool error, missing/malformed worker
report, unexpected SMT result or incomplete run cannot count as a current full
pass through the checked paths. Generation and partial diagnostics remain distinct.

The captured tree is not an atomic filesystem snapshot or sandbox; external
tools remain trusted and later edits can stale a report. This closes a bounded
proof-harness implementation gap, not AP-17's general induction/certificate or
independent-review obligations. See formal/evidence-harness.md for exact limits.

### 27.6 Captured command interpretation pathway

PS-CH couples context activation, captured interpretation, current grant/source/
compatibility validation and coherent publication in one bounded reference state.
It reuses actual finite splice, mapped-point and inverse operators, rather than
only comparing independent guard formulas. Five positive profiles, eight targeted
fault controls and twelve witnesses cover one pending text-changing command over
two interpretation contexts and a six-transition exploration horizon.

Compatible and unrelated cosmetic changes can proceed under the selected model
profiles; incompatible, source-stale and revoked work is refused without changing
the current root. Captures remain consistent/immutable and contexts remain held
while prepared. Diagnostics off/full/fault cannot alter authoritative state or
retroactively reject a committed command in the checked reference pathway.
Acceptance and post-commit diagnostic witnesses freeze their relevant facts at
publication so later events cannot satisfy a different ordering accidentally.

This is finite reference-path safety and reachability, not a concrete schema,
general compatibility algorithm, source-neutral D01 refinement, native callback, wall-clock
noninterference, liveness or whole-engine refinement proof. The interpretation
function and cosmetic classification are modeled premises. PH-09 and D33–D35
retain their concrete representation/validator/lifetime obligations. No existing
unbound handoff is relabeled proved through a new shared assumption.

### 27.7 Canonical byte-edit reference evidence

Three algorithmically different constructions compare original-position emission,
right-to-left private splicing and delta-adjusted sequential application with
reverse inverse recovery. The finite corpus has 59,052 generated evaluations and
six literal byte fixtures, including adjacent nonempty replacements and multibyte
boundaries. It checks exact bytes/length, valid UTF-8, source preservation and
72,901 adjacent-pair coalescing comparisons. Sixteen invalid-domain controls
and ten faulty alternatives exercise the specified test boundaries, including
sparse-array rejection and dense equality checks in the private byte oracle.

See formal/text-oracles.md for the exact alphabet, bounds, fixtures and premises.
These are same-author design expectations, not independent Cleanroom assurance,
arbitrary-length induction or concrete backend refinement. This corpus assumes
canonical ordered input; adopted D02 normalization and ambiguity rejection are
specified separately in §4.2.1 with evidence in formal/batch-normalization.md.
The coalescing comparisons establish byte equality only, not mapping or complete
semantic equivalence; the separate normalization evidence gives a counterexample.
No-op
classification follows adopted §6.4 but is not proved by these corpus equalities.
Insertion ties, file-BOM interpretation (D21), grapheme profiles (D27), schemas,
resource limits and authority gates retain their existing decision/refinement
obligations. No runtime component or instrumentation path
is introduced by reference test tooling.

### 27.8 Publication clause traceability

The ten requirements §5.3 source bullets are decomposed into 41 review clauses
with exact source fragments, owning contracts, scoped positive case/property
references, conformance scenarios, residual gates and per-clause risks. Twenty-two
clauses have selected positive property references and nineteen have none listed;
these are not proved-clause counts. Text reconstruction and sixteen sensitivity
controls establish selected inventory/reference integrity, not semantic adequacy,
independent review or actual conformance. See formal/publication-clauses.md and
its machine-readable companion.

The existing publication boundary IF-03 / INS-02 remains the enforcement and
observation placement. Recipient release and diagnostic drain retain their
separate current-policy gates; external effects keep their own evidence limits.
No schema, grouping/tie policy, external guarantee or new runtime path is chosen.
Whole-document finer decomposition and every concrete refinement remain open.

## 28 Remaining approved baseline contracts

This completes the baseline traversal requested on 2026-10-25, not the concrete
v1 operation/type/profile specification or implementation. D01–D12/D42 keep their
previous owning contracts. The following clauses adopt/refine the remaining
approved direction and supersede earlier recommendation-only wording on the same
choice. A required capability awaiting assets/native evidence is an unmet release
gate, not a satisfied requirement renamed unsupported. Exact unresolved profiles
are enumerated in formal/baseline-decisions.json; no numeric preset, dependency
version, platform result or completeness claim is supplied by assumption.

### 28.13 History grouping

Default to one semantic invocation per undo group. Typing coalescing requires an
explicit open group, the same author/executor intent, plan, participant set and
compatible context, plus remaining budgets. Close on explicit boundary, origin/
plan/participant change, reversal or incompatible context change. Timer proximity
alone never joins groups. Agent plans are isolated unless explicitly grouped under
this contract. Existing atomic publication determines group participants; grouping
cannot split or expand the operation. Actual typing compatibility/limits are profile
gates and must be declared before coalescing is enabled.

### 28.14 History retirement

Retire complete groups and the least dependency-closed set of continuations that
become invalid with them. Preserve unrelated scopes. Pins and promised floors
constrain the whole proposed retirement: refuse it if any required member cannot
be removed, rather than leaving a partial linked group. New admission may then
refuse under D06; it cannot invent more retention capacity. Report empty, blocked
and unavailable history distinctly within D12 projection. Representation, byte
charges, pin budgets and floor interfaces remain concrete profile/refinement gates.

### 28.15 Ordinary provider persistence

Use the agreed ordinary best-effort checks with synchronization enabled where
supported. Capture required acknowledgment strength before dispatch. Record write
success and synchronization failure separately; the latter is not proof of no
write and does not satisfy a stronger acknowledgment. Missing optional stronger
capabilities do not disable ordinary saves. Missing required evidence does block
the stronger request. Actual write/replacement/attribute/security/synchronization
procedures and provider tests remain release gates; no universal crash guarantee.

### 28.16 Causal queued baseline progression

Preserve original capture and original preconditions immutably. A derived dispatch
baseline may advance only through a permitted, attributable, uncontested causal
chain for the same destination/context under supported provider evidence. Never
relax an explicitly pinned caller condition. Missing, ABA-ambiguous, unknown or
contradictory evidence prevents progression; arrival order and new token appearance
are insufficient. Record derived evidence separately. Actual receipt/schema and
provider causality remain refinement gates; conservative refusal is available but
must not be advertised as demonstrated progression support.

### 28.17 Search navigation

Use the one exact ordered nonoverlapping match set from §15. A start without an
identified current match includes a match starting exactly at that byte position
in either direction. Next/previous from an identified current match excludes that
match and advances in the named direction. Wrap is an explicit Boolean, false
when omitted in the headless baseline; permit at most one wrap per invocation and
report it. With only the current match, wrapping may return it with a wrapped
result, never an internal navigation loop. Adapters may select explicit wrap
preferences without changing match-set or command semantics. Stale current-match
identity is not a new implicit start; reject or require a fresh request.

### 28.18 Matching profiles

Exact case-sensitive literal matching is always the base profile. Advertise
caseless matching only with a pinned Unicode default-fold profile and exact
whole-source-character expansion maps; no partial expansion match. No implicit
smart-case, locale or normalization. The explicit caseless capability's version,
mapping/conformance and supported limits remain gates, not silently waived work.

### 28.19 Comment content

The minimal comment has a non-confusable identity/version, document association,
plain UTF-8 body and supported document/point/range target under D04. An empty
body is valid authored content, not implicit deletion; delete is explicit. Accept
only declared bounded metadata fields/kinds; unsupported authority-bearing fields
reject. Producer author/audience labels do not grant rights. Rich bodies, threads,
mentions and workflow state stay excluded. Exact public field encodings and limits
remain technical gates; body, attachment and source versions remain distinct.

### 28.20 Annotation persistence

Keep core storage-neutral. A supported host format must version its schema, bind
the resource/document and exact source evidence, preserve authored identities,
bodies and target context, reject unsupported/malformed data on a staged candidate,
and report annotation versus source outcomes independently. Do not use a pathname
alone as durable identity or silently attach stale targets on reload. The reference
host uses versioned UTF-8 JSON under §29.4. Its concrete record schema, location,
migration and security-preservation procedure remain gates; selecting JSON or
passing a generic serializer guard does not close those obligations.

### 28.21 BOM round trip domain

For the base strict UTF-8 file profile, consume at most one leading EF BB BF
signature into BOM metadata and preserve any following literal U+FEFF as text.
Encoding prepends that signature exactly when BOM metadata is present. Reject
the ambiguous output tuple (BOM absent, text starts with U+FEFF) before dispatch
under this profile; never silently strip the character or change the metadata.
An explicit separately supported interpretation/conversion can select a different
domain. On the base supported domain require both byte round trip and text/metadata
round trip. Editing a literal leading U+FEFF remains valid; serialization refusal
does not authorize source mutation. Section 16.1.1 adds scoped streaming/reference
codec evidence; production/backend refinement remains open.

### 28.22 Clocks and shutdown

Use one declared local monotonic clock/epoch per applicable duration; inherit
remaining budgets and take the tighter child request. Never subtract different
epochs or treat unavailable/invalid clock evidence as unexpired. A request needing
an unavailable clock guarantee is unsupported/stopped under its contract, not
silently unlimited. Declare suspend behavior and phase endpoints before claiming
deadlines. Shutdown requires source/annotation decisions and reports unknown
effects at the bounded wait cutoff without releasing their obligations. Clock
provider, actual service/time values and forced-close retention remain gates.

### 28.23 Fault containment and reentry

Treat malformed/forged input and ordinary I/O failure separately from authenticated
supplier contradiction or uncertain integrity. Quarantine the smallest justified
attempt/destination/provider scope; broaden only with evidence of broader uncertainty.
Retain contested facts and block incompatible effects. Reentry requires authorized
revalidation/replacement with fresh context and retained historical attribution;
restart/timeout cannot clear contradiction or prove safe retry. Exact trusted fault
codes, escalation evidence and provider conformance remain technical gates.

### 28.24 Failed language activation

Install only a complete validated grammar/query/configuration combination. On
candidate failure retain last-known-good service only while its original complete
context remains supported, authorized and explicitly compatible with current source/
dependencies. Otherwise expose plaintext/unavailable language service and keep
source editing. Do not call an old incompatible tree current, partially install
new queries or unload held native assets. Actual compatibility predicates/assets
are gates; lack of evidence is not compatibility.

### 28.25 Independent embedded regions

Each supported fence body is an independent child interpretation. A literal body
map is contiguous; §18.6's named host-marker exclusion may use bounded exact
segments within that one body. Delimiters/prefix holes belong to the host; embedded
style overrides host style only within validated included segments, with host
fallback elsewhere. Child-only edit targets crossing those segments/body boundaries
are unavailable rather than clipped into a different operation. An explicit full
document-byte edit may cross regions through ordinary atomic validation; region
labels grant no authority. Invalid/unfinished/unsupported regions degrade locally.
Section 18.6 tests scoped actual discovery/aliases/maps/capture precedence; full
current-context/command/production integration remains a gate. General combined
multi-fence, arbitrary discontinuous and recursive injection plans remain excluded.

### 28.26 Language assets

Require a pinned host-controlled Markdown grammar/query set and at least one
working child grammar/query integration with exact maps, incremental/fresh checks
and license/provenance evidence. Mermaid labels must have truthful supported or
fallback outcomes; no renderer/execution/download is implied. Section 18.6 pins
and executes a scoped native reference; an abstract map theorem alone does not
establish that integration. Production packages/ABI, licensing/bundling and the
required frontend integrations remain release gates, not inferred from test tools.

### 28.27 Unicode conformance

Name the exact supported segmentation, line-break and bidi versions and any
tailoring independently. Bytes remain canonical edit coordinates; logical
graphemes, native indices and geometry are distinct conversions. Test the supported
version's applicable conformance data, not merely a library name. No automatic
source normalization. Actual version/dependency/conformance matrix remains a gate.

### 28.28 Geometry

Share semantic policy and use each frontend's actual geometry provider. All hits,
caret stops, painting, native composition and accessibility geometry must use the
same accepted context or an explicitly validated conversion. Return ambiguous,
virtual or unavailable rather than guess editable bytes. Unsupported runs preserve
logical source and navigation via declared safe fallback. Actual glyph/cell/bidi/
width/decorative profile and platform demonstrations remain required gates.

### 28.29 Composition ordering

In the baseline cancel outstanding preedit on accepted focus loss, undo/redo or
conflicting semantic command before that command's source mutation. A native
commit already accepted before that boundary remains an ordinary prior edit;
late commits for the invalidated session reject and never follow new focus.
Do not fabricate commits from key names or consumed IME keys. Platforms unable to
provide this preedit contract advertise committed-text capability rather than
pretend native preedit support. Controlled-event tests and real platform ordering
evidence remain required; the baseline does not assert native cancellation succeeded.

### 28.30 Accessibility

Both frontends retain keyboard/semantic action requirements. Advertise native
facilities only for named tested backend/OS/framework combinations with bounded
semantic text, coordinate and current-release evidence. Untested facilities remain
unverified, not certified by keyboard operation. The actual support matrix and
assistive-technology demonstration are unmet release gates until supplied.

### 28.31 Clipboard fragments

Structured fragments pair in source order only when fragment/target counts match;
otherwise reject unchanged. Flatten/broadcast, if exposed, are separately named
transformations. Reference plain-text export joins captured fragments with one LF
between fragments, preserving each fragment verbatim; this separator is not source
normalization and cannot preserve structured boundaries on an external round trip.
Plain-text paste broadcasts the full literal text to each target. No implicit
indent/newline transformation or complete-payload truncation.

### 28.32 Clipboard evidence

Export success means only the actual declared provider acknowledgment. Keep source
intact on failed/unknown export. Cut requires that acknowledgment plus renewed exact
source and edit-authority validation; otherwise report copied-but-not-cut where
appropriate. Retain only bounded session-local payload/evidence under explicit
rights/lifetimes; do not infer physical transfer, durability or erasure. Actual
provider acknowledgment/retention/release procedures remain integration gates.

### 28.33 Closed northbound surface

Every enabled operation has one versioned descriptor: identity, parameter/coordinate
domain, target/context dependencies, required capabilities, resource profile,
preconditions, effects, admissible outcome/event relation and cancellation/late/
duplicate/fault behavior. Reject unknown executable semantics before effects;
descriptive metadata never grants execution. Registered schemas are finite bounded
data, not arbitrary predicates or a scripting runtime. Typed and dynamic calls
share this relation. The complete concrete verb/type/event/code catalog is still
a technical specification gate: descriptor well-formedness is not API completeness.

### 28.34 Configuration

Use §22.2's typed per-setting composition: scalar replacement, list replacement
unless explicit stable composition, maps only at declared keys, absence inherits,
removal exposes lower layers and explicit reset selects library default. Host
restrictions intersect allowed behavior; they are never overridable preferences.
Reject unsupported keys/types and equal-rank conflicting values before activation
within the owning layer. Frontends additionally reject unresolved command/prefix
ambiguity before activating bindings. Multiple workspaces require explicit
association/order. Actual engine setting and frontend keymap catalogs remain
separate technical gates; input conflicts do not prevent headless engine commands.

### 28.35 Context retention

Retain complete captured interpretations and in-use provider/native assets under
finite limits. If a proposed new activation cannot coexist with required retained
contexts, refuse it and preserve the active context and obligations. Planned
drains/migration are separate explicit lifecycles, not implicit cancellation or
unload. Compatible accepted results still recheck current rights/dependencies.
Actual retention bounds/ownership/compatibility and safe discharge remain gates.

### 28.36 Diagnostic schemas

Default to stable approved codes and bounded content-free primitive fields with
declared units/provenance/classification. Raw content, host errors, paths, selectors,
identities and arguments stay excluded by default. Validate before capture; no
arbitrary formatting/callbacks in critical transitions. Invalid diagnostic data
cannot change the authoritative operation. Exact schema/metric catalogs and
measured capture cost remain technical/evidence gates.

### 28.37 Diagnostic loss

Base optional capture is bounded and nonblocking: when full, drop the new optional
record, retaining required authoritative status/effect evidence elsewhere. Any
coalescing profile must name its key and lost distinctions. Loss accounting
saturates at its declared finite maximum and exposes overflow/inexactness; never
wrap into apparent zero. Reset/switch starts a distinct observation generation;
do not present cross-generation deltas or unknown age as fresh exact counts.
Shutdown/off may discard optional queued capture with honest loss/availability.
Section 23.2.1 specifies a selected marker/queue/counter/generation contract.
Actual installed counters/queues, clock/freshness truth and measured capacity
values remain gates; that reference does not close the complete metric catalog.

### 28.38 Diagnostic grants

Richer collection and release require separate host-established field/scope,
purpose/destination and bounded lifetime/storage grants. Expiry/revocation stops
new collection and gates queued release; capture ceilings prevent later expansion.
Session-local minimized retention is the baseline, with explicit authorized
extensions rather than indefinite default history. Support bundles inventory each
included class; no automatic source/files/environment/memory capture. Actual grant,
retention and disposal schemas/procedures remain gates, not secure-erasure promises.

### 28.39 Measurement

Declare units, boundary, population/denominator, workload/environment, clock,
coverage/loss and censoring before comparing measures. Include offered/admitted/
rejected/completed and pending age, useful outcomes, saturation and tail distributions
together; completed-only averages and fast refusal cannot establish service.
MELT/golden/USE/RED share observations, not extra authority. Numeric budgets/SLOs
require measured evidence. Safety invariants never become statistical error budgets.

### 28.40 Risk based acceptance

Changes to publication, authority/disclosure, identity, persistence/effects,
resource promises or compatibility are high risk: require explicit contract and
assumptions, scoped model/proof argument where applicable, independently derived
expectations, adversarial/conformance tests and a separate challenge review.
Real providers/native/concurrency need actual integration evidence. Lower-risk
presentation/editorial changes use proportionate checks but cannot bypass a
changed high-risk dependency. Known invariant violations block acceptance;
risk acceptance cannot silently weaken safety. Actual reviewer/process/CI assignments
remain release gates; a second agent is not independent Cleanroom certification.

### 28.41 Reliability

Do not publish numeric reliability claims without a declared supported environment,
exposure/failure unit, representative human/agent population, sampling method and
uncertainty/censoring treatment. Adversarial cases supplement but do not substitute
for statistical usage sampling. Retain known failures/unsupported cases visibly.
Workload/corpus, exposure and measured results remain evidence gates.

### 28.43 Packaging

Keep core/coordinator/facade, optional language/layout, adapters and both thin apps
separable at semantic ownership boundaries; UI/runtime/telemetry ecosystem types
do not cross the authoritative core API. Feature/import alone starts no service,
loads no asset and grants no rights. Use one evaluated backend behind engine-owned
source/snapshot interfaces, not runtime backend extensibility. Actual crates,
versions/MSRV/features, asset licenses and support matrix remain technical/evidence
gates; both apps and required child-language/native capability are not waived.

### 28.44 Compatibility

Use explicit pre-1.0 behavioral profile versions. Same-profile compatibility cannot
strengthen caller obligations or weaken guarantees; semantic defaults count as
behavior. Unknown executable variants reject; informational fields may be ignored
only when declared nonsemantic by that schema. No stable native ABI or indefinite
support promise. Executable enums are exhaustive within explicitly versioned profiles
as selected in §25. Actual exported Rust types/compile compatibility, format
versions/deprecation/migration and security-support lifetime retain their explicit
release decisions and evidence; no dates or toolchain versions are guessed.

### 28.45 Ordinary editing

Keep explicit primary selection and direction. Default normalization orders
selections by source position, merges overlapping nonempty ranges, removes exact
duplicates and preserves the explicit primary's corresponding normalized range;
adjacent nonempty ranges remain separate. Collapsed-point affinity and coincident
insertion ambiguity follow D04/D02, not incidental ordering. A merged primary
range keeps the primary input's direction; another merged range uses the earliest
explicitly listed contributing selection's direction. Unmerged ranges retain
their direction. These are declared selection rules, not spatial-sort tie guesses.
These human-selection
rules never coalesce an explicit agent edit batch. Logical character commands use
the pinned grapheme profile; logical line/document endpoints use exact source
structure, with EOF a valid caret. Word classification, indentation/tab preferences
and visual commands require named profiles; no whole editor binding/mode scheme.
Section 26.1.2 defines explicit simple prefix shifts/generated-newline products;
keyboard Tab routing, fixed numeric preferences and grammar indentation remain
separate accepted configuration/provider profiles.
Actual detailed command catalog and Unicode/geometry conformance remain gates.
Section 29.2 selects the reference line and default grapheme/word profiles;
identifier-specific navigation is distinct, never an implicit word-rule override.

### 28.46 Supplied semantic evidence

Require exact scope/query/membership/context dependencies, current rights and
truthful complete/partial/unknown coverage for supplied semantic evidence. If a
command requires completeness, reject missing/partial/stale evidence rather than
apply an apparently complete rename. Conservative invalidation is the baseline;
precise invalidation needs supplier proof, including additions absent from prior
results. No graph/compiler/discovery service or cross-authority transaction is
added. Provider completeness truth and actual evidence/token schemas remain gates.

### 28.47 Security maintenance

Before supported release publish a real reporting route, accountable triage/update
owner, dependency/asset audit procedure and supported-fix version policy. Record
triage, containment, synthetic regression and release communication without
invented deadlines or indefinite backports. A private design review cannot satisfy
this operational process. Actual route/owners/cadence/support commitments remain
explicit release decisions and evidence gates.

### 28.48 Model governance

Treat changes to observable behavior, ownership/trust, authority/disclosure,
effects/dependencies, resource promises or compatibility as material. Review the
affected contract/model and invalidate dependent evidence before accepting the
change. Editorial changes preserve semantics and use source/reference/freshness
checks; uncertainty takes the material path. Stable clause/code/test/evidence
links and source/manual/generated ownership must be inspectable. Hash equality
does not prove semantic correspondence. Actual CI/traceability implementation and
final clause/operation audit remain gates.

### 28.49 Baseline completion and proof boundary

formal/baseline-contracts.md supplies conditional arguments, finite mechanism
checks and local SMT support for this traversal. formal/baseline-decisions.json
assigns every D01–D48 one owning contract, evidence role and residual gate.
That inventory's structural completeness does not close each whole D-row or prove
the entire engine, implementation, host profiles or categorical completeness.
The wider specification completion gate still requires the exact operation/type/
profile relations, finer clause reconciliation, independent expectations and
actual platform/resource evidence. No unsupported capability counts as delivered.

## 29 Adopted v1 reference profile

The user approved the coherent sensible-default set on 2026-10-27. These are
reference defaults, not new optional substitutes for required v1 capabilities.
Hosts may select other explicitly supported versioned profiles without weakening
the shared authority, atomicity, fidelity, current-release or boundedness contracts.
Default changes are behavioral changes under §§25/28.44. The machine-readable
selection is formal/reference-profile.json; public operation/type schemas remain
the owning contracts' responsibility.

### 29.1 Closed execution and discoverable information

Use the minimum supported versioned typed operation products from §22.1.1, with
exhaustive executable variants and one catalog for typed/dynamic discovery and
dispatch. Unknown executable versions/variants reject before execution. Public
information may extend only where its schema explicitly declares it nonsemantic;
it cannot change required claims, behavior, authority or decoding of an existing
variant. Default input targeting is explicit, never UI focus. Metadata visibility
is bounded/currently authorized, not a grant. No RPC, native plugin ABI, arbitrary
argument bag or scripting runtime is required. Actual IDs, Rust products,
per-operation total relations and compatibility tests remain technical work.

### 29.2 Lossless text and logical coordinates

The reference logical-line profile recognizes CRLF as one delimiter, lone LF and
lone CR as delimiters. Other Unicode separators remain content for this profile;
visual wrapping uses a separate layout profile. Reading, indexing and writing do
not normalize or replace any source bytes. Inserted text follows explicit command
intent/settings; line recognition alone never chooses a new-file newline style.

Logical line indices and UTF-8 byte columns start at zero. Each line has half-open
source spans `start..bodyEnd` (body) and `bodyEnd..end` (delimiter). Line bodies and
delimiters partition the source in order. There is always a line: empty text has
one empty line; a trailing delimiter introduces a final empty line. A body column
addresses only a scalar boundary from zero through the body byte length inclusive;
`(line, body length)` denotes the caret before its delimiter. The final line's
body-end is EOF, which is valid even when the line is empty. Out-of-range lines,
columns or scalar splits refuse conversion, never clamp. A point inside a CRLF
delimiter has no body-column representation: conversion reports unavailable,
not a rounded neighbor. Such an offset can still be a valid canonical byte-edit
coordinate under §4; the logical-line projection does not redefine that contract.

The reference grapheme and ordinary prose-word boundary profile is Unicode 18.0.0
UAX #29 revision 49, default extended grapheme clusters and default word boundaries,
without implicit locale tailoring or source normalization. Actual command behavior
(which segments are traversed and endpoint/selection semantics) still belongs to
the closed command catalog. Identifier-specific commands use a separately named
supported language/profile, not a silent modification of prose-word rules.
Unsupported required tailoring is unavailable. Word segmentation alone does not
claim dictionary-quality navigation for every script. Bidi and visual line breaking
retain independently named profiles; selecting UAX #29 does not select them.
Implementations must pass applicable pinned conformance data before advertising
this profile. Host alternatives require explicit version/tailoring metadata and
tests; dependency availability cannot silently downgrade the reference version.
Section 26.1.3 supplies scoped logical command products and executed pinned
reference-tool conformance, not production/incremental provider selection or a
universal Unicode proof. Its word significance and endpoint rules are command
profiles, not dictionary/language tailoring of the underlying default segmentation.

### 29.3 History and configuration

The default is one invocation per history group. Typing coalescing is opt-in through
an explicit bounded group/profile and closes on incompatible origin/plan/
participants/context, intervening incompatible command, explicit close or capacity.
Time proximity alone does not join groups; unrelated authors/plans never join.
Retirement preserves complete-group/dependency and admitted pin/floor promises.
Numerical retention limits and any timed typing profile require declared units and
actual clock/measurement evidence, not an invented universal timeout.

Use typed setting composition and deterministic scope precedence under §22,
not generic recursive merge or arbitrary predicates. Core operations are shared
semantic commands; bindings are adapter-specific and overridable. No Emacs,
Neovim or Helix modal/keybinding model is imported wholesale. Exact settings,
keymap conflicts, indent/tab preferences and command endpoints remain catalog
work under the adopted constraints, rather than unresolved architecture choices.

### 29.4 Reference annotation storage

The reference host format is a small versioned UTF-8 JSON document under RFC 8259,
not JSON-LD, an embedded database or a mandatory library storage backend. It carries
an explicit format/schema version, document/resource association, exact source
evidence and an annotation snapshot preserving authored identities/incarnations,
content/target versions, plain-text bodies and declared target context. Empty
bodies remain records. The base metadata profile is empty; optional metadata needs
its own closed versioned schema, not arbitrary executable/authority-bearing fields.

Use exact allowed fields and reject duplicate member names, unsupported versions,
invalid scalar strings, ambiguous identities, invalid targets and exceeded bounds
before any publication. JSON numbers must not round identity/version/coordinate
values: use an exact validated representation in the concrete schema. Load into an
owned staged candidate, validate association/current source/permissions/resources,
then publish atomically or leave current annotation state unchanged. Stale imported
target evidence may only enter a separately declared explicit detached/recovery
contract; it cannot silently attach to the current source. No executable contexts,
remote references, fuzzy repair or automatic fetch are implied by JSON strings.

The host supplies location/binding; no adjacent sidecar is inferred from a path.
Core storage stays neutral. Section 29.4.1 and its schema define the reference
field encodings. Numerical resource profiles, safe host association across rename/
replacement, identity restoration and provider durability remain integration gates.
Unsupported versions reject without rewriting the input. Source and annotation
save outcomes remain independent; format validity does not establish persistence.

### 29.4.1 Reference annotation snapshot version 1

formal/annotation-snapshot.schema.json fixes the JSON Schema 2020-12 structural
shape. It is an interchange contract, not a required schema runtime in the core.
All objects have exact required fields and no additional members. `format` is
`vellum.annotations`, `version` is the string `1`, and `records` is an array of
the captured live records, not a history log, tombstone archive or executable plan.
Array order is preserved by interchange but conveys no additional UI ordering or
authority. Optional metadata has no fields in this version; an empty `metadata`
object is therefore not an allowed extra member.

| Product | Exact fields and meaning |
|---|---|
| Snapshot | `format`, `version`, `document`, `source`, `records` |
| Document association | `namespace`, `value`: nonempty opaque host-domain strings, not a pathname, live handle or capability |
| Source evidence | `domain`, `token`, `byteLength`: nonempty opaque domain/token and the canonical UTF-8 source byte count; file BOM metadata is not a source offset |
| Record | `identity`, `contentVersion`, `targetGeneration`, `body`, `authoredTarget`, `placement` |
| Record identity | `namespace`, `value`, `incarnation`; at most one live record for a namespace/value, even if two input entries claim different incarnations |
| Document target | `kind: document`, `source` |
| Point target | `kind: point`, `source`, `offset`, `affinity: before or after`, `profile: position or content`; affinity and the existing §4.3.1 mapping meaning are explicit and separately preserved |
| Content-range target | `kind: range`, `source`, `start`, `end`; nonempty half-open UTF-8 byte range with §4.3.1 boundary-exclusive insertion behavior |
| Located placement | `state: attached or affected`, `target`; exact current source evidence, independently validated mapping/placement; affected does not claim intact applicability |
| Detached placement | Only `state: detached`; no current target is asserted and the body/authored target remain present |

Point profiles are required in both authored targets and located placements. The
user selected preservation of both existing meanings on 2026-10-28. Do not infer
one from affinity, file language, current placement or source content; do not omit,
default, coerce or normalize the field. Missing/unknown profiles reject the snapshot
without changing live state or rewriting input. This revises the draft version 1
shape; it creates no implicit migration from earlier draft profileless points.
Authored and located fields are preserved independently as data; their mapping/
continuity agreement still requires trusted target evidence at activation. An enum
in a file neither supplies that evidence nor authorizes repair or execution.

The reference checks cover 828 accepted decoded/staged values across 23 target
shapes, 256 staging gates, four existing-mapper distinction witnesses, 75 controls,
five assertion-killed mutations with passing baseline and 28 pinned JSON Schema
cases. The profile is injectively represented and copied through the selected
decode/stage path; this is not a production encoder, migration, native restoration,
atomic load or physical persistence proof. See formal/annotation-snapshot.md.

Counts, offsets and generations use exact canonical ASCII decimal strings:
natural values are `0` or a nonzero digit followed by digits; incarnation,
contentVersion and targetGeneration must be positive. No sign, leading zero,
fraction, exponent, trailing whitespace or implicit numeric coercion is accepted.
Their finite digit/representable-domain bound belongs to the supported resource/
engine profile; no universal 64-bit core representation is selected by storage.
Bodies may be empty and contain any valid Unicode scalar string. No Unicode or
newline normalization occurs. Duplicate JSON member names are detected after
escape decoding, at every object depth; plain and escaped spellings cannot bypass
uniqueness. Reject malformed UTF-8, leading JSON BOM, invalid escapes and unpaired
surrogates. Whitespace/member ordering permitted by the format is not identity;
this selects no canonical-JSON signature or content-hash protocol.

An authored target preserves explicit original source evidence, including historical
context where necessary. Validate its syntactic range against its declared source
length; this alone does not prove the historical source or semantic intent true.
When the authored target names the available current source domain/token, its
length must agree and its positions must pass the actual scalar-boundary checks;
claiming a different length cannot turn current evidence into unavailable history.
A located placement must bind the snapshot's current source and valid scalar
boundaries, with `0 <= offset <= byteLength` or `0 <= start < end <= byteLength`.
Detached state does not manufacture a current neighbor or discard the authored
target. Required current mapping evidence comes from trusted host/provider context,
not from a file's assertion that it is attached. Missing relevant historical or
current proof cannot be upgraded to intact placement by parsing the file.

Decode under a validated finite profile bounding input bytes, JSON value nodes,
nesting, decoded string bytes, records, integer digits, individual body bytes and
total body bytes. Keys count toward string/input work. Detect budget exhaustion
